# Work list (maintained by the agents; the user-facing summary is STATUS.md)

Cells and rows here may cite commits. Update this section in the same push as the number or fix it describes.

Instruments named by description below (the Pi 4 tryboot runner, the AM62P and i.MX8MP netboot runners, the AM62P kexec runner and chain runner, the i.MX8MP kexec and wrapper-jump runners, the Python record decoder) were deleted in Step 1 of `driver/docs/one-method.md`; their last commit is `c8436f0d`, and `tools/board.sh` replaced them.

> **PowerVR reset counts before 17797907 were not counted (2026-10-04).** Until
> 17797907 (branch pvr/fl-grow-on-demand), `board_gpu_resets()` returned 0 on the
> PowerVR by construction (driver/zephyr/lib/board/common/board.c). So every
> reset value that came from it reads **"not counted (the hook returned 0 by
> construction)"**, not 0:
> - every AM62P "GPU resets" / "resets" cell in the PowerVR rows of
>   2026-10-03/04 below (the Slint acceptance run, the scan-out view, the fence
>   poll's gl_test and glmark2);
> - glmark2's "GPU resets N" score line;
> - the runner's `resets=` and the board record's reset word.
> This applies equally to the glmark2 and pool runs in
> `tools/cts/log/benchmarks-baseline/glmark2-first-runs-2026-10.md`
> and `tools/cts/log/investigations/pvr-render-pool.md`, and to the kt3/zs run (e4cb0903).
> Recoveries counted from a console's own lines ("render: HWR during fence N",
> "recover", fence timeouts), as some rows below did, are real counts and are
> unaffected. From 17797907 on, the hook is the firmware's HWR counter since
> the render service started (`pvr_render_hwr_recoveries`). The rows are left
> as written.

> **Merging a branch that merged main before: resolve against the newest
> common ancestor of the conflicting file, not git's merge base (2026-10-04,
> land163).** `pvr/fl-grow-on-demand` had merged main at d3c62c02. Main then
> landed `pvr/render-pool-v2`, whose commits the branch also carried from
> 21251d51. git's merge base for the next merge was 21251d51. Against it,
> main's side of `render.rs` re-adds the owner report and its tests (already
> on the branch), and its fine-wait change (already merged at d3c62c02). A
> marker-by-marker resolution there interleaves the copies. The
> resolution that held: `git merge-file` with ours = the branch's file, base
> = the file at d3c62c02 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor d3c62c02` holds for
> both sides), theirs = origin/main's. Only main's new work (kick_times)
> came in as changes. Then assert the union: every `fn` name of either side
> is in the merged file (`comm -23` of the two sorted lists, both empty), and
> the crate compiles. The compiler caught a brace this resolution lost at a
> "both" hunk's seam; a name check alone would not have.

### AM62P: the lost FWCCB command, cached against uncached firmware window (gl_test 174, 2026-10-04)

The minimal reproducer gl_test 174 (fwccbloss), run interleaved in two
parts. In each part both arms are built from one tree, and the only
difference is `CONFIG_SAFEUI_GPU_PVR_FW_UNCACHED`. The event is "FWCCB:
slot S read empty; type 0x2abc0067 after 240 us (read offset S, write
offset S + 2)": a firmware command whose words were not yet visible when
the write offset had passed them.

| part | tree | images (cached / uncached) | run dir (main checkout) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (v7) | 2534fd2c | a21eeb88 / 22d50a4c | `build/fwl8ab-am62p-p1-20261004-124152` |
| 2 (v8) | 01caef79 | e58330b8 / e893a03a | `build/fwl9ab-am62p-p2-20261004-131550` |

| arm | runs | hangs | reached slot 12 | reached slot 28 | runs with an event | commands read |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cached | 20 | 0 | 20 | 20 | **5** (slot 12 x1 at request 7; slot 28 x4 at request 15) | 15540 |
| uncached | 20 | 7 (part 1 only: v7's hold missed; not the event) | 20 | 15 | **0** | 11467 |

- **The rate test:** Fisher's exact test on runs with an event, the run
  as the unit (the events sit at fixed requests in a deterministic ack
  schedule).
  - 5 of 20 against 0 of 20: one-sided p = C(20,5)/C(40,5) = **0.024**.
  - Against the 15 uncached runs that reached slot 28: 0.048.
  - Per command (5 in 15540 against 0 in 11467): 0.063, a check only,
    since commands are not independent trials.
- **Every event:** filled after exactly 240 us, and our next KCCB post
  was taken in 1 ms (the schedule there is 5 or 8 ms).
- **The ack times:** cached runs ack the same schedule every run: 1, 1, 1,
  2-3, then 5 ms x7, 2, then 8 ms. The uncached runs ack 1 ms throughout.
- **The PM-latency-10 probe** (be42a690, the v8 cached image with
  ActivePMLatency 10 ms, 2 runs, `build/fwl10pm-am62p-20261004-135216`):
  - the console shows "ActivePMLatency 10 ms", and the acks are unchanged
    (54-53 at 5 ms, 329 at 8 ms);
  - so the 5/8 ms period is neither ActivePMLatency nor our 1 ms poll. Its
    cause is open.
  - Both runs passed with no event: cached 5 of 22 over all images.
- **Decision:** the uncached window becomes the default (Linux
  drm/imagination's choice too), landing after the AM62P common round has
  run on its tip. Details: tools/cts/log/investigations/pvr-render-pool.md, the "AM62P
  glmark2 cell" sections from v7 A/B part 1 on.

### AM62P: the run with both freelist fixes (c18f9bfd, 2026-10-04)

glmark2 with the grow knob and the ready pages on (678661c1), run dir
`build/flready-am62p-20261004-061334/fl-ready-glmark2-on`: score 470, 0
GPU resets, no stop, unaccounted 0.
- **The ready pages did not change the firmware's acks.** Build wrote
  CURRENT 448 and READY 64 (current base 0x3900, where the old build wrote
  0x3800). But every grow ack is word for word fwccb-1's
  (512/256, 768/256, 1024/256, then 1280/0). The firmware keeps each
  grow's own pages as ready, whatever READY says. The switch stays opt-in;
  the item "the grow answer's READY word has no effect visible in the ack"
  is open. The fwccb-2 reading "our answers never give ready pages" is
  withdrawn.
- **The lost command recurred** (:804, after the third refused grow's 8 ms
  ack): no more grow requests, 8 re-posts at refract. That is 3 of 5
  refused-grow runs without the FWCCB check, and 1 clean case with it. On
  a poll with no empty slot the check adds no cache operation, so the
  counts do not show it changes anything. Details:
  tools/cts/log/investigations/pvr-render-pool.md, "The run with both fixes".

### AM62P: the firmware's freelist counts before the grow answer (70b79a74, 2026-10-04)

glmark2 with the knob and ready pages on, plus the "fw before the answer"
line (2613f5c9). Run dir
`build/flbefore-am62p-20261004-064909/fl-before-glmark2-on`: score 473,
0 GPU resets, 25 grow requests (3 served).
- Before the first answer the firmware read current 512, ready 0, grow
  pending, where build gave it 448 + 64. So READY at init is a reserve the
  firmware uses.
- Across each served grow, current stayed the same and ready became 256
  (DELTA), while we answered READY 96 / 132 / 164; current + ready = NEW.
  So in a grow answer the firmware takes NEW and sets ready = DELTA. The
  READY word has no effect.
- The open item is closed.

Since 57547c34, `PVR_BACKEND_OPT_SWAP_DROPS_ZS` is on by default for window surfaces, and since fcaa9f39 `eglSwapBuffers` calls the hook for windows only (EGL 1.5 3.10.1). gl_test cases 172 `swapzs` and 173 `splitzs` (cb6c5aea; written as 170/171 in b25c9ebc) assert a window's depth across a swap and across a glFinish split. The lead's runs, read from the consoles in the main checkout's `build/`. The run dir names below are the ones on disk.

**AM62P**, images from c8ab6517 (merge of origin/main 066d6630), U-Boot, one install, env diff 0. Run dir `build/fw2-am62p-20261004-024024/` (`-024029` in the lead's message).

## AM62P: the swap drops the window's depth/stencil, off against on (2026-10-04)

`PVR_BACKEND_OPT_SWAP_DROPS_ZS` (e4cb0903, opt-in, default off): the kick of a frame swapped into the window stores no depth/stencil (EGL 1.5 section 3.10.1: "The contents of ancillary buffers are always undefined after calling eglSwapBuffers"), and the next frame initialises them instead of loading them. Four images, all from e4cb0903, in zephyr-ws-yakogl with `CONFIG_YAKOGL_AM62P_RTI_SELF_ARM=y` and the inherited feeder off. Each pair's `.config` files differ in the knob's line only. Booted from U-Boot by `tools/board.sh`, one install; env diff 0. Run dir `build/fwzs-am62p-20261004-014255/` in the main checkout (the lead's message named it `-013800`). The lines below were read from its consoles.

**gl_test** (regression set):

| arm | image sha256 | knob line | result line | back after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ctl3 | `27630ba31284a91d...` | `gl_test: PVR_BACKEND_OPT_SWAP_DROPS_ZS=0` | `gl_test: all: 1 of 38 cases failed (37 passed; 0 timed out; first failure case 48 at index 31)` | 62 s |
| zs | `bfd158681c103982...` | `gl_test: PVR_BACKEND_OPT_SWAP_DROPS_ZS=1` | the same line | 61 s |

Case 48 is the ES 3 case that fails on main. No recover, timeout or re-post line in either. The cases that read a surface after `eglSwapBuffers` (15, 16, 17, 18, 21) read colour only (e4cb0903's message).

**glmark2** (800x600, fine wait and kick times on in both):

| arm | image sha256 | score line | re-posts |
|---|---|---|---:|
| kt3 (knob off) | `e6ba4104eed7ecdd...` | `glmark2: score 315: 29 scenes ran, 2 failed, 2 unsupported (33 list entries); window 800x600, shown yes, GPU resets 0` | 1 |
| zs (knob on) | `22fdb10499af4df0...` | `glmark2: score 550: 29 scenes ran, 2 failed, 2 unsupported (33 list entries); window 800x600, shown yes, GPU resets 0` | 1 |

The zs console prints `glmark2: PVR_BACKEND_OPT_SWAP_DROPS_ZS=1 (the swap drops the window's depth/stencil)`. Both re-posts are the known stall (fence 63293 off, 108446 on). Read "GPU resets 0" as absent: the PowerVR count is not wired at this commit. Both arms print `glmark2: FAIL rc=-5` for the same scenes: shadow and refract "Set up failed", and the two buffer-map entries unsupported.

## AM62P: the PowerVR fence poll, 1 ms against 20 us (2026-10-04)

The knob `CONFIG_SAFEUI_GPU_PVR_FINE_WAIT` (yakogl-drivers feature `pvr-fine-wait`, default off) reads the fragment UFO every 20 us instead of once per ms (`tools/cts/log/investigations/pvr-fence-wait.md`). Each pair of images differs only by the knob: the `.config` files differ in that one line, and each image's `libyakogl_drivers.a` has `busy_wait_us` with 1000 (ctl) or 20 (fine) in `render::wait_for` (objdump). The images were built in zephyr-ws-yakogl with `CONFIG_YAKOGL_AM62P_RTI_SELF_ARM=y` and the inherited feeder off, booted from U-Boot (netboot, env route) by `tools/board.sh`, one install per pair. env diff 0 after both pairs. The lead's runs; the lines below were read from the consoles in the main checkout's `build/` run directories.

**gl_test** (regression set, `CONFIG_GL_TEST_CASE=7`), images from 78c4c208, run dir `build/fw-am62p-20261004-000741/{ctl,fine}`:

| arm | image sha256 | result line | RTI | back after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ctl | `db5ceec4a6e0d6fd...` | `gl_test: all: 1 of 38 cases failed (37 passed; 0 timed out; first failure case 48 at index 31)` | armed | 61 s |
| fine | `8594b59dfe01c96f...` | the same line, word for word | armed | 64 s |

Case 48 is the ES 3 case that fails on main too. Neither console has a "recover", "timeout" or "re-posted" line. The knob changes no gl_test verdict.

**glmark2** (800x600, on screen), images from e7906077, run dir `build/fwg-am62p-20261004-001210/{ctl,fine}`:

| arm | image sha256 | score line | GPU resets | re-posts |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| ctl | `f73844beb156812e...` | `glmark2: score 303: 29 scenes ran, 2 failed, 2 unsupported (33 list entries); window 800x600, shown yes, GPU resets 0` | 0 | 0 |
| fine | `3c4ea68c85d282ca...` | `glmark2: score 316: 29 scenes ran, 2 failed, 2 unsupported (33 list entries); window 800x600, shown yes, GPU resets 0` | 0 | 1 |

Both print `glmark2: FAIL rc=-5`, for the same scenes in both arms. Failed: `[shadow] <default>: Set up failed` (depth-only framebuffer) and `[refract] <default>: Set up failed` (render pool). Unsupported: the two `[buffer] ...update-method=map` entries. That is the 2026-10-03 run's outcome (`driver/docs/glmark2.md` 5c), not the knob. The fine arm's one re-post is `W: render: fence 63380 (frame fence) not moved at 20 ms, re-posted 1 kick(s) (1 so far)`, in terrain's first frames, right after a new 256x256 HWRT. That is the firmware stall the 20 ms re-post works around. It also appears in glmark2 runs of images without the knob: 5 at 5398fb14 (`build/glmark2-am62p-20261003-222609`) and 1 at 0db1c28f (`build/pool-am62p-20261004-003056/glmark2-off`). One occurrence in one run does not attribute it to either arm. It stays open as the re-post defect (HANDOFF), not as a property of the knob.

No regression. The Pi 4 glmark2 cell is green, the second green glmark2 cell (after the i.MX8MP's). The three boards' glmark2 cells together: i.MX8MP green (round 4, above), Pi 4 green (this round), AM62P amber: since the reclaim default (land192's row; round `build/common-am62p-20261004-145517`, image `edcf0604`) its GM record is `594b1201 fc3f01c9 2184003f 03200258`, score 457, 33 ran, 0 failed, 0 unsupported, resets 0, but refract's depth-pass draw is refused in its frames ("glDrawArrays was not recorded (-12); the frame is missing it": the render pool had 7600 KiB requested against a largest free range of 3936 KiB, fragmentation), while shadow, which failed in land189's earlier round (32 ran, 1 failed), now runs.

The four scenes that were unsupported, from the GM console, against the per-scene prediction:

| entry | scene | fps | prediction | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 17 | buffer, interleave false, map | 99 | 60-110 | inside |
| 19 | buffer, interleave true, map | 114 | 60-110 | above by 4 (see below) |
| 23 | shadow | 5 (41 frames, gl 243 ms a frame) | 3-15 | inside |
| 24 | refract | 4 (39 frames, gl 249.5 ms a frame) | 10-50 | below |

Entry 19 against entry 17 (the same map method, interleave false, 99 fps): the GL time per frame is 4323 us against 5605 us (the `glmark2-frame:` lines; swap and show are the same). glmark2's wave mesh has four vec3 attributes per vertex: four VBOs without interleave, one with it (mesh.cpp update_vbo). Each frame updates about 10 vertex ranges (the wave's period is 0.05 of the length at duty 0.5, scene-buffer.cpp), and the map path maps each VBO once (mesh.cpp update_single_vbo). Our glMapBufferOES copies the whole store on write while a pending job still reads it (buffer.rs map_range: a fresh allocation, the old store copied, the old one freed after the job), so entry 17 does that four times a frame and entry 19 once, over the same total bytes. The fewer allocations and frees are the likely difference; the share of each part is not measured. glmark2's default list has one subdata entry (18, interleave false, 100 fps, GL 5554 us), so it compares with entry 17, not 19. (The 98 fps line after entry 19 is entry 20, `ideas`.)

Refract's miss has its cause in the console: at its start "osal(v3d): out of GPU memory for 7684096 bytes (1 frees held)", then "no GPU memory for a tiled copy of 7684096 bytes (0 of 8388608 bytes of copies live, a job open)" in each of its 39 frames. 7684096 is a 1600x1200 4-byte texture's tiled copy plus 4096: the 48 MiB carve-out did not give 7.7 MB in one piece with no kept copy live, so every frame tiled the texture into the job's 8 MiB arena (its high-water 7680184) instead of keeping it. Terrain did the same as in round 2: 399 tiled-copy refusals (415 then), 6 fps. Whose memory fills the carve-out by then is not in this console; the per-scene `glmark2-mem:` line (branch v3d/tiled-free) is the instrument for it. The draw-time sampler variants line printed twice in the run ("1 built" in shadow, "2 built" in refract), not every frame: no program re-links per frame. Shadow also printed "gl_fb_target: framebuffer 1 colour attachment has no storage" six times at its start. That line is wrong, not the framebuffer: since land186 a complete framebuffer whose only attachment is a depth texture is drawn with no colour target, but every colour-target lookup asked `target_loc` (framebuffer.rs) first, and it logged the missing colour buffer as a fault before the draw took the depth-only size. Reproduced on the host (three lines for one depth-only draw) and fixed on branch gl/depth-only-quiet (0b53e093); the draws themselves are the ones gl_test case 177 checks with read-back. Refract and terrain draw every frame, but each frame tiles its large texture again into the job's arena: slow, not lost (performance, step 2).

glmark2 ON, from the console:
- **441 recoveries.** The firmware's HWR counter reads 441 at the end
  (`HWR during fence 528 (counter 439 -> 441)`), with 441 `FREELISTS_RECON`
  lines and 483 `CONTEXT_RESET` lines (some recoveries reset both DMs). Only

  the counter move.
- **The first scene already fails.** The first reset is at console line 161:
  `CONTEXT_RESET ctxid=2 reason=1 dm=2` (guilty geometry, MMU 0). Lines
  187-188 are reason 2 resets of both DMs, `MMU=0x0010650000000000` (IPF
  CREQ), and a guilty 3D follows at PC 0x98c5c001. This is the same failure
  as the gl_test ON run.
glmark2 OFF (the control), from the console:
- 0 `CONTEXT_RESET`, 0 `FREELISTS_RECON`, 0 re-posts.
- conditionals 0:0 879 us a frame (gl 27, swap 847), 5:0 1,783, 0:5 891.
- The same as the fw2 default run (`a6ce172b`, also 550, within 0%). Its
  eight "render pool exhausted" lines (4608 KiB x3, 3072, 1876 x2, 7500 x2)
  equal fw2's eight, line for line (diff of the two consoles). pvr/bgtag
  predates land161's frame-set default, so terrain and refract exhaust the
  pool on both arms the same way.

- **"GPU resets 0" in the score line and the record does not count.** It is
  the known defect of main's PowerVR board layer: recoveries are not counted
  there (they are counted only on pvr/fl-grow-on-demand). This run's
  recoveries are the console's 441, not the field's 0.

**The split arm** (value 2: the tag on, the init quad kept, so each kick
differs from today only in ISP_BGOBJVALS bit 9). `bgtag2-gltest` from 6751a446
(`a5a7e6535a88c1a4...`), run dir `build/bgtag2-am62p-20261004-041848/`:
- `gl_test: PVR_BACKEND_OPT_BGTAG=2`.
- `gl_test: all: 11 of 40 cases failed (29 passed; 9 timed out; first failure
  case 1 at index 0)`.
  - FAIL: 16 and 48. TIMEOUT: 1, 23, 13, 19, 172, 173, 21, 17, 18.
  - 13 CONTEXT_RESET, 13 "HWR during", 13 FREELISTS_RECON. The first comes at
    the first kick (console line 183: `CONTEXT_RESET ctxid=2 reason=1 dm=2 ...
    MMU=0x0000000000000000`; "HWR during fence 2 (0 -> 1)").
- Case 1's triangles are now present: `half: inside small tri (32,40) =
  0xff00ffff want 0xff00ffff ok`. The quad was what made them appear. The
  resets came back regardless, and case 1 timed out on its later kicks.

**Verdict.** Against the two outcomes written before the run: the triangles
came back, but the resets returned at the first kick with only the tag bit
changed. So the tag bit with our background program is the cause. The knob
is dead until the ISP's tagged-background semantics are known. No source
here says what a tagged background does to the parameter buffer. pvr/bgtag
is not landed; this section is its record.

## Pi 4: depth textures on the V3D, gl_test case 169 (2026-10-04)

The Pi 4 glmark2 row's entries 23 shadow and 24 refract were "Unsupported": both need GL_OES_depth_texture, which the V3D did not claim because its TMU path sampled no float texel format (`DEPTH_TEXTURE_EXTENSIONS`, `src/gl/state.rs`). Branch v3d/depth-texture: (1) the TMU's R32F format (`TEXTURE_DATA_FORMAT_R32F` 29, Mesa's row `R32_FLOAT`, v3dx_format_table.c:91, tex_check against Mesa); (2) a sampler variant keyed by `LodKey::ret32` whose look-ups take the TMU's 32-bit output (TMU Config Parameter 1 bit 0, one word per channel), compiled at draw time for a binding whose texture is R32F; (3) `v3d_depth_resolve`: the depth texture's D24S8 buffer read back on the CPU through Mesa's `v3d_load_tiled_image` (UIF without the XOR), each word's bits 31..8 over 0xffffff. Proven by a minimal case, not by glmark2: gl_test case 169 dstex (a 4x1 depth ramp uploaded and sampled; one DEPTH_STENCIL texture on both points of an FBO drawn with both tests; that texture sampled), 12 checks, pixel read-back. ### Pi 4: a framebuffer with no colour attachment, gl_test case 177 (2026-10-04)

The V3D half of `DRAWS_WITHOUT_COLOUR` (a8002f3b, on land186's contract): a draw with no colour target opens a job at target address 0, whose tiles load and store no render target, only the depth/stencil buffer, as Mesa's v3d job with nr_cbufs 0 does; a tile list that stores nothing stores buffer NONE (v3dx_rcl.c:315-321; job_check part 18). The image runs case 177 alone, built from 678ee569 (`CONFIG_V3D_GL_TEST_CASE=177`, ES 3.0 report, so the pixel is (d, 0, 0, 1)), through tools/board.sh.

| board | image sha256 | boot | result | back to Linux |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raspberry Pi 4 (V3D) | `5fac334552d6e82f...` (`V3D_BUILD=678ee569`) | tryboot | all 9 checks ok: linked 3, no GL error after the setup, status 0x8cd5 (COMPLETE), no error after the draw or the sampling; depth top 0xff0000b8 (want 0xff0000b7), left 0xff000049 (0xff000048), bottom 0xff00004b (0xff00004a), right 0xff0000b6 (0xff0000b5), tolerance 2; `gl_test: case 177 zonly: PASS`; `v3d_gl_test: 1 of 1 cases passed (229 ms)`; record DONE; recoveries 0, MMU faults 0; board.sh `verdict=done result=legacy:gl_test_case resets=0` | 252 s |

Equal to the prediction written before the run (PASS, 9 checks, the four depth values above within 2). Each depth reads exactly 1 above the window-sized value, and that is what NEAREST sampling of a texture twice the window gives: window pixel x = 32 samples at u = 32.5 / 64, texel coordinate 65.0, so texel 65 with centre 65.5, half a texel past the pixel's own position (65.0 at twice the size); the same on y. Half a texel on each axis is 1/128 in normalized x and in y, so the ramp's depth d = ((xn + yn) / 2 + 1) / 2 moves by 1/256, which is 1.0 of 255. Run dir in the main checkout: `build/zonly-pi4-20261004-135841/20261004-1358-gl_test-5fac3345/`. Whether glmark2's shadow and refract now run on the Pi 4 is the glmark2 cell check of the next common round.

## i.MX8MP: a uniform array at a run-time index, gl_test case 45 es3dyn alone (2026-10-04)

The i.MX8MP gl_test row's per-case runs (the set reads 36 of 40, first failure 16, the other three unnamed): the three candidates from the older set runs were run alone, one boot each, from U-Boot through tools/board.sh. 45 es3dyn and 44 es3hdr fail alone; 17 ctx2 passes alone (`594b010e 0011ff01 00000011 00000000`, 17 checks: its set failure depends on the cases before it). Case 45:

| run | image sha256 | record words | what the record says | back to Linux |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before (a92ae953, main + docs) | `dbd1635139fc55a2...` | `594b010e 002d0102 bf990000 bf9900e6` | check 1 failed: red 0x00 where 0xe6 is wanted; green, blue and alpha right | 31 s |
| after (2f816946, this fix) | `40021192d78918d8...` | `594b010e 002dff01 00000002 00000000` | PASS, 2 checks made (the prediction, word for word) | 31 s |

Cause: red is the only channel of `cols[k] = (0.1k, 0, 0.2, 0.25)` that depends on the index, and the run read exactly 3 x cols[0]. The GC7000 offline row es300/dynidx.frag read `cols[k]` with `movar` and a relative constant-file read (`mov t3, u0[a.x]`), which returns element 0 whatever the index on this GPU (the online compiler's own note, src/shaderc/online/select.rs, LoadUniformIdx, measured on cases 108-128). Mesa's GL path never emits it on HALTI2+: etnaviv sets `lower_uniforms_to_ubo` (etnaviv_compiler.c:66), the state tracker lowers uniforms to UBO 0 (st_program.c:653, st_glsl_to_nir.cpp `st_nir_lower_uniforms`), and a run-time index stays a `load` from the uniform block in memory. Our tools/vivante/etna_shc.c skipped that pass; it now runs it. Compiled against all 327 table sources, the pass changes exactly the four rows that held `movar`. Two were replaced in place with the new `gen_shader_table.py --replace` (es300/dynidx.frag and qt3d/e0880dcd5582d4de.frag; 328 rows byte for byte), and dynidx now reads `imullo0.s32 k*16; load.u32 ..., u0.w` (UBO_ADDR). **Open item:** qt/imageparticle_sprite.vert and qt/imageparticle_tabled.vert keep `movar`: the generator's layout check refuses them, because their `ubuf.sizetable` is packed (stride 1) in the GL core's block where Mesa's offsets assume a vec4 per element. The host test `no_table_row_indexes_a_uniform_array_through_the_address_register` names them. Case 45 in the set is the next common round's check (predicted GT 38 of 40 or better, with 16 msaa and 17 open).

## Pi 4: a stale tiled copy given back before the job opens, gl_test case 179 (2026-10-04)

glmark2's shadow re-tiles its depth texture every frame: the GL core resolves the depth into the texture's storage (a new stamp) after flushing the depth pass, and the main pass's draw then opens a job in which `tiled_copy` freed the old stamp's kept copy. The V3D OSAL holds a free made with a job open until that job has run (v3d_frees.h), although the open job never reads a stale copy, so the old and the new copy were both in the carve-out for a frame (two 7.8 MB copies for shadow's map). Fix b7170d35 (`drop_stale_copies`): when a draw arrives with no job open, the stale copies of its textures are freed before the job opens, so the free waits only for the job in flight. Host rig test first (a_stale_copy_is_given_back_before_the_job_opens; without the call the new copy's allocation fails with the old one held). gl_test case 179 retile pins it on silicon: two frames with no glFinish, a 256x256 depth texture alone in an FBO drawn at window depth 0.25 then 0.75, sampled and read back; on the V3D the carve-out in use right after each sampling draw (its job still open) must not grow from frame 1 to frame 2. An A/B whose arms differ: CONTROL d8c84bf2 = origin/main 1fa941e3 + the case alone (b7170d35 not an ancestor; the counter's string absent from the image), FIX cb1bb374 = b7170d35 + 67514bae + the case (the string present). Both `CONFIG_V3D_GL_TEST_CASE=179`, ES 3.0 report, by tryboot through board.sh from the 985077e1 runner; run dir `build/retile-pi4-20261004-151012/` in the main checkout (copied to records/pi4/).

| arm | image sha256 | checks | carve-out after the sampling draw (frame 1, frame 2) | result | back to Linux |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONTROL (`V3D_BUILD=d8c84bf2`) | `9b178b66ccf30bcb...` | 1-7 ok (pixels 0xff000040 then 0xff0000bf at (32,32) and (4,4)); 8 MISMATCH: difference 0x00041000 | 16323072, 16589312 bytes | `gl_test: case 179 retile: FAIL`; board.sh `rc=4 verdict=failed`; recoveries 0 | 251 s |
| FIX (`V3D_BUILD=cb1bb374`) | `cd969d143e2fa45d...` | 1-8 ok; "yakogl/v3d: a stale tiled copy of 266240 bytes given back before the job opened" printed between frame 1's reads and frame 2's | 16323072, 16323072 bytes | `gl_test: case 179 retile: PASS`; board.sh `rc=0 verdict=done`; recoveries 0 | 254 s |

Both arms equal the predictions written before the runs, word for word: control checks 1-7 ok and check 8 FAIL with 266240 (0x41000: the 256x256 R32F copy, 262144 bytes, plus 4096); fix PASS with the counter line and a difference of 0. The control shows the case can see the hold (its zero is not a zero no mechanism could make non-zero); the pixels show the new stamp was sampled in both arms (a stale copy would read 0x40 in frame 2). Whether it changes glmark2's shadow and refract is the arm run's question (GM image d0932b24 with the per-scene memory line, GT 889599db), not claimed here.

## Pi 4: the stale-copy fix in glmark2 and gl_test, and the per-scene memory line (2026-10-04)

The arm for b7170d35 against round 3 (1fa941e3), by tryboot through board.sh from the 985077e1 runner; run dir `build/arm-pi4-20261004-152027/` in the main checkout (copied to records/pi4/). The GM image also carries the per-scene memory line (42bd90ff: `glmark2-mem:` before each entry's setup and at its end, from the OSAL's `osal_mem_line`), so the GM arm is b7170d35 + 67514bae + cb1bb374 + 42bd90ff; the GT image is b7170d35 alone.

| row | image sha256 | record / result | against round 3 | back to Linux |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GM glmark2 (`PVR_SAMPLE_TREE=42bd90ff`) | `d0932b243a844247...` | `594b1201 fc3f00b7 2184003f 03200258`: 183, 33 ran, 0 failed, 0 unsupported, resets 0 | identical record | 417 s |
| GT gl_test (`V3D_BUILD=b7170d35`) | `889599db9b35048f...` | `gl_test: all: 0 of 12 cases failed (12 passed; 0 timed out)`, resets 0, no tiled-copy refusal | the same verdicts | 254 s |

The counter first: "yakogl/v3d: a stale tiled copy of 7684096 bytes given back before the job opened" printed once, at 15:25:06, the start of entry 23 (shadow): shadow's own 1600x1200 depth copy was the first early drop, so the change was exercised in glmark2. It moved nothing glmark2 measures: shadow 5 fps and 0 tiled-copy refusals both with and without it (round 3 had none either), and the refusals are round 3's to the count: terrain 228 x 1404928, 114 x 356352 and 57 x 266240 bytes (399, as round 3), refract 39 x 7684096 (as round 3). Its effect is the one case 179 measures (above). The sampler-variants line printed twice, as in round 3.

The memory lines, read in full (entries 0-32). glmark2 tears a scene down before its result line (main-loop.cpp:116-121), so "end N" is after entry N's teardown and equals "before setup N+1". At every boundary from entry 1 on, used minus held is 17817856 bytes (17833984 at entry 22): the permanent set (job arenas, window, programs). Everything above it at a boundary is the torn-down scene's memory still held. The large holds: entry 10 9.8 MB, 11 9.9 MB, 15 12.3 MB, 16 11.5 MB, 21 20.0 MB (longest free run 11632640), 22 terrain 31.8 MB (longest 61184), 23 shadow 23.6 MB (longest 8355584), 24 refract 31.6 MB (longest 368640); smaller ones of 2.3-3.9 MB at entries 2-4, 9, 12 and 17-19. Where the holds are gone (entries 25-32, 87 KB held) the free space is one piece: longest 31883264 bytes of about 31.9 MB free; the same at entries 0-1 (31960832).

Why the frees stay held: a free with no job open is fenced on the last job submitted (v3d_frees.h), and the OSAL learns that a job completed only in wait(), completed() or the next submit (FRDONE has no interrupt). A scene's last job has finished on the GPU long before its teardown, but the teardown and the next setup make no wait or submit, so the OSAL's completed fence is stale and the frees stay held; the next setup allocates around them. Refract shows the cost: its first 7684096-byte allocation fails with 1 free still held after the OOM path's drain, refract's own setup allocations already sit in the gaps, and 7.7 MB in one piece is never found again (39 refusals, each frame tiling into the job arena: 4 fps). Terrain starts with 20 MB held and an 11.6 MB longest run. A drain at the boundary would give both about 31.9 MB in one piece at their setup (the boundaries without holds); whether terrain then fits through its own frames these boundary lines cannot say. The fix this points at (a non-blocking poll of the job in flight before fencing a free and before placing an allocation while frees are held) is not part of this branch.

## Pi 4: the OSAL looks at the job in flight before a free or an allocation, gl_test case 180 (2026-10-04)

The memory lines above showed the torn-down scene's frees held at every scene boundary, because the OSAL learns a job completed only when it waits or submits. Fix a528c8a3: `v3d_frees_poll` (v3d_frees.h) looks at the job in flight without blocking (zephyr_v3d.c `finish_inflight(true)`) before every free is fenced and before an allocation is placed while frees are held. Host check tools/v3d/osal_frees_check.c 23 of 23 (shapes 10-12; the poll without its drain fails shape 11). gl_test case 180 teardown pins it: a 1024x1024 texture sampled, its job flushed and left 20 ms to finish with nobody looking, the texture deleted and one of the same size made; on the V3D the carve-out must not grow. A/B whose arms differ in the OSAL: CONTROL 0c1253db = acc0bd3f + the case (a528c8a3 not an ancestor; zephyr_v3d.c.obj text 14473 bytes), FIX e351cd83 (text 14605 bytes, another object hash). By tryboot from the 985077e1 runner; run dir `build/poll-pi4-20261004-154507/` in the main checkout (copied to records/pi4/).

|---|---|---|---|
| case 180 CONTROL (`V3D_BUILD=0c1253db`) | `f70c2c04a232ab34...` | checks 1-4 ok (A 0xff0000ff, B 0xff00ff00); 5 MISMATCH: carve-out 25218304 before A's deletion, 30810880 after B's creation, growth 0x00555600; FAIL; board.sh `rc=4 verdict=failed`, resets 0 | 255 s |
| case 180 FIX (`V3D_BUILD=e351cd83`) | `8c57c49720f40e8e...` | checks 1-5 ok: 25218304 before, 21019904 after, growth 0; PASS; `rc=0 verdict=done`, resets 0 | 254 s |
| GM glmark2 (`PVR_SAMPLE_TREE=e351cd83`) | `752e7e4c35d9cf5f...` | `594b1201 fc3f00b7 2184003f 03200258`: 183, 33/0/0, resets 0, identical to round 3 | 417 s |
| GT gl_test (`V3D_BUILD=e351cd83`; run dir `build/poll-gt-pi4-20261004-160316/`) | `3726e5c16fa6198c...` | `gl_test: all: 0 of 12 cases failed (12 passed; 0 timed out)`, resets 0, no tiled-copy refusal; as round 3 | 253 s |

The control's growth, 5592576 bytes, is B's storage with its whole mip chain: the GL core lays out every level of a power-of-two texture (texture.rs `chain_layout`), 4 x (1024^2 + 512^2 + ... + 1) = 5592404 bytes, which the OSAL's 256-byte granules make 5592576. The prediction said 4194304 (level 0 alone) or 8392704: the direction held, the size did not (chain_layout was not read before writing it). In the fix arm A's storage and its kept copy (4198400 bytes, the only copy line in the console) came back before B was placed, so the carve-out went down by the copy.

The counter of the GM run: "frees held 0" at every scene boundary from entry 0 to 32, the longest free run 31960832 bytes everywhere but after terrain (29880064). The poll drains the between-scene holds completely. Its glmark2 effect is none: the record is round 3's, and the tiled-copy refusals are round 3's to the count (terrain 228 x 1404928, 114 x 356352, 57 x 266240; refract 39 x 7684096). So neither hold refused them:

- Refract (scene-refract.cpp:177-216: a depth texture and an RGBA colour texture at twice the 800x600 canvas, 1600x1200, one level each) starts with 31985408 bytes free, 31960832 in one piece. It then holds the R32F depth storage (7680000), the colour storage (7680000), the depth texture's D24S8 buffer (about 7.7 MB) and its first kept copy (7684096), about 30.7 MB, and its second 7684096-byte copy finds about 1.2 MB: "out of GPU memory for 7684096 bytes (1 frees held)", then tiled into the job's arena every frame (textures high-water 7680184 of 8388608). Its peak is about 17.8 + 2 x 7.68 + 7.7 + 2 x 7.684, about 56.2 MB, against the 49.8 MB carve-out: structural. The Pi 4 GM cell's step-2 items, each saving at least 7.68 MB: (a) sample a render-target texture from its render layout without a CPU copy (Mesa keeps render targets UIF and samples them as they are); (b) sample the depth texture from its D24S8 buffer with a TMU depth format, as Mesa does, instead of R32F storage and a copy; (c) a larger carve-out. Refract draws every frame through the arena fallback: slow, not lost.
- Terrain's first refusal comes one second into the scene with 0 frees held and 31960832 bytes contiguous at its setup, so its own live set passes 30.5 MB; itemizing it needs a per-allocation trace (a later instrument).

Terrain also logs "GL error 0x502 in glGenerateMipmap" 16 times and "a texture on unit 0 is incomplete and samples (0,0,0,1) ... 800x600, levels 1 of 1" (the same in the AM62P's land192 round): an ES 2.0 image refuses mipmaps of a non-power-of-two texture, so terrain samples black. Every GM cell reads "green by record, terrain's picture wrong" until GL_OES_texture_npot lands (the next item).

PARKED (ES 3.0 on hold by the user, 2026-09-26 17:48; not for landing). Cause: the online compiler samples a 2D array as one tall stacked image, so the TPU filters and wraps across layers. Design (the root fix, as Mesa's pvr does it): sample one layer as a 2D image at the layer's address (`smp` with `tao`, the address = base + layer * LAYER_SIZE, attested against pco_shc fixtures), and lay the storage out layer-major (each layer's whole mip chain together, pvr_arch_tex_state.c:318) for the programs of that back end. One deqp image per commit whose CONFIG_DEQP_CASE is exactly the 11 regressed names (random.all_features.fragment.2, 7,

| commit (first parent of main) | image sha256 | pass | fail | refusals "a cube coordinate the chain did not consume" |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 38905bef | 3bad1681198a211e | 11 | 0 | 0 |
| 7a8bca90 | 394ea5398b3c60a4 | 11 | 0 | 0 |
| 5079a9c9 | 7d2cad9dbf59e389 | 11 | 0 | 0 |
| ded52c6d | 26e4e5b1bdb02238 | 0 | 11 | 11 |
| 34ab6934 | 1b15472d47badc87 | 0 | 11 | 11 |
| 4f40f622 | 3fb28ba6c1bdcf68 | 0 | 11 | 11 |

5079a9c9 is ded52c6d's first parent, so ded52c6d is the first-parent commit that introduced it. Its second parent brings
15550645 (usc-stepc); ded52c6d's diff to src/ against its first parent is file for file a126f952's (step C:
pvr_native_cube defaults to 1, the table's cube programs regenerated, draw.rs). Every failure is "Fail (Failed to compile
shader)": nine fragment and two vertex shaders, 558 to 3,826 bytes, each refused by the code generator
(src/shaderc/online/powervr/assemble.rs, SelOp::SampleZ). Selection emits SampleZ only when native_cube_enabled()
(powervr/select.rs, the samplerCube arm), and the chain folds it into the Sample right after it (powervr/chain.rs,
cube_z); in these 11 shaders a SampleZ reaches the assembler instead. So the defect is in step B's native-cube lowering
(6d718fe0), and step C made that path the default. The table (offline) path is not
involved: these images compile online. The images at the other first-parent points of the range were built and not run.

### 1j. The shaders.random regression fixed: a dead cube sample takes its SampleZ (d5c35a00, 2026-09-25)

Cause (host, then board): all 11 shaders have a `textureCube` whose result nothing reads. Selection's eliminate_dead
deleted the cube sample and kept its SelOp::SampleZ (no destination, so "an effect"), expand_samples found no sample
to fold it into, and assemble.rs refused it. d5c35a00 makes SampleZ die with the cube sample after it. No
spec-versus-silicon question is involved (our own representation; in Mesa's NIR the coordinate is one source of the
tex instruction, nir.h nir_tex_instr_src_size, read in a local Mesa 17.3.8 tree; gitlab.freedesktop.org and the GitHub
mirror could not be read for pco's current sources).

| board: full-tree image 5, loops + random (image 8fdbd83b1f4e2321) | 2,512 / 13 (758a3123) | **2,523 / 2** (random.all_features fragment.53 and vertex.39, the old two) |

### 1l. Read from the board with CONFIG_DEQP_ECHO_QPA (ce920150): texture.vertex.41's source, the vertex.cube masks (2026-09-25)

The deqp sample's echo option (default off; the two commits right after this one, first written as bf8b67e1 and ce920150) prints the whole QPA log, shader sources and images
included; tools/cts/qpa-from-uart.py rebuilds the .qpa (both captures whole: 1 and 6 cases, 0 not whole) and
tools/cts/cts-images.py writes the images. Logs and images <main checkout>/build/am62p-fix/ (uart-v41-echo.log,
uart-vcube6-echo.log, vcube6-img/).

texture.vertex.41 (image 0b08f242f2c26787, aa9d5ce9 + the echo, SampleZ fix not in it): the vertex shader dEQP
generates on the board is 1,110 bytes, `uniform samplerCube o` with `v_color = textureCube(o, v_color.wzx)` that the next
line overwrites: the dead-cube shape of the other ten. The x86 host generates another shader for the same case
(1,033 bytes, a `sampler2D`, differing from its third line on; the board's carries `float(2.38419e-07)`). Why dEQP's
generator diverges between the two builds is not measured. The board source is now the 11th host fixture
(57cd2aff), refused without the SampleZ fix and compiled with it.

texture.vertex.cube.filtering.nearest_mipmap_{linear,nearest}_linear_{clamp,mirror,repeat} (image 6365abf292392918):
the three wrap modes give identical masks. Every failing pixel is in ONE quadrant of the 168x112 viewport: the
checkerboard cube (texture 1) at the minifying scale 1.0, drawn as six 28x28 cells, one per face, whose explicit LOD
is log2(size / 28) > 0 and small (dEQP's calculateLod). All six cells fail (nearest_mipmap_nearest_linear: 258 pixels
in each; nearest_mipmap_linear_linear: 444 to 784 of 784), and the failures are the cells' interiors, not a band at
the face edges: 120 of 1,548 and 544 of 3,884 failing pixels lie on a cell's border row or column. The other three
quadrants (texture 0 minified, both magnified) pass.

| case | failing px | Result's colours there | Reference's colours there |
|---|---:|---|---|
| nearest_mipmap_nearest_linear_* | 1,548 | 2: pure black and white (NEAREST at level 0) | 34 greys (LINEAR at level 0) |
| nearest_mipmap_linear_linear_* | 3,884 | 24 tints such as (43,11,3), (6,38,46): level 0 blended with level 1 (NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR) | black, white and greys of level 0 only (LINEAR) |

So the TPU switches from the magnification to the minification filter at LOD 0, where GL ES 2.0 3.7.8 puts it at
c = 0.5 for a LINEAR magnification with a NEAREST_MIPMAP_* minification (the spec text: opengl.org's "6.1.4 Filtering"
notes, https://www.opengl.org/archives/resources/code/samples/sig99/advanced99/notes/node56.html). The reference filters
the cell LINEAR at level 0; the board minifies it. This is the i.MX8MP's hardware-floor case shape (Mesa etnaviv lists
the same six), here on the PowerVR. No threshold field is known in the TPU sampler words (texstate: dadjust is a LOD
bias, minlod/maxlod clamp, and the TPU picks min or mag on the clamped LOD, Mesa pvr_arch_sampler.c:88-97 as cited in
backend.rs; Mesa's sources could not be re-read today: gitlab.freedesktop.org, its raw endpoint included
(src/imagination/vulkan/pvr_pipeline.c), answers with a bot check); a web search for a PowerVR sampler threshold found
nothing public, and Mesa has no PowerVR GL driver to
compare (Vulkan puts the switch at 0). An exact emulation exists for an explicit-LOD look-up only (LOD' = 0 when
LOD <= c, c a per-sampler word the driver fills); an implicit-LOD look-up in a fragment shader cannot be corrected
that way. **Verdict (the user, 2026-09-25 18:33): recorded as the PowerVR hardware floor**, as the i.MX8MP's same six
are; the explicit-LOD emulation is not implemented. The six are counted as failures in every tally and named "floor".

### 1m. texture.mipmap.{2d,cube}.projected read from the board: 2D fails in one fixed pixel of each 2x2 quad (2026-09-25)

Echo images (CONFIG_DEQP_ECHO_QPA) at 39f62a1d's code: 2d.projected.{nearest,linear}_{nearest,linear}_clamp (image
e9d966a8be2d01d8) and cube.projected.* (130ffba52edae198); both captures whole (4 and 4 cases, 0 not whole), 12 images
each. Logs and images <main checkout>/build/am62p-proj/.

| case | failing px | where |
|---|---:|---|
| 2d.projected nearest_nearest_clamp, linear_nearest_clamp | 22 of 65,536 | all 22 at the same position in their 2x2 quad (x odd, y odd in the PNG) |
| 2d.projected nearest_linear_clamp, linear_linear_clamp | 80 of 65,536 | all 80 at that same quad position |
| cube.projected (4) | 1 to 5 of 16,384 | single pixels on a level boundary, mixed quad positions |

Per cell (dEQP draws the 2D cases as a 4x4 grid of 64x64 cells, each with its own projection and bias, es2fTextureMipmapTests.cpp;
cells named (column, row) in the PNG, row 0 at the top):

| 2d.projected case | cells failing | failing pixels per cell |
|---|---:|---|
| nearest_nearest_clamp, linear_nearest_clamp (GL_*_MIPMAP_NEAREST) | 5 of 16 | (1,3) 5, (2,0) 6, (2,1) 3, (2,2) 4, (3,1) 4 |
| nearest_linear_clamp, linear_linear_clamp (GL_*_MIPMAP_LINEAR) | 7 of 16 | (0,1) 8, (0,3) 6, (1,3) 6, (2,0) 8, (2,1) 27, (2,2) 8, (3,1) 17 |

The case name is the minification filter, texel filter then mipmap filter (es2fTextureMipmapTests.cpp:1082-1085). The
two MIPMAP_NEAREST cases give the same cells and counts as each other, and so do the two MIPMAP_LINEAR ones: the
filter inside a level changes nothing, and only the mipmap filter (how a level or level pair is chosen) does. That
fits a LOD error. The
cube.projected pixels: linear_linear and nearest_linear (92,29), (90,65), (90,66), (90,67), (97,114);
linear_nearest (14,55); nearest_nearest (51,27), each on a level boundary.

In every case the failing pixel shows the colour of the level on the other side of a level boundary: its colour is
the reference's within 2 pixels. So the level choice is off by one right at the boundaries: a LOD error, not a wrong
texel.

Why one quad position (2D): dEQP's verifier (framework/opengl/gluTextureTestUtil.cpp:1477-1531) allows the LOD a
pixel's own derivatives give, and those at its four AXIS neighbours (+-1 in x or in y), never a diagonal one. A
projected coordinate's derivatives change from pixel to pixel. If the texture unit takes one set of derivatives per
2x2 quad (coarse differences, anchored at one pixel), the diagonally opposite pixel gets a LOD from outside what dEQP
allows, and only that pixel can fail. The non-projected mipmap cases, whose derivatives are constant, all pass. This
reading is ours (inferred from the mask and the verifier). No public PowerVR document on the TPU's derivatives was
found (a web search, 2026-09-25), and Mesa's sources could not be read from this host. The cube's 1-5 pixels do not
show the quad pattern; the same cause is not shown there.

What the hardware offers for an exact result, per our pco-derived ISA tables (src/shaderc/online/powervr/isa_tables.rs):
fine derivatives (`fdsxf`, `fdsyf`) and `smp`'s `lodm = gradients`. A projected look-up could take per-pixel
derivatives of s/q and t/q in the shader and sample with explicit gradients, at the cost of four derivative
operations and two data words per such look-up. (Corrected in 1n: dEQP's projected cases do not use texture2DProj at
all, so the older pvr_proj_divide A/B never reached them and says nothing about them.) The lead decided to try it
behind a switch; the result is 1n.

### 1n. Explicit per-pixel gradients for the projected mipmap cases: exercised, no fix (2026-09-25)

The measured code is NOT on main (the lead's decision): `git format-patch` of a700d12c and 2999ef33 (on bc0cb387) is
kept as .claude/worktrees/am62p-proj-grad.patch in the main checkout (untracked; it applies to 4189b32a). It adds
pvr_proj_grad (default 0): the online compiler takes d/dx and d/dy of the sampled coordinate with `fdsxf`/`fdsyf` in
the extended `sngl_ext` form and samples with `smp lodm=gradients`, words u, v, dudx, dudy, dvdx, dvdy as pco's
textureGrad build has them. The extended form is used because pco_map.py (Mesa 26.2.1 and main 2bbecc4, read via git)
has encode_map(O_FDSXF) / (O_FDSYF) write the SHORT `sngl` form with sngl_op dsx / dsy, the coarse ops, although the
short form's 4-bit sngl_op holds dsxf (0b1010); nothing found explains it. The corpus has no smp with lodm=gradients
and no sngl_ext dsxf/dsyf, so the patch's host test decodes the program back field by field and register by register
against pco_shc's textureGrad program (negative control: swapping dudy and dvdx fails it). Mode 1 = texture2DProj
only, mode 2 = every implicit-level 2D look-up in a fragment shader.

- Mode 1, texture.mipmap.2d.projected.* + cube.projected.* (16), one commit a700d12c: 0/16 in both arms (images
  af8acfc90e7bc507, 4900e39aae04080b). NOT EXERCISED: dEQP's "projected" cases never call texture2DProj.
  glsTextureTestUtil.cpp renderQuad multiplies each vertex position by its corner's w, and the shader is texture2D of
  the perspective-interpolated varying.
- Mode 2, texture.mipmap.2d.* + cube.projected.* (88), one commit 2999ef33 (images 587fb69a09fe57bd mode 0,
  012e2ae03c8482f8 mode 2): 72/16 in both arms, identical case by case; no case outside the 16 moved.
- Exercised, from the echo masks (mode 2 image c8e7d1cbc5780666 against 1m's mode-0 images):

| 2d.projected case (clamp) | failing px mode 0 | failing px mode 2 | mode 2's quad slots (PNG) | rendered px that differ |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| nearest_nearest, linear_nearest | 22 | 37 | (1,0) 21, (0,1) 16 | 450 |
| nearest_linear, linear_linear | 80 | 78 | (1,0) 51, (0,1) 27 | 10,826 |

Verdict: cause not shown. Per-pixel explicit gradients change the TPU's level but do not give dEQP's. The failures
move from quad slot (1,1) to (1,0) and (0,1), and for MIPMAP_NEAREST they grow, so 1m's per-quad-derivative reading is
untested by a working fix. Three candidates remain, and these data cannot tell them apart: `fdsxf`/`fdsyf` are not
the per-pixel differences assumed; the TPU's level from gradients differs from dEQP's formula (its precision, or how
it combines the two gradient vectors); or the reading is wrong. The cube four are not reached by this path
(textureCube). gl_test 138 was not written (no fix for it to pass; the number stays free). Logs and images
<main checkout>/build/am62p-grad/ and build/am62p-proj/.

### 1o. rasterization.limits.points on the AM62P: the reported point size range (4d91ff2f, 2026-09-25)

64]`, `Testing with pointSize = 80, fboWidth = 40`, and fails es2fRasterizationTests.cpp:686: the test area, which a
point clamped to 64 leaves green, came out red. The GPU drew the point at 80. Both PowerVR compilers clamp
gl_PointSize to [1, 511] (powervr/prepare.rs; pco through nir_lower_point_size), Mesa's PVR_POINT_SIZE_RANGE_MIN/_MAX
(src/imagination/common/pvr_limits.h:47-48), which Mesa's PowerVR Vulkan driver reports as pointSizeRange
(pvr_physical_device.c:755-756). 4d91ff2f reports [1, 511] on the PowerVR (the V3D keeps 512, the GC7000 64).

Not measured, and why:

- **lifetime.\* (56)**: the group's init builds a program with interleaved transform feedback of gl_Position
  (es3fLifetimeTests.cpp:97, `TCU_CHECK(isOk())`). Transform feedback is not implemented (every
  MAX_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_\* is 0), so the link fails by design and dEQP ends the whole run with die(). On Linux
  that ends the process too. On Zephyr it was a data abort: dEQP's exitProcess() calls fflush(NULL), and
  picolibc's tinystdio fflush() reads stream->flush without a NULL check (offset 0x18 = the FAR). Fixed in the
  sample (50aa3958, on main): a qpRedirectOut() hook prints dEQP's message, "deqp: fatal:" and the summary, then
  takes Zephyr's fatal path. The tally reads "deqp: fatal:" as FATAL. The group stays unmeasurable until transform
  feedback exists.

Harness notes from this run:

- An image that outlives its watchdog window ("RTI feeder lifetime over after 18 feeds", SafeUI soc_a53_wdt.c,
  FEED_INHERITED_WDT_SECONDS=600) can print no summary. The AM62P kexec runner waited 1,500 s for one; it now stops
  at that line with rc 6 (2322ef1a). Image 197 is the first rc 6 (682 s instead of about 1,560 s).
- texture.filtering.3d ran about 19 s per case under the pattern `filtering.3d.*` (29-30 cases in 600 s, images
  19 and 19c) and a few seconds per case named one by one (images 191-193: 22 cases each, 53-65 s from the jump to Linux back, boot
  included). All 27 cases
  run both ways have the same verdict. The cause is not measured. The sizes and formats cases stay slow when
  named (194-197: about 25 s per case).
- Kick re-posts ("fence N not moved at 20 ms, re-posted"): the driver prints the first 8 and then every 256th
  (pvr_render.c), so a log with 8 means at least 8 and fewer than 256. The exact count is absent, not 8.
  Stalls, fence timeouts, BIF faults, Zephyr FATAL: 0 lines in every log except the two lifetime ones.
- The "cube-bind"/"cube(draw)" debug lines (src/gl/draw.rs dump_cube_atlas) fire for any texture with 2 or more
  layers, so 3D and 2D-array textures are printed as "cube".
- The first builder died at image 16 on "/tmp: Disk quota exceeded" (other sessions' /tmp use). Images 16-25
  were rebuilt with TMPDIR under the worktree's build/.

### 1t. Bucket c: sixteen vertex-stage samplers on the AM62P hang the GPU; the limit stays 8 (2026-09-26)

The 15 uniform_api cases of RESULTS 1s ("N vertex texture units required, 8 supported", N 9..14) wait on
GLES_VS_TEX_UNITS, which is 8 on the PowerVR. Mesa's pvr gives every stage 16 samplers
(pvr_physical_device.c:634). Before raising it, gl_test 149 vsunits measured the vertex stage with 16
samplers: sampler k reads a 1x1 texture of its own colour on unit k, draw k (a one-hot weight) writes it into cell
k of a 4x4 grid, and every cell's centre is read back; the clear is blue. Branch am62p/vsunits149b on m5's
126a446e: 5d962387 (the case), 840c19c3 (its switch entry for every GPU; 5d962387 had put it inside the V3D's
block, and those images answered "no case 149": records VSU-GLT149-5d962387, VSU-GLT149-5a43e8b7, not results),
219fd92e (GLES_VS_TEX_UNITS 16 on the PowerVR).

Prediction, sent before the run: arm A (limit 8) cells 0..7 their own colours and 8..15 black; arm B (limit 16) all
16 their own colours. Both wrong:

| arm | image | GL_MAX_VERTEX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A 840c19c3 | 5edc27aaf1d3b341 | 8 | TIMEOUT: 1 GPU reset (HWR), all 16 cells 0x00000000 |
| B 219fd92e | 91d219f3c536f345 | 16 | TIMEOUT: 1 GPU reset (HWR), all 16 cells 0x00000000 |

Both arms: "FWCCB: CONTEXT_RESET ... dm=2", "HWR[0] dm=2 type=3 ... BIF read VA=0x0005000000 TCU 0 tag_id=25",
geom_ufo=0: the geometry job faults in the texture unit on the same unmapped address, whatever the limit. So the
fault is not "units 8..15 unbound" (the limit changes which descriptors the draw fills, and the fault did not
move); a vertex shader with sixteen samplers faults as such. Cause not shown. The gl_test default set on 219fd92e
(image e7922b66d8b32e22, record VSU-GLT-219fd92e): 37 / 1 (46 refused: invalid shader (4.5.4)), identical per case
to 126a446e, 0 recoveries. Not run: uniform_api on 219fd92e (the limit cannot land on a case that hangs). GLES_VS_TEX_UNITS stays 8; 219fd92e is not for landing.
The next measurement: the smallest sampler count that faults (a vertex shader with 9, 10, ... samplers), and the
vertex descriptor block's address and size against VA 0x0005000000, before any limit change.

### 1u. The cause of 1t: a direct read of sh256+k returns sh<k>; the online compiler now reads past sh255 through idx0 (2026-09-29)

The cause of 1t, measured on unlanded branches (STATE-am62p, records/am62p/{vsunits-cause, vsunits-bound,
vsunits-sh256, doutd-split, shared-size, sh-index}). A vertex stage whose shared registers pass sh255 (V x 20
descriptor dwords + the uniforms) read wrong: V=13 silent zeros, V=14/16 a TCU fault at VA 0x0005000000. The DMA was
not the cause. The DOUTD burst split (7ff706db) changed nothing, and every size word (PDS_STATE0, DOUTD, VDM_STATE5)
equals Mesa's. gl_test 150 (shprobe) showed that a vertex read of sh256+k returns sh<k>. Our direct 11-bit form
matches pco_isa.py, but Mesa never emits it: pco_legalize.c try_legalize_large_hwreg_offsets rewrites every hardware
register operand >= 256 to `movi32 idx0 = base` + an idx0-relative read (Mesa 26.2.1 source). dfdb721c does the same
(prepare::index_high_shared: mbyp slot 0 and the sample's image and sampler words; any other operand past sh255 is
refused, not wrapped).

Landing tip am62p/sh-index-land **c46a5ad0** = origin/main d6719d3b (cde7cf03 + review/v3d-gl-tests) + gl_test 149 (adb588ee 8c9f7404 97a0bde8) +
gl_test 150 (0a7e2905) + c46a5ad0, all `cherry-pick -x`. 4533ff3d (drop the sh256 draw refusal) is not picked
because that refusal never reached main. Host on c46a5ad0: host-test,shaderc-online 2654 / 0 (3 ignored), host-test
1771 / 0, clippy 0 on both, fmt ok. usc_limits `light_amount.14omni`: the chain holds 2,001,456 B (was 1,882,660,

### 1w. texture.mipmap.{2d,cube}.projected FIXED: exact per-pixel gradients from the plane equations; random fragment.53 / vertex.39 FIXED by exact constant folding (2026-09-30)

Branch am62p/proj-lod: 85f92805 (the gradients) + fd705ae6 (no gradients for a constant W; fmad; shared gradients),
on 2362422d, then merged with 939c1fda (b74eb0a6: fold_constants, below). All runs on Zephyr, online compiler, AM62P, one image per filter line
(tools/cts/am62p-deqp-images.sh); records in records/am62p/proj-lod/ (INDEX.txt sha256 65a323ed, 25 files).

**Cause.** The TPU takes its implicit level from one set of derivatives per 2x2 quad. For a
perspective-interpolated coordinate the derivatives change from pixel to pixel, and the pixel diagonal to the
quad's anchor got a level outside what dEQP's verifier allows (1m's mask: every failing 2D pixel in one quad slot).
The evidence is the fix: with exact per-pixel derivatives all 16 pass and no control moves. 1n's attempt differed in
the derivatives (fdsxf/fdsyf, whose encoding and meaning were never settled); this path uses no derivative
instruction.

**The formula.** The iterator gives u = P / Q, P the component's plane and Q the W plane (`ditrp`), both linear in
the pixel's x and y, so du/dx = (A_P - u A_Q) / Q and du/dy = (B_P - u B_Q) / Q -- the derivative dEQP's reference
takes. A and B are each plane's first two coefficients (ROGUE_USC_COEFFICIENT_SET_A/B, read with `mbyp` from the
coefficient file as pco reads a flat varying's C), Q is W's no-divide iterate (gl_FragCoord.w's register). The
sample is `smp lodm = gradients` with d/dx, d/dy per coordinate after the coordinates (pco_emit_nir_smp's order).
It applies to an implicit-level texture2D / texture() / native textureCube of a smooth varying read as it is; a
computed coordinate, a flat varying, a bias, a level and texture2DProj are untouched. Switch pvr_proj_lod (Linux
YAKOGL_PVR_PROJ_LOD): 0 off, 1 2D, 2 2D and cube (default).

**Constant W.** A program whose vertex shader writes gl_Position.w as one compile-time constant on every path
(ir::Module::constant_position_w: a literal, through the locals vec4(...) lowers to, stored at top level; an if,
a loop, a return before it, a uniform, an attribute or arithmetic is not constant) has every varying affine and the
TPU's own level exact. At link (backend.rs link_online) its fragment shader, when it samples with plane gradients,
is compiled again without them; the program is the one pvr_proj_lod = 0 compiles, dword for dword, and so are its
blend variants (host test a_constant_w_program_samples_as_the_switch_off_does). Cost of that link: one more fragment
record, 1,920 keep bytes for a textured quad, 0.3-0.4 ms on the host (a vertex compile included); the shader object's
own record stays until it is deleted. The offline table path is unchanged. **No dEQP GLES2 texture group has a
constant W** (glsTextureTestUtil's vertex shader writes gl_Position = a_position), and gl_test's textured cases
either write a_pos or compute the coordinate (femtovg samples a computed coordinate and never takes the gradient
path), so the constant-W path is shown on the host only; on the board it is the program every earlier run drew
with.

**Cost** (tests/usc_limits.rs what_exact_gradients_cost_a_program, groups / dwords / temps, fd705ae6):

| fragment shader | pvr_proj_lod 0 or constant W | perspective W, 85f92805 | perspective W, fd705ae6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| textured quad (Slint-like) | 44 / 96 / 33 | 71 / 162 / 35 | 67 / 154 / 35 |
| dEQP mipmap shader | 52 / 116 / 33 | 79 / 182 / 35 | 75 / 174 / 35 |
| two look-ups of one varying | 48 / 104 / 36 | 98 / 224 / 39 | 75 / 168 / 37 |
| cube | 32 / 68 / 28 | 67 / 154 / 34 | 61 / 142 / 34 |

The first 2D look-up costs 23 groups (W's no-divide iterate with its fences 8, 1/W 1, W's slopes 2, per coordinate
2 slope moves + 2 fmads + 2 scalings), a later look-up of the same varying 4 (its gradient words), a cube 29.

**Board.**

(link_substituted's zero list) is compiled from the source without that list (online_blend_variant); seen while

### 1z. AM62P: 4x MSAA (2026-10-01)

Everything here is at the tip of the land119 series (the PowerVR and GL-core commits are the ones of pvr/msaa-4x, 211e4f89 before the rebase), on Zephyr, AM62P, with the dEQP image config `rgba8888d24s8ms4` (4 samples, RGBA8888, depth 24, stencil 8). No hardware recovery in any run. UART logs: build/logs/ of the pvr/msaa-4x worktree, uart-img<N>-<tag>.log; the final ones are *-g4x (4x), *-g1x (1x) and img2-f4x.

**Result at 4x.**

| group | result |
|---|---|
| multisample | 16 / 16 pass (16 NotSupported at 1x) |
| fragment_ops | 1923 / 1923 pass |
| color_clear | 19 / 19 pass |
| depth_stencil_clear | 11 / 11 pass |
| rasterization | 43 pass + 9 CompatibilityWarning |
| fbo.render | 319 / 319 pass |

The 9 warnings are "Interpolation of multisampled wide lines failed": rasterization.interpolation.basic.{line_loop, line_strip, lines}_wide, interpolation.projected.{line_loop, line_strip, lines}_wide and primitives.{line_loop, line_strip, lines}_wide. They were there before any of the fixes below; not investigated further.

**1x regression, same groups, unchanged from section 1y:** multisample 16 NotSupported, fragment_ops 1923 pass / 0 fail, color_clear 19, depth_stencil_clear 11, fbo.render 319, rasterization 47 pass plus the usual 5 QualityWarnings.

**The three causes.**

1. *INSTANCE versus FULL sample rate for programs that read the pixel.* A multisampled frame ran the fragment program at the PDS INSTANCE rate, so one invocation served all four samples. A program that reads the pixel (blend, framebuffer fetch) then saw one value for four samples. Such a program now runs at FULL (per sample) rate on a multisampled frame.
2. *Sample coverage and alpha to coverage were ignored.* glSampleCoverage and GL_SAMPLE_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE had no effect on a multisampled target. A new variant axis, LodKey::sample_kill (bit 63), adds a kill epilogue to the fragment program; the fragment meta word carries the sample mask and the alpha-to-coverage flag; these programs run at FULL rate. This follows Mesa's pco lower_isp_fb and pco_nir_lower_alpha_to_coverage. The FULL rate also matters for plain discard shaders: at INSTANCE rate sample 0 decided the whole pixel, so a discard killed or kept all four samples together.
3. *A draw with an empty coverage mask hangs the next frame.* glSampleCoverage(0, FALSE) or (1, TRUE) kills every sample of a draw; on the AM62P the next frame then hits a hardware reset (HWR, dm=3). The hardware cause is unknown. The GL core now drops such a draw (covers_no_sample in culls_everything). **Residual risk:** other draws that kill every sample (alpha to coverage with alpha 0 everywhere, a shader that discards everything on 4x) may hang the same way; they are not caught.

**Performance note.** 4x frames that use the coverage or alpha-to-coverage variants are slow: kicks over 20 ms were re-posted in multisample.proportionality_alpha_to_coverage and in depth_stencil_clear. Frame times were not measured. This belongs to the performance phase.
