## The twin-draw rung, host half: 65 of 324 sources can be drawn both ways

team-lead's instrument, and the reason for it is the miscompile: a suite score
is bounded by its coverage, and the corpus is far wider coverage than 29
hand-written cases. Each source gets drawn twice into the same scene -- once
through the online compiler, once through the offline table's blob for the same
source -- and the pixels are compared, following `gl_test` case 52's "draw it
both ways and compare" pattern.

The host half cannot compare pixels. What it can settle, and what the board run
depends on, is **how many sources have both sides at all**
(`tests/twin_draw_list.rs`):

| | count |
|---|---|
| corpus sources in the table | **324** |
| **TWINNABLE** (blob + online compiles) | **65** |
| blob exists, online refuses | 256 |
| online compiles, no blob | 0 |
| neither | 3 |

and the refusals, by kind:

| refusal | count | is it a defect? |
|---|---|---|
| GLSL ES 3.00 source | 166 | no -- correctly refused by an ES 2.0 compiler |
| `Abi(OutOfMemory)` | **74** | **an open limit**, see below |
| unsupported `#version` | 13 | no |
| parse: "expected a type" | 3 | front-end gaps, es100-frontend's list |

FemtoVG-named sources: **30 of 44** are twinnable.

Two things worth saying plainly.

**The population is 324, not 137.** "137 through the chain" is the ES 1.00
subset that compiles; the table holds 324 sources, and the rung's denominator
is 65. A rung reporting "0 mismatches" without that number would be reporting
over a set nobody had counted -- the failure pvrgpu-platform's USC gate hit
when it read 0 over 72.4 % while skipping 159,305 groups, and which is now the
rule that a gate asserts its population. This test asserts it.

**74 sources refuse with `Abi(OutOfMemory { left: 30 })`.** I assumed that was
the temps ceiling and grouped it as such; printing one message in full said
otherwise -- it is the code generator running out of ABI space, a separate
limit with its own number. Recorded as an open item rather than attributed:
whoever owns the ABI allocator should see 74 of 324 table sources hitting it,
and the whole `distancefieldtext` family is in there. It also caps the
twin-draw rung's reach until it moves.

The board half (drawing each twinnable source both ways and counting
mismatching pixels per source) is next, after the record read and the vendor
arms. The expected table is 0 mismatches for all 65, with no exceptions yet:
exceptions get written when the board says so, not before.

## The confirmation rung on 43a3ccf: k=22..24 is right ONLINE and wrong REMOTE

The band 2|3 ceiling is 26 on main now (read from `abi.rs`, not from the commit
message), and re-deriving on `43a3ccf` gives:

| k | online | remote |
|---|---|---|
| 20 | 25 temps | 21 temps |
| **21** | **26 temps** | 22 temps |
| 22 | **REFUSED BY CEILING** | 23 temps |
| 23 | REFUSED BY CEILING | 24 temps |
| 24 | REFUSED BY CEILING | **25 temps** |
| **25** | REFUSED BY CEILING | **26 temps** |
| **26** | REFUSED BY CEILING | **27 temps** |
| **27** | REFUSED BY CEILING | **28 temps** |
| **28** | REFUSED BY CEILING | **29 temps** |

The online half of the ruling is exactly right: `k=21` is 26 temps, admitted on
a stock pair, and every rung above it is refused by the guard working as
intended.

**The remote half is not.** The ruling names `k=22, 23, 24` for the remote arms,
but on the remote path those are **23, 24 and 25 temps** -- all BELOW the 26/27
boundary, all predicted to draw. Running them would have produced three draws
and looked like "the wedge is gone at these temps", when the rungs simply never
reached the boundary. That is the same failure as the old n4 ladder, arriving
from the other direction: last time the compiler moved under fixed file names,
this time the file names moved between back ends.

It is the rule catching its own author, which is the point of having it: a rung
is named by the temps the pair's compiler reports, and `k` is not a rung.

### The rung, corrected

| arm | path | k | temps | prediction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| control | online, stock pair | **21** | 26 | **draws** |
| control (cross-check) | remote | **25** | 26 | **draws** |
| wedge | remote | **26** | 27 | **wedges** |
| wedge | remote | **27** | 28 | **wedges** |
| wedge | remote | **28** | 29 | **wedges** |

The remote control at k=25 is worth its board time: it puts 26 temps on the GPU
through the OTHER compiler, so if it draws while the online 26 also draws, the
boundary is a property of the temp count rather than of either compiler's
output, which is the claim the whole ladder rests on and has never been tested
directly.

## WITHDRAWN: the 14 FemtoVG sources "that cannot be twinned"

> **Everything in this section is withdrawn.** The online compiler builds all
> 16 FemtoVG vertex shaders. The refusals were MY HARNESS: it compiled 324
> sources in one process, and the compiler's keep arena (512 KiB of `.bss`
> holding every compiled shader's code, reflection and names for the life of
> the process, never reset because the GL core's `ShcShader` points into it)
> fills after about 65 shaders at ~8 KiB each. Everything after that is refused
> with `Abi(OutOfMemory)`. shaderc-remote named it (`2e6914b`):
> `conicalgradient.vert` and `lineargradient.vert` both compile, arena
> 0 -> 3648 -> 7568, and 69 of the 71 refused compile once the arena is reset.
>
> So the "product gap" below -- no vertex shader for gradients, image
> particles, stencil clip or texture fill -- was false, and I stated it in the
> strongest terms available. The corrected measurement is in the next section.
>
> Two things are worth keeping from the error. The `left: 30` being identical
> across all 14 was visible in my own output and is the signature of a shared
> budget rather than a per-shader limit; I read it as "a fixed budget exhausted
> at the same point", wrote that down, and still concluded a per-shader
> property. And the pattern I found so convincing -- every blocked source a
> vertex shader -- was an artefact of table ORDER, not of stage.
>
> Kept rather than deleted because the reasoning is the point.

## The 14 FemtoVG sources that cannot be twinned, named

team-lead asked for these individually, because a FemtoVG source the online
path cannot compile is a PRODUCT gap before it is a rung gap: this is the set
Slint draws with. Every one of the 14 gives the SAME refusal:

    online shaderc: the code generator refused this vertex shader:
    Abi(OutOfMemory { left: 30 })

    imageparticle_colored.vert          lineargradient.vert
    imageparticle_coloredpoint.vert     lineargradient.batchable.vert
    imageparticle_deformed.vert         radialgradient.vert
    imageparticle_simplepoint.vert      radialgradient.batchable.vert
    imageparticle_sprite.vert           stencilclip.vert
    imageparticle_tabled.vert           stencilclip.batchable.vert
                                        texturefill.vert
                                        texturefill.batchable.vert

### The pattern, which is sharper than the list

FemtoVG-named sources split **16 vertex, 28 fragment**. Of the 14 blocked,
**14 are vertex and 0 are fragment** -- every fragment shader in the set
compiles, and **14 of the 16 vertex shaders do not**.

The two vertex shaders that DO compile are `conicalgradient.vert` and
`conicalgradient.batchable.vert`. That is a minimal pair for whoever owns the
limit: `lineargradient.vert` is refused and `conicalgradient.vert` is not, same
family, same stage, same table, both with known-good blobs.

`texturefill.batchable.vert` being in the list is worth noting separately: it
is the shader pvrgpu-platform uses as the USC-2 gate example, so the two halves
of the compiler disagree about whether it is buildable -- the USC side builds
it group by group while the GC7000 side refuses it for ABI space.

### What this means for the product, stated plainly

The online compiler cannot today build the vertex shaders for image particles,
linear gradients, radial gradients, stencil clipping or texture fill. Those are
not corner cases; they are how Slint draws. A product image using the in-process
compiler would have no vertex shader for most of what it puts on the screen.

That is not a regression and nothing has broken -- the offline table has blobs
for all of them, which is what the shipping images use -- but it is the honest
size of the gap between "the in-process compiler works" and "the in-process
compiler can replace the table", and it belongs beside the 137/142 score rather
than behind it.

## The twin-draw partition, corrected: 137 twinnable, FemtoVG 44 of 44

With `forget_compiled()` between sources, so the harness measures the compiler
rather than its own arena:

| | before (one process) | corrected |
|---|---|---|
| corpus sources | 324 | 324 |
| **TWINNABLE** | 65 | **137** |
| blob exists, online refuses | 256 | **184** |
| online compiles, no blob | 0 | 0 |
| neither | 3 | 3 |
| **FemtoVG-named twinnable** | 30 of 44 | **44 of 44** |

The refusals that remain are real:

| refusal | count |
|---|---|
| GLSL ES 3.00 source (correct for an ES 2.0 compiler) | 169 |
| unsupported `#version` | 13 |
| the temps ceiling | **2** |
| `Abi(OutOfMemory)` | **0** |

The twinnable count landing on **137** is a coincidence worth flagging so nobody
reads meaning into it: it is not the same 137 as "137 of 142 through the chain".
Same number, different set.

### The two ceiling refusals, and a check that came back clean

`shapestroke.vert` and `shapestroke.batchable.vert`, at `num_out 5`, our temps
**21** against that band's ceiling of 16.

The ceiling's own criterion is "the highest `temps` any shipped BLOB in each
band carries", so a table source refused by it would be a contradiction if the
blob were above the bound. Checked rather than assumed -- the table's blobs for
those two carry **7 and 8** temps. Well under 16. No contradiction; the band is
consistent with its rule.

What it does show is a compiler-quality gap on a single source: **21 temps where
the reference needed 7**, on a shader both can build. That belongs with
shaderc-remote's allocator work rather than with the ceiling.

### The generator, verified against the passes that could fold it

shaderc-remote ran `gen()` against all three of their passes, including the
unwired range splitter (their measurement, my generator):

    k=21 num_out=2: coalesce removes 0 | split adds 0 | temps 26
    k=20 num_out=3: coalesce removes 0 | split adds 0 | temps 26

Coalescing removes nothing because the subtraction chain leaves no copy whose
two values fail to meet; splitting adds nothing because every rewrite of `s` is
read before the next, so there is no dead gap. Sinking moves 98 of 104
definitions and the temps stay at 26 -- the consumption order forcing all k
values live is doing the work, not a pass failing to fire.

They also confirmed "k is not a rung" from their side: `k=20` at num_out 3 and
`k=21` at num_out 2 both land on exactly 26 temps.

## The wedge probes are out of `tools/shaders/`, and the table reference is pinned

### Why they moved

`gen_shader_table.py` takes `os.walk(tools/shaders)` as its input list, on
purpose ("the input list is the whole tree rather than a hand-kept list"). So
anything under that tree becomes a row in the SHIPPED offline table at the next
rebuild, decided by nobody. es100-frontend found 13 of mine in a regenerated
table:

    wedge_probe/steps/s08.vert .. s36.vert   wedge_probe/a_many_temps.vert
    wedge_probe/b_many_instructions.vert     wedge_probe/d60_temps_low.vert
    wedge_probe/d70_temps_high.vert          wedge_probe/consume_v_color.frag

Some of those are shaders whose PURPOSE is to hang the GPU. `a_many_temps.vert`
shipping in a product image's table is not something anyone would choose, and
the ladder rows would have started counting in every "N of M sources" figure
the team quotes.

They now live in `tools/cts/wedge_probe/`, beside the harness that uses them.
`temps_survey.rs`, `temps_ladder.rs` and `wedge_real_sources.rs` follow, and
**no table row is affected** -- the probes were never in the committed table,
only in a regenerated one, so this changes nothing that ships and prevents a
change that would have.

### The committed table is THE reference, and the wedge fact's provenance

Regenerating the GC7000 table on this host changes **308 of the 324 existing
blobs** (this host's `etna_shc`/glslang against whatever produced the committed
table). So a rebuild is not "add two rows", it is "replace the reference".

Every wedge number in this document that involves a blob was measured against
the COMMITTED table, and that provenance matters most for one of them:

> **"the reference compiler's output wedges at temps 40"** -- the fact that
> makes the wedge a driver defect rather than a defect in our compiler -- was
> measured on `a_many_temps.vert`'s reference build.
>
> **CORRECTION (2026-09-22, mine).** I wrote "from the committed table" here and
> the lead adopted it into the preservation ruling. It is wrong, and checking
> before extracting is what caught it: `a_many_temps`, `hsl_to_rgb_vertex`,
> `rgb_to_hsl`, `k23` and `consume_v_color` are **not rows in the committed
> source table at all** -- 0 matches each, against 324 rows. They never were:
> they live under `wedge_probe/`, which is exactly why a regenerated table
> would have ADDED them (es100-frontend's finding) and why they moved out.
>
> So there is no committed-table blob for those sources to preserve, and the
> extraction as specified cannot be performed. Their reference builds came from
> `etna_shc` at run time through the remote back end, which is the only path
> that can produce them at those temp counts.
>
> That changes the exposure rather than removing it: the fact rests on
> `etna_shc`'s identity, not on the table's. shaderc-remote has now pinned that
> identity in the generator header, so the right preservation for these facts
> is the etna_shc digest recorded beside them -- not a file copied out of a
> table that never held them.

The same applies to the twin-draw partition and to any byte comparison in the
ladder work. Until shaderc-remote pins `etna_shc` and reports how many of the
324 reproduce byte-identically, ladder byte comparisons are against the
committed table only.

## The twin-draw partition, every bucket named

es100-frontend named the last unnamed bucket, and the grouping keys are updated
for the messages the compiler now prints (`ef31582`):

| | count | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| **TWINNABLE** | **137** | blob + online compile: the rung's population |
| GLSL ES 3.00 | 169 | 166 by `#version`, 3 by type name under a mislabelled `#version 100`; correct for an ES 2.0 compiler |
| desktop GLSL 450 | 13 | correct for an ES compiler |
| the temps ceiling | 2 | `shapestroke{,.batchable}.vert`, num_out 5 -- a named defect with an owner |
| neither | 3 | |
| `Abi(OutOfMemory)` | **0** | was my harness; gone with the arena reset |
| parse gaps | **0** | were `sampler2DArray` under a mislabelled `#version 100` |

**Every refusal is now either a correct refusal or a named defect with an
owner.** No bucket reads "the compiler cannot do this" without a name attached,
which was not true of this table an hour ago.

The 13 are not a corpus quirk: the offline generators accept GLSL 450 with
explicit locations as well as GLSL ES 1.00, so those sources exist *because* the
offline path wants them, and the online path refusing them is the point of
having two spellings.

One distinction kept from es100-frontend because it prevents a wrong diagnosis:
`#version 300` WITHOUT `es` is a typo, not an unsupported version -- there is no
desktop GLSL 300/310/320 -- so it gets its own bucket rather than being counted
as desktop.

### What this survey cannot see, which is worth knowing before reading it

It walks `SHC_SOURCE_TABLE`, the GENERATED table, not the source tree.
`armselect.frag` and `es100/swizzled_broadcast.frag` are on disk and on main,
and they do not appear here at all -- not as "online compiles, no blob", but as
absent, because the table has not been regenerated (the rebuild is blocked on
toolchain drift).

So the "online compiles, no blob" row cannot rise when a new source lands; both
halves of this partition come from the same generated file, and that row can
only be nonzero for a source that is IN the table and lost its blob. Anyone
expecting it to count new sources will be disappointed for a structural reason
rather than a bug, and the population announced with the rebuild is what moves
these numbers.

## Pairing by name would make the twin-draw rung cover 6 programs, not 137

A draw needs both stages and the table lists shaders one at a time, so the
obvious pairing is by base name -- `lineargradient.vert` with
`lineargradient.frag`. Measured before writing the walk:

    DRAWABLE PAIRS: 12 of 137 twinnable sources have a twinnable partner
    = 6 complete programs; 125 sources have no twinnable partner
    first unpaired: matattr.frag, matattr2.vert, matattr3.vert, matattr4.vert,
                    fill_color.frag, fill_color.glyph.frag

**So name pairing is unusable.** The corpus is mostly fragment shaders with no
same-named vertex shader beside them -- `fill_color.frag` has no
`fill_color.vert`, the FemtoVG fragment shaders are written against a handful of
shared vertex shaders, and the vertex-only families (`matattr2..4`) have no
fragment twin at all. A rung built that way would draw 6 programs and report a
denominator that sounds like corpus-wide coverage.

The remaining design is the one the rung's question actually needs: pair the
source under test with a **generated partner** for the other stage, synthesised
from the source's own reflection so the varyings link, and bind zeros/identity
to its attributes and uniforms. Many shaders then draw a flat colour, which is
fine: the question is whether the two COMPILERS agree on the same input, not
whether the picture is a picture. Both arms get the same generated partner and
the same bound values, so any pixel difference is still attributable to the
compiler.

That is more work than name pairing and it is the difference between a rung
that covers 6 programs and one that covers 137. Measuring first cost one test
run; discovering it after writing the walk would have cost the walk.

## THE THREE DISCRIMINATING ARMS RAN, and all three DRAW

**Run by the user, 2026-09-22, not by me.** My session's classifier refused the
command (its purpose is to hang a GPU) and the lead declined to route around
that, so the user ran it and pasted the output. Recorded here verbatim as
theirs.

| arm | fragment partner | result |
|---|---|---|
| `k23.vert` (27 temps in our blob) | `consume_v_color.frag` | covered **4096 of 4096**, (16,16) = `0xffff0000`, PASS, exit 0 |
| `hsl_to_rgb_vertex.vert` | `hsl_to_rgb_vertex.frag` | covered **4096 of 4096**, (16,16) = `0xff31531e`, PASS, exit 0 |
| `a_many_temps.vert` (40 temps) | `consume_v_color.frag` | covered **4096 of 4096**, (16,16) = `0xffff0000`, PASS, exit 0 |

All three at grid 92 (8,649 vertices, 16,928 triangles), "the draw returned" on
each, through the vendor user space on `galcore 6.4.11.p2`, display from GBM on
`/dev/dri/renderD128`. `galcore` was at refcount 5, held by `sarta`, reported
and not removed; the product container was neither stopped nor restarted.

**The prediction on file -- all three draw -- held.**

### What this settles, and what it does not

The same GLSL that wedges our stack at 27 and at 40 temps draws under the
vendor stack on the same GPU, same silicon, same kernel driver version. So:

> **The wedge is not a property of these sources on this hardware.** It is
> ours: our driver's programming, or an assumption in the blobs we run about
> state that galcore sets and `gcgpu` does not.

That is the question the whole ladder existed to answer, and it is answered
against us.

**It does NOT yet distinguish two remaining stories**, and the difference
matters:

1. the hardware wedges above some register count and the vendor compiler simply
   stays below it -- in which case the temps axis is real and our compiler's
   counts are the problem; or
2. our driver wedges at any count, and temps was a proxy for something else
   that happens to correlate -- in which case the ladder was measuring the
   wrong axis all along.

The measurement that separates them is **the vendor compiler's own register
counts for these three sources**, beside ours (27, 16/17, 40). If the vendor's
counts are at or above ours, story 2 and the driver's state programming is the
cause. If below, story 1 stands and the vendor avoids a real limit.

That measurement is mine and next, through the vendor user space's own
reporting -- never a CPU read of the shader-state registers, which is what reset
this board twice.

### `texture.mipmap`: power-of-two mip chains (`713c3b5`)

The fix steps a PowerVR mip chain by `npot2(h * layers) >> i` rows, which is
the TPU's own arithmetic. Prediction, written before either arm was read:
2d unchanged; cube cases reaching level >= 1 go FAIL -> PASS; nothing goes
PASS -> FAIL; gl_test unchanged.

| arm | cases | pass | fail | timeout | fence timeouts | recoveries |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before `es2-9c0f78a` | 112 | 44 | 60 | **8** | 16+ | 9 (7 by the runner; 2 reloads by hand: one after the failed gcgpu-reload, one before the last resume) |
| after `es2-713c3b5` | 112 | 44 | 68 | 0 | **0** | **0** |

The 8 Timeouts are `cube.generate.*_fastest`. Each one wedged the GPU in an
HWR storm (dm=3, BIF read faults from TCU tag 25, i.e. the texture unit
reading past the storage). With the fix they complete and read Fail.

**No case changed from pass to fail, and none from fail to pass.** Pass/fail
cannot show what the fix did; the invalid-pixel counts dEQP prints can:

| cases | before (invalid px) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `cube.basic.*` (4) | 16384 each | 640 – 1404 |
| `cube.projected.*` (4) | 12735 – 16384 | 649 – 1318 |
| `cube.generate.*_nicest` (8) | 12800 – 15360 | 1890 – 2326 |
| `cube.generate.*_fastest` (8) | wedged | 1844 – 2552 |
| all 40 failing `2d.*` cases | — | identical to the pixel |

So the prediction "cube FAIL -> PASS" is **refuted as stated**. Before the fix
the whole cube image was wrong; after it, 4–15 % of it is. That residue is a

## One gl_test 63 through etna_shc poisons the GC7000 for every later client (2026-09-23)

A board fact, and the reason several results from this session are void.

**The trigger, deterministic.** One run of gl_test case 63 (matattr: mat2/3/4 vertex
attributes) with its program compiled by etna_shc, through either the remote pair or the
offline pair. After it, every LATER client on the board draws garbage: fresh processes, on
any pair, the online pair included. The frames read 0x00000000 or 0xffffffff, the clear
included. There is no fence timeout, no recovery and no kernel line. The state persists
until the GPU core is reset. Measured on gcgpu `72b5fd64a143`, with strictly serial runs
and 0 holders of /dev/gcgpu before each one:

| sequence | then online 69 / case 1 |
|---|---|
| fresh load; online 69 x60 | 60/60 PASS; `mmu_straddles` +1 on every run, so it is NOT the cause |
| online-compiled 63 (fails its own checks), x4 | PASS / PASS every time |
| remote e31bd3e 63, x2 | FAIL / FAIL |
| offline e31bd3e 63, x2 | FAIL / FAIL |
| remote 63, `scrub_allocs=1` (every allocation zeroed) | FAIL / FAIL, so not memory contents |
| remote 63, then a forced recovery (gl_test 72 on the 9c0f78a lib, resets +1) | PASS / PASS |

A core reset clears it. gc-backend's command-stream decoder shows on the host that every
register the matattr draws write is also written by ordinary draws, and that every stream
clears the attribute array first. So the poisoned state is below the programmed registers:
an internal cache or state machine, or the MMU. The missing flush or invalidate is still
open. Containment: `close_reset` (a reset of an idle GPU on the last close), and
`dump_state`, which lets the status block be compared.

**What it voided.** The onset of the first bad window was a remote 63 at about 07:35 JST,
inside my e31bd3e case loop. **It was not `mmu_straddles`, not concurrency and not the code
under test.** The window closed at the reset of 07:39, and a second window opened with the
41e005b control's 63 at 07:41. Void, and re-measured where noted:

- the e31bd3e **remote** failures of 69/70/73/74. On a fresh module 69/70 PASS 3/3 on
  both remote pairs; 71, 72, 73 and 75 PASS; 74 FAILS without poisoning (etna_shc's own
  code, gc-backend's). **So there is no remote regression at e31bd3e, and my first report
  of one is retracted.**
- the "offline e31bd3e fails nearly the whole regression set" run. On a fresh module
  offline e31bd3e scores 31/38 (GLSL 450) and 25/29 (ES 1.00), the known targets, the same
  as offline 41e005b.
- the head loops c00 on e31bd3e (80 / 12 / 7 / 1 Timeout). Its one "new" timeout,
  `do_while_constant_iterations.101_iterations_fragment`, PASSES 3 of 3 alone on a fresh
  module (canary PASS, 0 recoveries), and through the remote pair too.

Nothing before 07:35 ran 63 through etna_shc in this session. Task 1, the chunked shaders
sweep, arm d, arm c, the five-arm gl_test and the e31bd3e online gl_test and m4 stand.

**A second opener.** gcgpu is exclusive per PROCESS, by design (gc_chardev.c). A second
process gets `EBUSY` and "held by pid N"; a second fd in the same process is allowed on
purpose. None of today's runs overlapped: the file birth times and the kernel's close lines
are serial.

**The instrument, from now on.** gl_test case 1 runs as a canary before every measured
client, or every dEQP chunk. A failed canary aborts the run, and nothing measured after it
is reported.

### The cube residue after `713c3b5`, read from dEQP's images

8 cube cases were run with `LOG_IMAGES` on `es2-713c3b5`. The invalid pixels are
1–2 px lines lying exactly on the cube-face **seams** in screen space, and they
appear in `nearest_nearest` too, where there is no bilinear tap. In
`cube.basic.nearest_nearest`, 381 of the 640 are pure black; the rest are
neighbouring faces' colours. Two mechanisms explain that picture:

1. **Seam LOD.** `pvr_cubeUV` returns `v = (uv.y + face) / 6`, which jumps by at least
   1/6 across a seam. A 2x2 quad on a seam therefore gets a huge derivative
   and samples the last level (maxlod is clamped to the written chain,
   `backend.rs:2027`). This is shader translation and is not fixed here.
2. **The last level read wrong.** It is 1x6, and a 1-wide level was laid out at
   `tex_pitch(1)` = 2 texels a row. The TPU reads it one texel a row
   (Mesa `pitch = cpp * width`). `fde0086` fixes that; the same mechanism is
   predicted to be behind every failing `2d.*_non_square` case (32x64, tail 1x2
   and 1x1).

The half-texel face clamp at LOD > 0 (the lead's first suspect) is real for
LINEAR filters only: the `linear_linear` masks carry extra edge rows. It is
secondary to the seams.

## Native-cube probe: predictions, written before any run (2026-09-23, am62p-board)

**Why it exists.** YakoGL samples a cube through a stacked 2D texture and the
translator's `pvr_cubeUV` since `0bbdb8a` (2026-09-17): "The TPU's cube and
array texture types need the twiddled memory layout this core does not write".
That reason is correct: Mesa gives a LINEAR layout only `TEXTYPE_STRIDE`, and
only for 2D and 2D_ARRAY views; a CUBE view is `FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED` there,
and `TEXTYPE_CUBE` exists only for TWIDDLED memory (`pvr_arch_tex_state.c:139-170`).
The emulation costs the seams (the cube residue after `713c3b5`, above) or,
fixed in the shader, ~130 instruction words per fetch (the shelved
`279815d`/`da5fe1d`: 212 -> 344 on the minimal `textureCube` shader). The
native fetch compiles to **54** words where the emulated one is **212**
(pco_shc build-new, the probe's part S shaders). The probe asks whether the
hardware path works on this silicon before anyone rebuilds the texture path.

**What it is.** `driver/tools/pvrlab/user/cube_probe.c`, linking the static
archive; everything opt-in and off by default:
- `gl::cube_probe` (`yakogl_probe_native_cube(1)`): the draw resolver
  re-lays out a cube's texels into Mesa's twiddled cube layout on the CPU
  (face-major; each face a full chain to 1x1, `pvr_image.c:141-190`; each
  level in `texture::twiddle_index` order, the block order the ETC path
  already feeds this TPU) and binds it as `GLES_TEXTYPE_CUBE_TWIDDLED_PROBE`;
- the PowerVR descriptor for that type: `TEXTYPE_CUBE` (3), the twiddled
  `IMAGE_WORD1` (`texstate.xml:292-312`: num_mip_levels [0:3], depth 5 at
  [4:14], mipmaps_present [15], texaddr [16:53], baselevel 0), meta layer
  size = one face's full chain (`pvr_arch_tex_state.c:278-286`);
- `PVR_BACKEND_OPT_PBE_TWIDDLE`: colour target 0 written `TWIDDLE_2D`
  (`pbestate.xml` REG_WORD0 memlayout [32:33] = 1, REG_WORD1 size_x [60:63] /
  size_y [28:31] = log2; Mesa `pvr_arch_job_common.c:140-157, 280-290`).
Host tests pin the shadow's texel placement, the descriptor words and the PBE
words. Every sampled texel is encoded (R = 16 face + level, G = 32 x, B = 32 y),
so a wrong answer names what was read.

**Board order.** Only after fde0086's push and its A/B, with fragment_ops or
any other client stopped by its runner PID.

### Predictions

| part | arm | prediction | what a failure would say |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (explicit LOD, NEAREST, 3072 samples: every texel centre of 6 faces x 4 levels, and 1/1000 inside both edges of every face and level) | emul (ES 3.00, `pvr_cubeLod`, probe off) | **0 wrong** | nonzero = the harness or the emulation is wrong; the native arm cannot be read until it is 0 |
| A | native (GLSL 450 `samplerCube`, probe on) | **0 wrong** | every sample from face 0 (or one face) = `depth`/layer count not taken. Right face, level 0 right, levels >= 1 wrong = level offsets inside a face. Right face and level, (x, y) permuted = twiddle bit order (x/y interleave swapped). A consistent face permutation = face order or orientation. Levels near the tail reading the next face = layer stride not the full chain to 1x1. `00000000` everywhere = the descriptor was refused or the TCU faulted: read dmesg for BIF faults and HWR before anything else |
| S (implicit LOD, 8 x 8, the quad crosses -X, +Z, +X; the 2x2 quads at columns 2-3 and 6-7 straddle a seam) | emul | the straddling quads read **level 3** (the 1x1 tail; the stacked v jumps by >= 1/6), every other pixel level 0 or 1 | no level 3 on the seam quads = the emulation's seam defect is not what the dEQP images showed |
| S | native | **no level 3 anywhere**; every pixel level 0 or 1, faces -X / +Z / +X in that order across the row | a level 3 on the seam quads = the hardware derives the cube LOD the same broken way (unexpected: Mesa relies on it) |
| B (16 x 16, each pixel writes (16 x, 16 y), read back raw) | PBE_TWIDDLE on | **256 of 256 "twiddled"** (or "twiddled+yflip" if the FBO rows are stored bottom-up) | "linear 256" = memlayout is ignored and the twiddled render-to-face path needs another mechanism. Partial counts = size_x/size_y wrong (the interleave stops at the smaller size). Nothing written = the PBE state was refused |

If A native and B both hold, native cube is the product path (twiddled
storage, twiddled render-to-face, and the translator passing samplerCube
through), and the shader seam fix is dropped. If A holds and B does not, the
renders Qt's IBL makes into cube levels are the blocker, and that is decided
then.

## Candidate, unowned: native 2D arrays without twiddling

Mesa describes a LINEAR 2D_ARRAY view as `TEXTYPE_STRIDE` with the array
layers (`pvr_arch_tex_state.c:139-146`; the layer stride in the image meta).
So `pvr_arrUV` (the translator's 2D-array emulation, with its own half-texel
inset and LOD behaviour at layer boundaries) could become a native fetch with
no change to the GL core's linear storage. Not measured, not started.

check is gl_test case 85 (six 1x1 faces rendered and read back).

## Rust YakoGL + Qt Quick 3D on Zephyr: why it reset in 15 s (2026-09-23)

Every principledmaterial image built with the Rust library reset the board
within ~15 s and never drew; the C-era image (`build/q3d`, 2026-09-22) runs.
A Rust `gl_test` Zephyr image (GL_TEST_PANEL=2) does draw its spinning cube,
so this is not Rust-on-Zephyr in general. No console reaches the host, and DDR
is not retained across the reset (`driver/tools/kexec-zephyr/README.md`), so the
fault was read off the panel. A diagnostic Zephyr module, kept out of every
tree, replaces `k_sys_fatal_error_handler` (with `CONFIG_QT_RESET_ON_FATAL=n`,
the RAM console on, UART console off, `CONFIG_LOG_MODE_MINIMAL`). It draws the
RAM console's tail with an 8x8 font on the DSS application plane (the buffer
Qt last set, recorded through `-Wl,--wrap=am62p_dss_set_app_buffer`, or its
own buffer), waits 90 s and cold-reboots. The camera read:

    qt.rhi.general: Created OpenGL context QSurfaceFormat(version 3.0, ...
      redBufferSize 5, greenBufferSize 6, blueBufferSize 5, alphaBufferSize 0, ...)
    QZephyrWindow: eglCreateWindowSurface(buffer 0) failed: 0x3009
    QEGLPlatformContext: eglMakeCurrent failed: 3009
    QRhiGles2: Failed to make context current. Expect bad things to happen.
    Failed to create RHI (backend 2)
    Failed to initialize graphics backend for OpenGL.
    abort()
    >>> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR 4: Kernel panic on CPU 0

Qt's Zephyr platform plugin (`qtbase/src/plugins/platforms/zephyr/
qzephyrglcontext.cpp`) hands `QEGLPlatformContext` the context's default
format, every colour size -1, without the screen's depth (eglfs merges it in).
`eglChooseConfig` sorts per EGL 1.5 3.4.1 (`src/gl/egl.rs`; dEQP-EGL checks
the order): with no colour size asked for, the smaller `EGL_BUFFER_SIZE` comes
first, so Qt takes the 565 config. `eglCreateWindowSurface` then returns
`EGL_BAD_MATCH` for it on an XRGB8888 window, correctly. The C-era library
listed its configs in a fixed order with 8888 first (`55de113`
`gl_egl.c:385-387`), which hid it. With only the 565 config moved last,
principledmaterial renders on the Rust library (above).

The fix belongs to the Qt port: ask for the screen's depth (8/8/8 on an
XRGB8888 screen). Making YakoGL list 8888 first would break 3.4.1. Not
changed here; the Qt repository is held back by its owner.

## gl_test case 85 `cubetail`: predictions, written before any run

The six 1x1 faces of a 4x4 cube's level 2, each cleared to its own colour
through an FBO attachment (a PBE write), in face order 0..5 and then, with
other colours, in reverse order 5..0; after each pass all six are read back
with `glReadPixels`. Pass 1 face f = (16+32f, 64, 240-32f); pass 2 face f =
(200, 16+32f, 96). Exact 8-bit values, tolerance 0.

| arm | prediction | what a failure says |
|---|---|---|
| `76722f6` (before fde0086: 1-wide rows a pair apart) | 12 of 12 | a failure here is not fde0086's; the case or the FBO path is wrong |
| `fde0086` or later | **12 of 12**, if the PBE writes only the pixel inside the 1x1 clip | pass 1 correct but pass 2 faces 1..5 reading face f-1's green (16+32(f-1)) = the PBE writes the whole pixel pair, and fde0086 corrupts render-to-cube-level; face 0 stays right in both passes |

Not included: sampling level 2 (GL_TEXTURE_BASE_LEVEL is not modelled, and a
shader with an explicit LOD above 0 would be a new table entry).

## Native-cube probe, first run at `bfff969` (2026-09-23)

Pair `es2-bfff969` (libGLESv2 `8ca8d5bc…`, cube_probe `6ffdc7a0…` on the
board), module `9c0f78ac81f1` (driver sources identical), shader server as
above. 0 fence timeouts, 0 HWR, no fault line.

| part | prediction | measured |
|---|---|---|
| A emul (control) | 0 wrong | **0 of 3072 wrong**: held |
| A native | 0 wrong | **2560 of 3072 wrong**. The 512 right are exactly face 0, every level, centres and edges; faces 1..5 read `00000000` |
| S emul | seam quads read level 3 | `x0 x0 x3 Z3 Z1 Z1 Z3 X3` in every row: the two straddling quads (columns 2-3, 6-7) read level 3; held |
| S native | no level 3 | every pixel decodes as face 0 level 0 (`00000000`) except the last column (`X1`, a real +X read): the same face defect as A |
| B PBE TWIDDLE_2D | 256 twiddled | **256 of 256 twiddled**, in `texture::twiddle_index` order: held |

The native failure matched none of the predicted signatures exactly. The
closest, "every sample from face 0", was wrong in its detail: faces 1..5 read
zeros, not face 0's texels. That is a face STRIDE the TPU does not share
with the shadow. Mesa aligns a layered image's layer size to the page
size (`pvr_image.c:190-196`, 4 KiB, tied in its comment to
`RGX_CR_TPU_TAG_CEM_4K_FACE_PACKING_EN`); the shadow packed faces 340 bytes
apart, so the TPU read face f at f x 4096, past the 2040-byte shadow. Face 0
being right at every level also settles the descriptor, the level offsets
inside a face and the twiddle order. The shadow now puts faces on 4 KiB
boundaries; prediction for the re-run: A native 0 of 3072 wrong, S native
faces -X / +Z / +X across the row with no level 3.

## gl_test cases 82 `fragcoord` and 83 `pointcoord`: predictions, written before any run

Case 82 was renamed `fragcentre` (shader `es100/fragcentre.frag`) when it was
merged with gc-backend's case 84 `fragcoord` (e25f7b6), which had taken the
same case name, file and shader symbol; the two cases are separate.

Measurements for usc-backend's record design (the gl_FragCoord y transform
and gl_PointCoord), on the REMOTE pair (pco compiles the shaders). Readback
is raw `glReadPixels`, GL rows, so "GL (x, y)" is the same pixel in every
target.

**82** writes R = 4 floor(x), G = 4 floor(y), B = 128 fract(x) + 64 fract(y):

| target | GL-correct answer | predicted on the remote pair | what the other answers mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| FBO (not flipped) | G = 4y, B = 96 | **G = 4y, B = 96: PASS** | B = 0: the hardware position reaches the shader without the +0.5 centre and pco does not add it (then the (scale, offset) pair must carry +0.5 too) |
| default framebuffer (stored top-down, flip_y) | G = 4y | **G = 4 (63 - y): FAIL** (usc-backend: pco reads the hardware y raw) | G = 4y here as well: something already flips it, and the record field would be double-counting |

**83** draws one 16-pixel sprite centred on the pixel corner (32, 32) with a
vertex colour (0.25, 0.75, 0.5) the fragment shader never reads, and
`gl_FragColor = (s, t, 0, 1)`:

| predicted | what it says |
|---|---|
| **FAIL: every sprite pixel reads the vertex colour (R 0x40, G 0xbf)**, following usc-backend's reading: pco iterates gl_PointCoord from coefficients 4..11 and moves the user varyings after them, its record does not say so, and the backend lays out coefficients from the record | the point-coordinate plane is not produced, and the FS's point-coordinate read gets the colour varying's coefficients |
| PASS: s and t ramp as ES 2.0 3.3 gives them (t from the top) | the TA produces the plane and the layouts agree after all; usc-backend's concern would be disproved |
| a ramp with t from the BOTTOM | point sprites work but the origin is Vulkan's lower-left convention mistaken for GL's, or the reverse |
| black inside the sprite | the point was not rasterised at size 16 (the size attribute or the PPP point path) |

## Task, unassigned: window/pixmap GPU mappings are never released

`eglDestroySurface` leaves a window surface's mapping in place on purpose
(`src/gl/egl.rs` destroy_surface: "the pool VA range is not reclaimable
without an unmap"), and pixmap EGLImages map their pages the same way.
`gpu_free` is not a substitute: the Zephyr OSALs (`zephyr.c`,
`zephyr_gc.c`) put any allocation with a CPU view on the pending-free list
and would hand a heap range that maps the CALLER's pages back to the pool.
It needs an unmap in the OSAL interface and in both render services.

Does anything churn them in steady state? Not Qt on this platform: the Zephyr
plugin creates its window surfaces once, lazily, and destroys them only
with the window (`qzephyrwindow.cpp`); Qt's EGLImage paths (qrhi,
qquickrendertarget) import native buffers and are not used here. The GC7000
product container runs the vendor stack, not YakoGL. What would exhaust the VA
pool is an application that recreates windows or pixmap images, such as a long
dEQP-EGL image sweep; pbuffers are freed.

The harness blamed that leak as an overrun: with two live mappings at one
CPU address (the old window and the new one), `rec.c` attributed a cache
operation to the first it found. It now takes the most recent. Rerun in
mode l0mpc: 142 runs, no HH-ERROR, and the invalidate that was pinned on
#39 (24000 bytes) is now on #60, the 24960-byte mapping that issued it.

## gcgpu f110fd13eebc on silicon: waits end, a client can no longer poison the next (2026-09-23)

The module was built from origin/main `f110fd13eebc` (sha256 `383acc77...` on the board) and
compared with `72b5fd64a143` (`3acfbfe5...`). All runs were serial, with a case-1 canary
before the measured clients. The wedge reproducer is gl_test 72 on the 9c0f78a library,
which hung 3 of 3 times today.

| arm | module, knobs | client exit | how | recoveries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 72b5fd6 | **121.8 s** | killed at 90 s; the close path's "1000 ms" wait took 32 s (00:14:54 -> 00:15:26 UTC) | 1, at close |
| B | f110fd1, hang_ms=0 | **91.0 s** | killed at 90 s; the close-path wait took 1008 ms | 1, at close |
| C | f110fd1, hang_ms=5000 | **10.2 s** | returned by itself, FAIL; "nothing retired for 5020 ms" twice, once per wedged draw | 2, in the client's own wait |

close_reset (the idle reset on the last close), with remote e31bd3e 63 run before a new
client:

| close_reset | then online 69 / case 1 | cost per client (gl_test 0 x10, mean open-run-close) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | FAIL / FAIL, twice | 44.9 ms |
| 1 | **PASS / PASS, twice, with no reload** | 47.6 ms (**+2.7 ms**) |

At hang_ms=5000 and close_reset=1, from a fresh load, the results against the regression set
were:

- m3 8/8, with 8 canaries.
- m4 25/29 on both pairs, failing 9 16 20 61 (unchanged).
- gl_test 25 stress PASS (191 s) and 26 heavy PASS (100 s). FemtoVG 27-38 12/12.
- **0 recoveries**, 34 idle resets (one per client).
- `max_quiet_ms` = **21**. This is the longest stretch any waiter saw with work outstanding
  and nothing retiring, including the ~200 s cases, so 5000 has about 240x headroom.
- `defer_full` 0, `defer_leaked` 0, `defer_peak` 33 of 256: the defer queue never filled.

**The status block cannot see the poison.** `dump_state` read clean, after online 63 and
after remote 63. The last one was confirmed poisoned: 69 and 1 FAIL right after it. All three
dumps read the same. SEC_STATUS was 0 with fault address 0, AXI_STATUS was 0xb7 and
IDLE_STATE was 0x7ffffffe (the FE in its idle loop) every time, and MODULE_STATUS and
DMA_DEBUG_STATE were unchanged. No MMU fault is latched and no error bit is set. The state
is internal: a cache or state machine that a core reset clears. gc-backend's b9cef32 (one
element per matrix column) is the candidate for the cause and is to be checked with
close_reset=0.

hang_ms and close_reset are still default-off. Both have now run the regression set on
silicon. Making them the default is a separate commit.

### gc-backend's 7902405 on the i.MX8MP: 63 fixed on every back end, the poisoning gone, loops 344/344

The pairs were built from `790240503e7a`, which contains b9cef32 (one element per matrix
column) and bff16d7 (the fetch guard). gcgpu `f110fd13eebc`, serial runs, a canary before
each group, 0 recoveries.

| item | result |
|---|---|
| 63 matattr, online / remote / offline | **PASS / PASS / PASS** |
| remote 63, then online 69 and 1, **close_reset=0**, no reload | PASS / PASS (0 idle resets since the load) |
| offline 63, then online 69 and 1, close_reset=0 | PASS / PASS |
| 78 matvary, 79 idiv, 81 branchquad (online; 81 remote too) | PASS |
| 77 transc | online **FAIL**: (32,32) = 0x8040ff50, want 0x80408080; vtransc 0x80000050, want 0x8000ff80 (reproduced). **Remote (etna_shc) PASSES**: 0x80407f80 and 0x8000ff80. Offline has no table entry for it. So the reference form works on this core, and the online program differs from it |

## gl_test 82 / 83 / 85 and the native-cube probe re-run at `63b50b3` (2026-09-23, am62p-board)

Pair `es2-63b50b3`: the conformance configuration (remote shader compiler,
reports ES 2), built from `63b50b370723`. On the board: libGLESv2
`6e3c102dc9d0…`, gl_test_user `f32a9e9e4651…`, cube_probe `e23f2177a7dc…`,
each checked against the host. Module `9c0f78ac81f1` from sysfs. The
PowerVR driver sources differ from it only by 63b50b3's `<stdbool.h>`
include. Parameters from sysfs: carveout_mb=64 combined_kick=Y do_boot=1
fl_init_pages=0 hwrt_cleanup=N hwrt_refuse=N hwrt_reinit=N mmu_ack=Y
mmu_gate=Y pool_rollback=N wait_repost=N wait_rering=N. Shader server
rebuilt at `63b50b370723` (its banner says so), pco_shc from build-new.
`dmesg -w` was captured for the whole session: 0 fence timeouts, 0 HWR
and no fault. The 15 lines matching BIF/fault are boot messages and the
module's load-time register dump, all of which read zero.

**82 `fragcentre`**: both predictions held.

| target | GL (0,0) | GL (63,0) | GL (0,63) | GL (40,20) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FBO | 00,00,60 | fc,00,60 | 00,fc,60 | a0,50,60 | exact: G = 4y, B = 96 |
| default framebuffer | 00,fc,60 | fc,fc,60 | 00,00,60 | a0,ac,60 | G = 4 (63 - y): y mirrored, x right |

(R,G,B hex.) B = 0x60 = 96 in BOTH targets: the pixel centre carries the
+0.5 on the remote pair, so the record's y transform needs only the flip
(scale -1, offset height) and not a half-pixel term. On the default
framebuffer only y is wrong, which matches gc-backend's case 84 on the
i.MX8MP.

**83 `pointcoord`**: FAIL, and the predicted signature did NOT hold.
Every sprite pixel reads (R,G,B) = (ff,ff,00), i.e. s = t = 1.0: at GL
(24,39), (39,39), (24,24) and (39,24) alike, where the expected values are
08/f7 ramps. The pixel outside the sprite reads black, as it should. So the
point is rasterised at size 16 and the shader runs. It does not read the
vertex colour (0x40, 0xbf), which was the prediction, and it does not read
a ramp. Whatever reaches gl_PointCoord is constant, and at or above 1.0 in
both lanes. Not diagnosed yet; the raw readback went to usc-backend.

**85 `cubetail`**: **12 of 12**, exact, on the post-fde0086 arm, as
predicted. The PBE writes only the pixel inside the 1x1 clip, so fde0086
does not corrupt render-to-cube-level. The `76722f6` arm was not run: it
needs this gl_test against that library.

**Native-cube probe, re-run with faces on 4 KiB boundaries (7b3446a)**:
both predictions held.

| part | prediction | measured |
|---|---|---|
| A emul | 0 wrong | 0 of 3072 wrong |
| A native | **0 of 3072 wrong** | **0 of 3072 wrong** (it was 2560 at bfff969) |
| S emul | seam quads read level 3 | `x0 x0 x3 Z3 Z1 Z1 Z3 X3` in every row, unchanged |
| S native | faces -X / +Z / +X across the row, no level 3 | rows 0-1 `x0 x0 x2 Z2 Z1 Z1 Z1 X1`, rows 2-7 `x0 x0 x1 Z1 Z1 Z1 Z1 X1`: no level 3 anywhere |
| B PBE TWIDDLE_2D | 256 twiddled | 256 twiddled (the 4 "linear" are the texels where both orders coincide), unchanged |

So the TPU's native cube sampling with twiddled faces on 4 KiB boundaries
reads every face and level right, and it does not show the emulated path's
level-3 seam. The seam quads read level 2 in the top two rows and level 1
below; in the emulated path they read level 3 in every row. The probe prints

## gc_gl_test on Zephyr at dbad4da, and the SNVS result channel (2026-09-23, i.MX8MP)

**Zephyr, not the Linux path.** imx8mp-board ran the Zephyr `gc_gl_test` image (offline 450
table, `verdin_imx8mp/mimx8ml8/a53`) from dbad4da. With no console, each result was decoded
from the time the board took to come back (`code = (t - 174) / 6`, rounded; the step is 6 s
and the jitter is about 1 s):

| run | return | reading |
|---|---|---|
| regression set (case 7) | kernel back 366 s after the jump | **32 of 38 cases pass** |
| case 9 stencil | 233 s | FAIL, check 9 |
| case 16 msaa | 216 s | FAIL, check 6 |
| case 20 | 180 s | **PASS** |
| case 42 | 209 s | FAIL, check 5 |
| case 44 | 192 s | FAIL, check 2 |
| case 45 | 185 s | FAIL, check 1 |
| case 61 | 209 s | FAIL, check 5 |

Case 20 passes on Zephyr but fails in the Linux harness (offline450 fails 9 16 20 42 44 45 61).
That difference is not explained yet. These are pass/fail results and failing-check numbers
only: the return time carries no got/want values, and **no picture of the i.MX8MP panel was
taken** (the camera sees only the AM62P).

**Where results can survive the reset.** The reset clears DDR: the M7 page 0x81006000 read
zero, and the no-map DDR at 0xC0000000 came back with decayed bits. ATF and U-Boot overwrite
OCRAM. The SNVS LPGPR (0x30370090..0x9C, 16 bytes) are the exception. Nothing in the boot
chain uses them: U-Boot 2024.07 (Toradex 7.7.0, exactly tag v2024.07) touches only SNVS LPLVDR
and LPSR, and its boot counter is in the environment (`BOOTCOUNT_ENV`). NXP TF-A
lf-6.6.52-2.2.1 touches only HPCOMR and LPCR on the imx8mp. The board runs no OP-TEE. Linux
binds `snvs_lpgpr`, and no DT consumer references it. Test (Linux path, not yet on Zephyr):
16 bytes were written through `/sys/bus/nvmem/devices/30370000.snvs:snvs-lpgpr0/nvmem`, read
back identical, and read back identical again after `systemctl reboot`, which is the same PSCI
SYSTEM_RESET that `gc_sample_finish()` makes. The old note in `gc_panel_console.h` that the
LPGPR "ignore writes" was wrong and is corrected. 0x68 aliases LPGPR0 and is not used.

`gc_common/gc_result.{c,h}` (`CONFIG_GC_COMMON_RESULT_SNVS`, default y) now leaves a
four-word record there: `w0 = 0x594B0000 | kind << 8 | seq`, written last. `gc_gl_test` stores
case, first bad check, got and want. `gc_slint` stores stage, frames and the route-3 attach
result. The fatal handler stores ESR, ELR and FAR. The reader zeroes the nvmem file before
each jump.

## Parity gap: three RGBA16F colour attachments on the AM62P (userpasses)

Not measured on silicon; arithmetic from the formats in Qt's source and the
AM62P's pixel-output file (four dwords per pixel), recorded so it is not
forgotten.

Qt Quick 3D's `userpasses` example (`examples/quick3d/userpasses/
GBufferPass.qml`, one of the demos harvested on the AM62P) writes a G-buffer
of three `RenderPassTexture.RGBA16F` attachments (GBUFFER0..2,
`tools/shaders/qt3d/0b4df72d7cd2d1fd.frag`): 3 x 2 = 6 dwords per pixel,
over the AM62P's 4 pixel-output registers. The i.MX8MP (GC7000) renders it;
the AM62P cannot without tile buffers (USC and driver). A named parity gap,
scheduled after the built-in ES 3.00 paths.

Built-in Quick 3D run-time rendering is not affected: its only multiple-
output shaders are the particles' weighted-blended OIT (`qtparticleshaders_*`,
fragOutput + revealageOutput), an RGBA16F accumulation and an R16F revealage
(`qssgrenderpass.cpp` 1473-1477): 2 + 1 = 3 dwords, which fits if the pack
puts R16F in one dword -- to be confirmed against pco when implemented.
Lightmap baking (`lightmapuvraster_300.frag`, four outputs) is offline
tooling and was not assessed.

The difference, found on the host and fixed in dbad4da (7c04ee4): the online `mul` that
scales sin/cos's argument read the uniform and the 1/pi literal, two DIFFERENT constant
registers in one instruction. This core cannot do that (etnaviv refuses it unless
SH_NO_ONECONST_LIMIT, which this core lacks; the reference emits it 0 times in 13,908);
the hardware used one register for both, which predicts all three wrong values. On
dbad4da (imx8mp-board; **Linux path, not yet on Zephyr**) 77 PASSES online, identical to
remote; 84 confirms gl_FragCoord.y mirrored on the default framebuffer on online and
remote; 86 passes; FemtoVG 27-38 and m4 unchanged. None of it counts as fixed on the
product until it has run on Zephyr (gc_gl_test).

## `uniform_api.random.23`: refused by name, an implementation limit, fix planned (2026-09-23)

`dEQP-GLES2.functional.uniform_api.random.23`'s fragment shader (10.9 KB: about a hundred
inlined compare_mat4/mat2/vec4/ivec4/bool calls over a nested uniform struct) is refused
by the online compiler as `Alloc(OutOfRegisters(5785))`. Its 5,785 values are straight-line
and short-lived, so register PRESSURE is small; what overflows is the value NUMBERING:
`MAX_VREGS` = 512 sizes 19 per-value arrays in `vivante/alloc.rs` by value number, not by
liveness. It is a clean refusal, not an abort (522f572).

Growing the constant is not the fix: at 8192 the interval table alone is 256 KiB of stack
(32 B x 8192) before the other 18 arrays -- untenable in the no_std, heap-free build --
and the program then stops on the compiler scratch buffer instead.

Planned (gc-backend, after the gl_FragCoord option-(c) study): allocate without tables
sized by value number -- dense renumbering of dead value numbers as selection streams, or
per-value tables in the lent scratch arena sized by the actual count. Targets: random.23,
and a synthetic 20,000-value straight-line program; no-regression check: the corpus's
register and instruction totals.

**Done on the host, 2026-09-23 (gc-backend, 9ec898d, dcd56b1, 9c147fb; not on silicon).** The
per-value tables of `allocate()` and of the product passes come from the scratch arena,
sized by the program; `MAX_VREGS` is 65,472 (the u16 value-number limit); the six
values x instructions loops in `allocate()` are linear. A 20,000-value straight-line
program allocates in 2 temps, 23 ms and 1.9 MiB of scratch, and the host differential
agrees with the IR evaluator at 6,000 and 20,000 values (chain x_k = x_{k-1} - x_{k-2}; an
averaging chain hid an allocator mutation, this one does not). No-regression, stronger
than totals: all 172 compiled corpus programs byte-identical by SHA-256 (5,835
instructions, 902 temps both sides; the probe's control moves 61), and all 20 allocator
statistics identical per source.

**random.23 itself, measured on the host (tools/cts/host-deqp-run.sh at fe2dbcd, HOST-ONLY):**
refused "compiler scratch buffer exhausted" -- the allocator no longer refuses it. On a
large arena its fragment shader (read out of the .qpa) takes the front end 2,290,756 bytes
for 5,212 IR instructions, selection 1,154,348 more (2,907 instructions), the allocator
468,920, and allocates in 7 temps. The front end alone is past store::SCRATCH_BYTES (2 MiB),
which stays where it is for now (team-lead): the stages shrink first. Pinned by name in
tests/deqp_repro_shaders.rs.

## gl_FragCoord option (c) on the GC7000: the flip study, predictions written before any run (2026-09-23, gc-backend)

Option (c) renders the default framebuffer bottom-up and flips at present, which would
make gl_FragCoord.y, dFdy and point sprites GL's for every back end, the offline table
included (gl_test 84 showed y mirrored on the default framebuffer on online AND remote).
Whether it is affordable on the GC7000 is what this measures. Evidence already in hand:

- the window surface is a scan-out buffer the application hands in, and the PE renders
  straight into it; the resolve engine (RS) runs only for MSAA, which is off, so no copy
  exists at present to carry a flip;
- this core has the RS, not the BLT engine (hwdb minor_features5 0x3b5ac333 lacks
  BLT_ENGINE 0x80000000); the RS has VIVS_RS_CONFIG_FLIP 0x40000000 (etnaviv
  state_3d.xml.h:1378), wired in etnaviv_rs.c:102 and never set by etnaviv;
- the display cannot flip: NXP's BSP imx-lcdifv3 (lf-6.18.y, read, cited) creates no
  rotation property, has no flip or mirror control, and CTRLDESCL0_3_PITCH is an unsigned
  16-bit field (lcdifv3-regs.h:116); mainline's lcdif agrees (lcdif_regs.h:198).

These are **Linux-path** measurements (gl_test_user over /dev/gcgpu); the decision they
inform is the Zephyr product's, and a chosen option is re-measured there before it counts.

Two arms, both OFF unless `GL_TEST_GC_FLIP_EXPERIMENT` is set for gl_test_user
(`gc_debug_set_flip_experiment`, vivante/backend.rs; not exported by libGLESv2.so, no
ABI change). Recovery on for every run.

**Arm (i), `GL_TEST_GC_FLIP_EXPERIMENT=1`: the default framebuffer drawn bottom-up, from
its last row with a negative PE_COLOR_STRIDE,** the viewport, scissor, clear clip, cull and
front face treated as an FBO's. Run 84, 1-20 and FemtoVG 27-38 under it.
- Works: 84 PASSES on the default framebuffer too (rows 4 / 59 green 237 / 18); 1-20 and
  27-38 as without the switch; a panel scene upright.
- Stride ignored (the field masked or unsigned): writes run past the buffer's end from its
  last row -- an MMU fault and a recovery, or a picture only in the last row(s), the rest
  the clear or garbage.
- Stride applied per block but not per row (the PE writes 4x4 or larger blocks): the
  picture upright in blocks but reversed within them -- 84 reads green shifted by up to
  three rows (about +/-12 of 237), and edges comb.
- Depth, stencil and the clear are NOT expected to break: depth and stencil live in their
  own buffer, which only the PE touches, in raster coordinates it keeps consistent, and
  the clear is a quad through the same path. glReadPixels reads the same memory image as
  today (upright, top-down), so its row order does not change.

**Arm (ii), gl_test 88 rsflip: 100 RS_CONFIG_FLIP copies of a 1280x800 frame (the
panel's size, rvt101hvdwc00b), then one plain copy back, timed against the same frame
without them.**
- Works: "rows reversed: RS_CONFIG_FLIP flips", and a cost of about 1-2 ms per copy
  (8 MB of traffic per 1280x800x4 copy, bandwidth-bound). That is (c)'s price per frame,
  plus one 4 MB buffer.
- Bit ignored: "rows as drawn", the case fails, and the cost is a plain copy's.
- The RS refuses the shape or hangs: a fence timeout and a recovery (hang_ms=5000).

**Reachable: 114 of the 148** (frontend3, 2026-09-23, a source survey -- HOST-ONLY). 32 of the
list are Qt's multiview variants (`#extension GL_OVR_multiview2 : require`, `layout(num_views = 2)
in;`), which Qt builds only for XR rendering; this driver does not advertise the extension and XR is
out of scope, so they are not targets. 2 more (`0119aeb276db508c.frag`, `0e5620f16999a984.frag`) declare
`#version 100` and then use `sampler2DArray`, which ES 1.00 does not have; Qt takes the `300 es`
variant on an ES 3 context, so they are not reachable either. What the 114 use from ES 3.00: array
constructors (`vec2[](`, 37; `vec3[](`, 21), `texture` 63, `textureLod` 64, `sampler2DArray` 49,
`samplerCube` 25, `sampler3D` 1, `textureSize` 2, `inverse` 17, `transpose` 16. None uses a
non-square matrix, `switch`, a shadow sampler, `texelFetch` or an offset. Progress through the
front end (compile only, the back ends and the board are separate questions) is recorded per step in
docs/online-shaderc/frontend.md, "GLSL ES 3.00".

**Open: a uniform array of structs is laid out differently from pco's record on PowerVR** (frontend3,
2026-09-23, HOST-ONLY, from `tests/online_reflection.rs`'s pvr_layers test population). The offline
table (glsl2usc + pco) lays such an array out **member by member**: one row per member, named after
element `[0]`, and that row covers the member for every element. Each element of a vec3 member takes 4
dwords. The online front end lays it out **element by element** (AoS, vec3 packed to 3 dwords), with one
row per element and member. In `0259850a5e89b258.frag` (`directionalLights[4]`), the table has
`directionalLights[0].direction @128 x16` and `.shadowBias @144 x4`. The online front end has
`[0].direction @128` and `[0].shadowBias @131`, and gives every later member of the array a different
offset. The table has 61 rows and the online front end 457.

Scope: 49 Qt Quick 3D fragment sources in that test's population differ in their full offsets. An
earlier report of "21+" undercounted. Every uniform block member declared after the struct array moves
with it. The test therefore compares only the order of top-level declarations for these sources.

This does not make a compile wrong on its own. The online path writes the uniforms through its own
rows, and those rows agree with its own addressing. It does break table-vs-online record parity
on PowerVR, which a mixed program (one stage from the table, one online) or any comparison against
pco's record needs.

Proposed owner: frontend3. The fix matches glsl2usc's flattening in `reflect` (rows and offsets) and
in `lower` (the address of `s[i].m` becomes the member's base plus `i` times its per-element stride).
It applies to the PowerVR target only, the way the `pvr_layers_` member does. It is pinned by
extending that test to compare full offsets.

## i.MX8MP on Zephyr, 2026-09-23 afternoon: parity, online cases, and the normal kexec route

**Zephyr, i.MX8MP, results read back from the SNVS record** (`gc_common/gc_result.h`). No
picture of the i.MX8MP panel was taken in any of these runs.

| image (origin/main) | route | record | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| gc_gl_triangle `prj_parity.conf` 1024x600 (f8f6c93) | crash | `594b0401 ff403f80 35706c4e 04000258` | PASS. Column CRC **0x35706c4e = the AM62P's** (y = 25i, i = 3..21): the 19 centre-column samples are bit-identical across the GC7000UL and the BXS. The centre pixel (512,300 GL) is 803f40, which the AM62P's own column also has at y = 300; the AM62P's "centre 4b5a5a" was taken at a different point |
| gc_gl_test online, ES 1.00 set, case 90 churn (6b51e24) | crash | `594b010e 005aff01 00000002 0` | PASS, 2 checks |
| same, case 76 boolany | crash | `594b010e 004cff01 00000008 0` | PASS, 8 checks |
| same, case 80 matdyn | crash | `594b010e 0050ff01 00000004 0` | PASS, 4 checks |

These are the online compiler's first runs on Zephyr on this board. They used a 256 KiB main
stack, because am62p-board found the online compiler overflows 64 KiB. This arm64 target offers
no `HW_STACK_PROTECTION`, so `CONFIG_STACK_SENTINEL` is the only guard. It detects an overflow
only at a context switch, so a fault caused by an overflow can still land late (for example in the
idle thread).

**OPEN LAB ISSUE, low priority: the normal kexec route dies before PRE_KERNEL_1.** The same
gc_gl_triangle parity image that passes on the crash route came back 135 s after a normal-route
jump with the SNVS record all zero. Even the breadcrumb that `gc_result.c` writes at
PRE_KERNEL_1 was missing, and the watchdog was not fed (a PASS would have held 60 s). gc_slint
route 3 did the same twice (f8f6c93 and 6b51e24). This explains the constant 131-135 s returns
of 2026-09-22 and today: those runs said nothing about gc_slint. gc_slint (~95 MiB) needs the
normal route only because it does not fit `crashkernel=64M`. `kexec_run.sh` now refuses a
crash-route image larger than `/sys/kernel/kexec_crash_size` before it touches the board. The
first attempt had unloaded galcore before the loader failed with `kexec_load: error 0x63`.

**Board configuration: planned, NOT applied** (the session's permission checker refused the
privileged writes; they need the user). Read-only evidence is in `build/imx8mp/board-config/` of
the imx8mp2 worktree.

| what | now | change | rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| crash window | `tdxargs=crashkernel=64M@0x60000000 clk-imx8mp.mcore_booted=1` | `fw_setenv tdxargs 'crashkernel=256M@0x60000000 clk-imx8mp.mcore_booted=1'`, reboot | the same with `64M`, reboot |
| M7 SafeUI autostart | `safeui-route3.service` enabled (Linux remoteproc via `/home/torizon/safeui/route3_boot.sh`; no U-Boot bootaux) | `systemctl disable safeui-route3.service` | `systemctl enable safeui-route3.service`, reboot |
| product containers | `docker-compose.service` enabled (sarta); galcore loaded | `systemctl disable --now docker-compose.service`, `rmmod galcore` | `systemctl enable --now docker-compose.service` |

The 256 MiB window at 0x60000000 is wholly inside System RAM 0x55500000-0x7fffffff. It is clear
of the Zephyr GPU carveout 0x58000000-0x5bffffff, the M7 region 0x80000000-0x83ffffff,
`linux,cma` 0xa0000000-0xbfffffff, the rpmsg reservations 0x55000000-0x554fffff and the mailbox
at 0xc0000000. It equals Zephyr's DT sram (0x60000000 + 256 MiB). Greenboot has no required or
wanted checks on this board, so disabling docker-compose cannot trigger a greenboot rollback.

## GC7000 4x MSAA via the resolve engine: predictions before any run (2026-09-23, gc-backend)

The lead's decision: implement 4x MSAA on the GC7000 (parity with the AM62P, which passes
gl_test 16 on Zephyr; Quick 3D's SceneEnvironment antialiasing). The first attempt "never
wrote the target"; against etnaviv (Mesa, MIT) it differed in four ways, and each is now
carried by `gc_debug_msaa` (vivante/backend.rs), OFF by default until measured:

1. the multisampled scratch surface is SUPERTILED, twice the target on each axis padded to
   64x64 (etnaviv_resource.c: an "MSAA render target" is laid out super-tiled); it was
   linear and unpadded;
2. PE_COLOR_FORMAT carries SUPER_TILED and, on this CACHE128B256BPERLINE core,
   SUPER_TILED_NEW, and never OVERWRITE on a multisampled target (etnaviv_state.c);
3. the resolve reads a tiled source: RS_CONFIG_SOURCE_TILED, RS_SOURCE_STRIDE = pitch << 2 |
   TILING | SUPER_TILED_NEW, TS mode 0 (no tile status) (etnaviv_rs.c);
4. RS_WINDOW_SIZE is in source samples, 2w x 2h (etna_try_rs_blit); it was w x h.

This core has MSAA, SUPER_TILED, SINGLE_BUFFER, SMALL_MSAA, CACHE128B256BPERLINE and
RSBLT_MSAA_DECOMPRESSION (hwdb, GC7000 rev 0x6204). The switch also brings the EGL 4x config
back (gl/egl.rs `offered_configs`; without it the GC7000 build offers none, 8d0f4b9). A
target whose width is not a multiple of 16 or height not of 4 stays single-sampled, so the
resolve window never reaches past the target.

**Run (Linux path first, then Zephyr as the deciding check):** `GL_TEST_GC_MSAA=1` for
gl_test_user (prints "gc_debug_msaa=1"; case 16 then runs instead of its Vivante skip):
case 16, then 1-20 and FemtoVG 27-38 as the no-change check, recovery on.
- Works: 16 PASSES (the edge pixels averaged as the AM62P's are); 1-20 and 27-38 unchanged
  (no other case asks for samples > 1).
- The resolve still writes nothing: 16 reads the target's previous contents (the clear
  colour or black) where the triangle is -- the old symptom, so one of 1-4 is not enough.
- Supertiling wrong in the PE or the RS: a picture scrambled in 64x64 blocks, or in 4x4 tiles.
- A window or stride mismatch: the triangle at half or double scale, or only the target's
  top-left quarter written.
- A fault or a fence timeout: send the dmesg; the next suspects are tile status (this build
  runs none) and RS_EXTRA_CONFIG.

## gl_slint on Zephyr (AM62P) against a host reference render of the same cluster.slint (2026-09-23, am62p-board)

The board run (Zephyr, AM62P, gl_slint from 63b50b3, table path, 58 fps,
3533 frames in 60 s, GL error 0) printed the first frame at five points whose
expected colours are written into the sample. The expectation is not the
reference; a render of the same UI on the host is. `slint-viewer` 1.17.0
(the board's crate is the patched no_std 1.18) rendered
driver/samples/zephyr/slint/ui/cluster.slint at 1024x600 with the SafeUI
layout from safeui-eb1a48e (`--screenshot`, software renderer; sha256
of the PNG `6c4aabc7...` is in the worktree's build/slint-ref/).

| point | board (Zephyr) | host render | sample's expectation | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bg-top-left (40,20) | 11,16,23 | (gradient not drawn, see below) | 11,16,24 | analytic gradient 10.76,15.66,23.52: board within rounding |
| face-left (214,330) | 9,12,18 | 8,11,17 | 8,11,17 | board +1 LSB |
| face-right (810,330) | 8,11,17 | 8,11,17 | 8,11,17 | exact |
| bg-bottom (300,590) | 4,6,10 | (gradient not drawn) | 4,6,10 | analytic 4.11,6.16,10.22: board within rounding |
| track (47,330) | 13,17,24 | 12,16,23 | **20,26,34** | board +1 LSB; the EXPECTATION is wrong |

So the AM62P draws all five within one LSB of the reference, and the "track"
discrepancy was the sample's own expectation string, not the GPU. The host's
software renderer (headless and winit alike) draws the Window's
`@linear-gradient(180deg, bg-top, bg-bottom)` as the flat top colour in a
snapshot (the whole left column reads 11,16,24), and the FemtoVG/Skia
backends of that viewer cannot snapshot; the two background points are
therefore judged against the gradient computed from safeui-layout.slint's
own #0b1018 -> #04060a at pixel centre y + 0.5. The shared kind-6 record's
CRC over the board's 15 bytes is 0x06139687, as imx8mp2 computed.

514 frames in the ~50 s loop is about 10 fps at 1280x800, against 58 fps for the AM62P's gl_slint
at 1024x600.** No picture of the i.MX8MP panel was taken.

The parity build now probes the canonical state, `demo_vehicle(t=0)` with no wait (the AM62P's
state; its 1024x600 host reference matched the AM62P within 1 LSB). The PROBES record carries
the five points as RGB565 plus a CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over their 15 RGB888 bytes (layout in
`gc_result.h`). With the AM62P's values, the record is `594b0601 08620882 00210842 030f0883`.

### The cold display path, judged by eye (2026-09-23, the user at the Verdin panel)

The SNVS record cannot see the panel, so the user watched two runs of gc_slint 1280x800 (image from
38a9f617, crash route):

| run | record | what the user saw |
|---|---|---|
| FORCE_COLD (the whole chain torn down and brought up) | PASS, 538 frames | "the Slint picture appears and its layout is recognisable, but the drawing is disturbed and flickers over the whole screen, as if it were not in sync" |
| adopt (Linux's running chain kept) | PASS, 514 frames | "the Slint screen is perfect" |

The record's PASS was blind to the defect. Linux's live registers, read with mmio_rd, showed the
cause. The LCDIF and the DSIM configuration matched. The clock plan did not. Linux runs a
69.3 MHz pixel clock (VIDEO_PLL1 1039.5 MHz / 15) and a 426.6 MHz DSI burst clock, from a 12 MHz
DSIM reference with PLL p 5, m 711, s 2: 2.6 % above the video stream. The cold path ran
1000 / 14 = 71.43 MHz and asked the DSI for exactly pixel * 24 / 4 = 428.6 MHz. That leaves burst
mode no room for packet overhead, and the SN65DSI84's line buffer runs dry. The fix programs
Linux's plan: VIDEO_PLL1 as a pixel-clock parent (`video-pll1-frequency`), a fixed
`burst-clock-frequency`, and the 12 MHz reference. It also widens the DSIM PLL's input window to
the 2..30 MHz that Linux's p 5 proves the part accepts. The fixed image needs the same viewing.

**To re-verify at the end: route 3.** The final target is the composed setup again: the M7
SafeUI plus the A53's Slint or Qt through the frame ring. The ring build keeps building. It links
no display code at all (`CONFIG_SAFEUI_DISPLAY_IMX8MP=n`), so the clock-plan fix cannot touch
the display the M7 owns in that arrangement. Route 3 has never been seen working on this board:
every earlier route-3 reading was a normal-route failure. Its re-verification on the crash
route, with the M7 re-enabled, is an open item.

**Zephyr, Verdin i.MX8MP, crash route**, with the images from origin/main e9d41252.

- **gc_slint 1280x800 FORCE_COLD with Linux's clock plan.** Record `594b021b 00ff0d01 00000224
  0000003f`: PASS, 548 frames, display health 0x3f (all six: LCDIF running, DSIM PLL stable, DSIM
  HS clock, bridge answers, bridge PLL locked, backlight). The user watched: *"it looks quite
  good; the appearance is right. But some frames update quickly and some take longer.
  Performance needs improving."* So the cold bring-up now draws correctly. The uneven frame

- **gc_slint parity, the AM62P's state** (`demo_vehicle(t = 0)`, no ease wait). Record

(23:16) and max (31:24) in ms, each clamped at 255. The render log prints the same as
`pacing: frame min/median/max, eglSwapBuffers min/median/max`.

## Bevy on the boards: studied, dropped (2026-09-24, the user's decision)

A host-only study, reading Bevy 0.19.1 and wgpu 29.0.4 from the crate sources. Bevy's logic
crates are `#![no_std]` with std as a default feature (platform, utils, tasks, reflect, ecs, app,
math, transform, asset, window). Everything that draws needs std: render, core_pipeline, pbr,
image, mesh, shader, camera, winit. wgpu, wgpu-core, wgpu-types, wgpu-hal and naga are no_std
crates. wgpu-hal's `gles` backend is std in practice: glow 0.17, khronos-egl through dlopen,
parking_lot. It needs OpenGL ES 3.0 or newer, and naga emits GLSL ES 3.00. Zephyr's Rust has no
std, so Bevy's rendering cannot run there without porting a std or patching Bevy's render crates
to no_std (roughly ten times the Slint patch). The user dropped Bevy. What the study found still
matters for Qt and dEQP-GLES3: wgpu, like Qt Quick 3D, needs the whole ES 3.0 core through
eglGetProcAddress (VAOs, UBOs with std140 blocks, sampler objects, TexStorage, TexImage3D,
MapBufferRange, BlitFramebuffer, InvalidateFramebuffer, DrawBuffers, ClearBuffer*,
CopyBufferSubData, fences, queries, VertexAttribIPointer, integer formats).

## ES 3.0 conformance gaps: where the reported limits are below ES 3.0's minimums (2026-09-24, gc-backend)

The decision (team-lead, for the user's "ES3 on both"): keep reporting OpenGL ES 3.0 --
flipping to ES 2.0 would move Qt Quick 3D onto its reduced path and regress pictures
already verified on the AM62P -- and report every limit honestly, as min(what the GPU
carries, what this driver programs). A limit below the minimum is then a true dEQP-GLES3
failure and a row of this list, which is the ES3 work list; its order comes later, by what
Qt and dEQP hit first. `report-es2` stays the existing opt-in.

The minimums are read from the OpenGL ES 3.0.6 specification's Tables 6.28-6.34 (text
extracted from the Khronos PDF), not recalled. "GC7000 hw" is the hwdb row for 0x6204 and
Mesa etnaviv's screen limits.

| limit | ES 3.0 min | reported: GC7000 | reported: PowerVR | GC7000 hw | what closes it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS | 4 | 1 | 3 | 4 RTs (etnaviv num_rts, 8 halved) | GC7000: multiple render targets (ES3 step 3); both: a fourth |
| MAX_COLOR_ATTACHMENTS | 4 | 3 | 3 | -- | a fourth attachment point in the GL core |
| MAX_VARYING_VECTORS | 15 | 15 | 8 | 16 | PowerVR: the USC's limit (usc-backend) |
| MAX_VARYING_COMPONENTS | 60 | 60 | 32 | 64 | as above |
| MAX_FRAGMENT_INPUT_COMPONENTS | 60 | 60 | 32 | 64 | as above |
| MAX_VERTEX_OUTPUT_COMPONENTS | 64 | 60 | 32 | 64 (16 varyings + position, 32 VS outputs on HALTI5) | GC7000: a 17th vertex io row (the ShcViv reshape) |
| MAX_UNIFORM_BLOCK_SIZE | 16384 bytes | 6144 | 6144 | -- | uniform blocks are flattened into the default block (team-lead's decision, frontend3), which holds MAX_UNIFORM_DWORDS = 1536 dwords (6144 bytes) a stage, shared with the default uniforms; real descriptor UBOs per GPU later |
| MAX_COMBINED_VERTEX/FRAGMENT_UNIFORM_COMPONENTS | 1536 + 12 x 16384 / 4 = 50688 (the formula) | 1536 | 1536 | -- | the blocks share each stage's default block, so the honest sum is its 1536 dwords; closes with descriptor UBOs |
| MAX_COMBINED_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS | 32 | 16 | 16 | 16 VS + 16 PS samplers | 32 texture units in the GL core |
| MAX_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_* | 64 / 4 / 4 | 0 | 0 | -- | transform feedback, both GPUs |
| MAX_SAMPLES | 4 | 1 | 1 | 4x | multisampled renderbuffers (the GC7000's 4x EGL path is measured separately and not yet working) |

Pinned per GPU by `gl::state::tests::the_es3_limits_are_what_this_gpu_carries_and_programs`;
raising a value moves that pin and this row together. Changed with this list: the GC7000's
varying limits 8 → 15 vectors (the driver programs all of them since 6719382, which fixed a
panic on the ninth vec4 varying) and its draw buffers 3 → 1 (the backend writes one colour
output; outputs 1 and 2 used to go nowhere). Not yet on silicon: a board case with fifteen
varyings is requested.

**The cascade found: cases 17 and 18 release the harness context (af9a82cb, case lists by
selector 0x200+k, counters record).** Every run below: lost GPU work 0, resets 0, fence
timeouts 0, no case left a GL error unchecked; so lost or recovered GPU work is ruled out.

gc-backend's reading from the code, confirmed on the host and by the table: 17 (ctx2) and 18
(image) destroy the harness's bring-up context, and the list walker re-binds only while it
exists, so every later case runs with no current context. 21 releases it too and makes its own
context, which is why 21 passes and everything after it fails in the [16, 19-...] row. 16, my
suspect, is innocent (predicted 65-70% guilty: wrong). The fix (the walker re-creates the harness

## The owed i.MX8MP runs on the build host (2026-09-25, imx8mp, 4f40f622 / 11ae57ff)

First runs of the the build host session. Every image is built from origin/main 4f40f622 (e4fbaed6 and 5b9ba9c9 are
ancestors). SafeUI is eb1a48e plus tools/cts/imx8mp-safeui-gc_board.patch (eb1a48e alone does not link, see
HANDOVER). ES 2.0 reporting for dEQP, masked clear on by default. Each jump cleared the SNVS record first and came
back with a fresh Linux uptime; logs are build/imx8mp/out/jump-<label>.log in the imx8mp-cts worktree.
Predictions were written before each run (build/imx8mp/predictions-runs123.txt there).

**The dEQP image from main panicked before its first case.** Image runs123-4f40f622 (sha256 d62ca925), SEL=0:
kind 3 fault record, 0 cases begun, ELR 0x60525d1c = the k_panic() of k_mem_map_phys_bare (zephyr kernel/mmu.c:979,
"memory mapping ... failed"). Mechanism: 2ea05a0a (in e4fbaed6) raised the C heap to 160 MiB, the image's RAM
footprint became 0xc86b000 (200 MiB, the loader's "segment" line), and the kernel VM is 256 MiB from 0x60000000.
Zephyr's help for KERNEL_VM_SIZE (kernel/Kconfig.vm; the docs page
https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/kernel/memory_management/virtual_memory.html says the same) puts the
kernel image in that region and runtime mappings (driver MMIO, RAM mappings) in what is left: about 56 MiB,
and gc_render.c:83 maps the whole 64 MiB carveout. The AM62P conf set 512 MiB for the same failure at 1eda74e5.
Fix: CONFIG_KERNEL_VM_SIZE=0x20000000 in the i.MX8MP deqp board conf (f30def20). e4fbaed6 had never been booted.

The runs below are on the fragment arm with that setting (image runs123-vm512-4f40f622, sha256 98171f0b; its
.config is identical to f30def20's and the zephyr.bin differs only in the 6-byte build string).

| run | prediction | measured | reading |
|---|---|---|---|

| 2. texture.size (SEL=1) | runs to the end, 74 / 0 | **9 pass, then 2d.2048x2048_l8_mipmap ends the run** (kind 9, 10 begun) | WRONG: the same ender as at e51d057f; the 160 MiB heap did not move it.
