Lost work, resets and fence timeouts were 0 in every chunk. 85 flips inside the chunk on both arms (as in the
255c53e4 chunk) and passes alone: not the change's.

Verdict: exercised, no difference. gc_debug_flat_shade and gc_debug_first_component_use both default to 1, so the
before arm wrote GENERIC for 89's flat varyings and the after arm COLOR, and both drew the last vertex. 79389c5f's
premise ("a flat varying marked GENERIC takes the first vertex") is refuted on silicon. Its reading of Mesa is also
not what Mesa does: etnaviv (Mesa 26.2.1, etnaviv_compiler_nir.c:1451-1471) marks COLOR only the legacy colour
slots VARYING_SLOT_COL0/COL1 and every other varying, flat or not, GENERIC; a flat varying only sets
PA_CONFIG SHADE_MODEL_FLAT (etnaviv_shader.c:260-264). Internet check (user rule of 2026-09-25): Lucas Stach's
2017 patch "etnaviv: fix varying interpolation" (mesa-dev, 2017-09-15,
https://mesa-dev.freedesktop.narkive.com/txKjF6pq/patch-v2-1-2-etnaviv-fix-varying-interpolation) says GC880+
"derive[s] this from the component use" for colour semantics; no source was found on how the component use
treats ES 3.0 flat user varyings, and Mesa's GC7000 CI runs dEQP-GLES2 only (deqp-etnaviv-gc7000-r6204.toml,
version_check "GL ES 2.0"), so no CI result covers them either. The board measurement is the evidence:
gc-flatuse is not needed; the recommendation is not to land it (team-lead decides).

### What the 43 MiB are: held frees, deferred twice (2026-09-25, imx8mp)

Local instrument (build/imx8mp/instrument-held-probe.patch; image heldprobe-2c87c2e4, one jump, SEL=0x2001 on
texture.size): at the first carveout allocation failure the OSAL (src/osal/zephyr_gc.c) held **4 frees = 32 MiB**
(0x8004 KiB) with **submitted - completed = 0**, gc_render's defer queue held **8 MiB** (0x2008 KiB), the tiled copies
**0**. Prediction (written before the run): held >= 16 MiB. So 40 of the 43 MiB live are frees waiting for a kick.

The code says why there is so much: on Zephyr a free is deferred twice. zephyr_gc.c keeps it until the kick that was
being recorded at the free has completed, then calls gc_render_free(), which stamps it again with g->fence_next, the
kick not yet submitted (driver/src/vivante/gc_render.c:311-318), so every block waits one more kick. With nothing
submitted since (dEQP does not flush between cases) the previous case's textures stay held: the 32 MiB wait for the
open kick, the 8 MiB for the one after it. The Linux harness (gc_chardev.c) calls gc_render_free() directly and defers
once. Fixed: the next section (imx8mp, the user's decision of 2026-09-25 16:52).

### The texture.size fix: a free waits only for the last kick that may read it, and only once (2026-09-25, imx8mp)

Correction to the paragraph above: at the failure no frame was open at all (the held probe read submitted - completed =
0, and the next case uploads before it draws). The 32 MiB were not waiting for an open kick: they waited for "the next
submit", and while nothing is recorded the backend submits nothing (vivante/backend.rs frame_submit returns at once when
not recording). **In plain words: a free tagged with "the next submit" waits forever while nothing is recording.** The V3D
had the same defect (v3d_frees.h, T4). The second cause is the one above: after its own fence the OSAL handed the block to
gc_render_free(), which held it one kick more.

The fix (landing commit cc4afda7 on 61e95404; its diff against its parent equals 6c002731's, index lines aside, and
6c002731 is what the images below were built from):
- the GC7000 backend tells the OSAL when it records a frame (OSAL_QUERY_GC_FRAME_OPEN, 9: additive, after the V3D's 7/8);
- src/osal/gc_frees.h (plain C, host-checked by tools/gc/osal_frees_check.c, 25 checks, a check.sh row): a free is held
  for submitted + 1 while a frame is open, else for the last submitted kick, and given back at once when that kick has
  completed; until the backend reports, a frame counts as open (the old rule);
- gc_render_free_retired(): a block whose kick has completed goes straight to the pool; z_gpu_alloc drains first.
No GL-core change. The first attempt, 35d0e717 (a GL-core finish-and-retry plus the retired free, without the query),
did NOT move the board: texture.size still ended at index 9, and a local instrument read 12 retries, 0 successful, 35 MiB
still live after the finish, because the frees were tagged with a submit that never came. A retry counter on the second
attempt (5a0a3860, the query plus the retry) read 0 retries over texture.size (marker 0xc0ffee): the retry was dropped
(not exercised; shared code). The host mock (testutil) already tagged only an open frame, which is why the first
attempt's host test passed while the board did not.

| check (image built from 6c002731 = cc4afda7's code) | prediction | measured |
|---|---|---|
| texture.size (SEL=1, image oomfix-6c002731, no instrument) | 80 / 0, all begun | **80 / 0 / 0 / 0, 80 begun** (kind 8): the 64 cases that never began now pass |
| free counters over texture.size (local instrument, frees stats at run end, tag 0xee) | at once > 0, leaked 0 | **339 freed at once, 0 drained, held high-water 0 KiB, 0 leaked**: every free came with no frame open and its kick done |
| whole tree (wholetree-6c002731, 29 entries, one jump each) | run 6 except texture.size 80 / 0 | **17,212 pass, 20 fail, 120 notsup, 19 other of 17,371 begun**; 28 of 29 records bit-identical to run 6's, the 29th is texture.size (80 / 80). No fault, no missing record |
| gl_test chunk 48..95 (SEL=256), 6c002731 vs bb2a8363 (= 3dddcd29's code) | identical but for 85 | identical: pass bits 07df / fffffc70 on both (85 not passed on both, the known chunk flipper); lost work, resets, timeouts 0 |
| gl_test chunk 96..143 (SEL=256), the same two arms | identical | identical: pass bits 0013 / c7b51af2 on both (pass 97, 100-103, 105, 107, 108, 112, 114, 116, 117, 119-122, 126-129, 132). **Both arms record lost work 1, resets 1, fence timeouts 1**: a GPU recovery present on main before the fix, not caused by it; the 255c53e4 chunk recorded 0 resets, so it is new since then. Quarters 96-107 / 108-119 / 120-131 / 132-143: lost work, resets, timeouts 1/1/1, 0, 0, 0. 96-101: 0; 102-107: 1; 102-104: 1; 105-107: 0. Alone: 104 1/1/1, 102 0, 103 0; 104 as SEL=8 (kind 1): check 1 got 0x00000000, want 0xff000000 (nothing drawn). Why: 104 is an ES 3.00 case whose band 7 loops to a bound of 1e9 and relies on "the 4096 cap (a DELIBERATE deviation)" (gl_test.c); that cap exists only in the PowerVR back end (src/shaderc/online/powervr/unroll.rs, UNIFORM_LOOP_CAP = 4096), so the GC7000's loop runs until the fence times out and the GPU is reset. 104 runs on the GC7000 only since 8463ac2c (2026-09-25 11:15: an ES 3.0-reporting library runs the `300 es` cases; the gc_gl_test image reports ES 3.0); the 255c53e4 chunk skipped the ES 3.00 cases (114 was "skipped, ES 3.00" there), hence its 0 resets. Not a driver regression and not the OOM fix: the GC7000 compiler lacks the structural guarantee that it never emits a non-terminating program |

### The GC7000 loop guard: gl_test 104 fixed (2026-09-25, imx8mp, 1787af61)

The fix (1787af61; 1f41bdf9 gates one test under report-es2, test code only): online/select.rs, the GC7000's own
selection, puts a hidden counter at every loop's head (`mov.f32 cnt, 0` before it; at the head `add.s32 cnt, cnt, 1`,
`cmp.ge.s32 stop, cnt, limit + 1`, `branch.not stop -> body`, `branch -> end`), so every loop ends. `limit` is the head
entry count of a constant `for` loop in the front end's shape (constant init, `i < B` / `i <= B` int or float either
order, one step `i += C`, extra steps only before `continue`), simulated exactly up to 65,536 entries: such a loop stays
exact and its guard never fires. Every other loop gets 4096, the PowerVR's and the V3D's UNIFORM_LOOP_CAP. Team-lead's
decision (B): the shared unroller's output is not used (it rewrites every GC7000 loop); that is a Work-list follow-up.

**A GC7000-only property, not shared:** a constant loop longer than 4096 passes is exact here and cut on the other two
GPUs. Their unroller simulates at most 256 passes, then keeps the loop at count 4096 on its break flag; measured with a
temporary host test on 4189b32a, `for (int i = 0; i < 5000; i++)` gives `Trip { count: 4096, exit: Some(..) }`. The
GC7000's host test `a_constant_loop_of_5000_keeps_its_count_and_is_exact` (5001 entries, eval sums 5000) pins the
difference. Making the other two exact is the (C') proposal for the user (.claude/worktrees/proposal-loop-cap-constant-bounds.md).

**(C') landed (batch 62, origin/main 48db23cd holds f8999f57; the user's decision 2026-09-25 22:02: only after measurement
on all three boards).** The recognizer moved to the shared `online/loop_count.rs`; the PowerVR/V3D unroller asks it when
its 256-pass simulation runs out, so a constant loop of up to `EXACT_PASSES_MAX` = 65,536 passes is exact on all three
GPUs and every other loop gets 4096. The paragraph above ("A GC7000-only property") is history from here on. Board
regression, A/B 5a492d67 vs f8999f57: AM62P (am62p) gl_test regression set 37/38 on both arms, polygon_offset 14/14,
loop cases 70/71/87/98/104 PASS on both, no case moved; Pi 4 (m5) default 12/12 and 104/70/71/87 PASS on both, 98 the
same gl_VertexID refusal on both; i.MX8MP (imx8mp) 104 alone PASS, chunk 48..95 identical, and the five cases that
differed between arms (10, 37, 38 in 0..47; 113, 127 in 96..143) passed and failed on BOTH arms over 3..8 runs per arm
(in-chunk passes 37 1/3 vs 1/3, 38 1/3 vs 2/3, 113 5/8 vs 6/8, 127 7/8 vs 5/8), with the GC7000 programs of every gl_test
shader byte-identical between the arms (705 tools/shaders sources; a 65,536-pass known positive differs); 0 lost work,
resets and fence timeouts in all 24 chunk records. The i.MX8MP evidence: `records/imx8mp/cprime-case-table-final.txt`
(sha256 baa6558e3d3c90d1, 72 lines: every record's path, line 12 and the record line), `record_cf-*.txt`,
`gc7000-digest-*.txt`; the proposal with all three boards' rows: `.claude/worktrees/proposal-loop-cap-constant-bounds.md`
(copy `records/imx8mp/proposal-loop-cap-constant-bounds.md.final`). What this does not show: that the flip rates are
equal (n = 3..8 cannot), and anything gl_test does not cover. The fvgstroke failure (37 alone, 5 of 20 at 7e82d27c) is
on main before and after, and is its own item.

Host: select.rs loop_guard_tests (104's divloop.frag gets 4096 and the guard exits past the back edge; for 5000 gets
5001; 10 iterations get 11 and the guard compares against 12; the recognizer cases); revert check (recognizer off) 3 of 4
fail; tests/encoding_vocabulary.rs caught a first `mov.s32` the reference never emits (now legal_copy's `mov.f32`); full

## Correction: dEQP color_clear on Zephyr, i.MX8MP (2026-09-24, imx8mp2)

**The color_clear failures are the eight colour-masked cases,
as gc-backend predicted, not the unmasked ones.** The per-case bitmap (kind 9, dafa9962) was
right; I read it wrong. I took position i to be the i-th case in the order the group's source
adds them, but dEQP runs a group's cases sorted by name: TestNode::addChild (tcuTestCase.cpp)
inserts each child in name order. Everything below that named cases from that reading is
retracted: "single/multiple/subclears/short_scissored/scissored_rgb fail", "all masked pass",
"the results vary with the image", and the heap/filter reading built on it. The run-to-run
determinism was real; it was the same eight cases every time.

How it was settled (Zephyr, i.MX8MP; ff87fb10 adds a CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE of the first failing
case's full name to the record, taken from the same log lines as its result; same six-filter
table, one image, run-time selector):

| filter | bitmap | name check | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| `single_rgb,masked_rgb` | [Fail, Pass] | `acd1` = masked_rgb | masked_rgb ran first and failed; single_rgb passed (as each does alone) |
| `color_clear.*` (19) | F F F F P P F F F F P P P P P P P P P | `103c` = complex_rgb | in name order: complex x2, long_masked x2 fail; long x2 pass; masked x2, masked_scissored x2 fail; multiple, scissored, short_scissored, single, subclears pass |
| `single_rgb` | Pass | none | |

With the masked clear on (CONFIG_DEQP_GC_MASKED_CLEAR=y, same source): `594b0913 55555595
00000015 4b4c0003`: **18 pass, 1 fail**. The fail is index 3, name check `4b4c` =
**long_masked_rgba** (index 3 in name order agrees). Prediction was 19/19 at 65%.

The record now always carries the first failing case's name check (gc_result.h, kinds 8 and 9),
so a reading never depends on an assumed order again.

The bisect entries of the same morning (3d14eea9 image: `single_*` 2/2, `s*` 7/7 — all unmasked —
and `single_rgb,single_rgba` 2/2 pass) are consistent with this and need no correction.

**Why 24 vertex nested-loop cases went NotSupported -> Fail at 38ebdc15 with the same
refusal (not a regression).** dEQP decides between the two itself:
`ShaderLoopCase::init` (VK-GL-CTS modules/gles2/functional/es2fShaderLoopTests.cpp,
lines 248-268) turns a compile failure into NotSupported ("Loop type is not supported")
only when the context's capability probe for that loop type
(`isVertexDynamicLoopSupported()` and its three siblings, framework/opengl/
gluContextInfo.cpp: a small program with a uniform- or attribute-bounded loop,
compiled and linked once per process) says the type is unsupported; otherwise it
rethrows it as a failure. 38ebdc15 made the vertex dynamic-loop probe compile, so
dEQP stopped excusing the nested vertex refusals and counted them as failures --
the refusal itself was unchanged. The 24 fragment nested cases stayed NotSupported
there, so the fragment probe program still failed in that run; its shader alone
compiles at 38ebdc15 (checked on the host), so what failed was the probe's link
against a vertex shader that writes no v_color, not reproduced here. Moot at
d28c83f0: all four probes compile and link, no case is NotSupported, and no loop
case is refused.

color_clear's 11: the eight colour-masked cases (complex, long_masked, masked, masked_scissored,
rgb and rgba: the PowerVR clear applies no partial colour mask, `plan_clear` "no masked clear
shader") and **scissored_rgb, scissored_rgba, short_scissored_rgb**, which use no mask: a
PowerVR scissored-clear defect, open (the GC7000 passes those three). Per case the Zephyr
result is identical to the Linux path's (below).

`functional.prerequisite` at d3de621a (image 1a0a513c, the same flags as the 351ea217 one):
dEQP returned complete with 0 failed (rc 0 on the panel); the case count was not read off the
panel, so the STATUS cell keeps its pre-push marker until a serial-console run.

Before c96535f1 the same color_clear image (d3de621a) never got a kick through: `render: fence 1
timeout (ufo=0)` and every later fence the same, 4 cases Fail and the rest never reached. That
was the shape-2 wedge below.

### Shape 2 ("fence 1 timeout", freelist grow pending) was an inverted TA region clip

- **Reproducer.** dEQP-GLES2 color_clear.complex_rgb wedged on its first kick 3 of 3 on a
  freshly loaded module, Linux path, with the remote pair and the online pair of d3de621a and
  with a library built at 351ea217 (so neither the shader back end nor a recent library change).
  Stall line every time: `geom rd=0 ... | KCCB rd=w | gufo[seq 1]=0 fufo=0` and
  `freelist1 cur=512 top=511 max=4096 grow=256 ready=0 pending=1; fwccb grow req/done=1/1`.
- **Not the freelist.** `fl_init_pages` never reached the render service (it only sizes the
  boot-time lists in pvr_fw_boot.c; pvr_render.c:711-724 sizes its own), so the 1024/2048 arms
  measured nothing. A 128 MiB carveout measured nothing either ("render pool exhausted ... no
  pool memory for the 256x256 HWRT": no kick). With 256 MiB the HWRT was built with 2048 pages,
  no grow was asked for (pending=0, req/done 0/0) and it still wedged 3 of 3: the pending grow
  at 64 MiB was a side effect. wait_repost fired (3 per run) and did not move the fence: not
  the lost kick either.
- **The kick.** complex_rgb's random scissor boxes include rectangles wholly outside the target.
  After the y flip `top = h - y1` was never clamped, so a box above the target went to
  TA_REGION_CLIP inverted (top > bottom) with no ISP scissor entry. One call reproduces it:
  `glScissor(0, -200, 100, 50); glClear(COLOR)` on a 256x256 pbuffer: 20.98 s, two fence
  timeouts, `geom rd=0`; a box inside: instant; a box wholly left: no wedge but tile column 0
  cleared (region 0..0, no scissor entry). All three predicted before running.
- **Fix** (b16c13f5, on main in c96535f1): `draw_box()` computes the clamped box once and
  `record_draw` records a draw whose box is empty as nothing (not counted in `ndraws`, so
  flush's covering object still guards an otherwise empty frame). Host tests: no inverted
  region clip over a sweep of boxes with both flips, and boxes wholly outside record nothing;
  both fail with the check removed.
- **Board, c96535f1, Linux path**: the reproducer and both other boxes 0.00 s, 0 timeouts;
  complex_rgb alone 3 of 3 with 0 timeouts (Fail as a pixel verdict: the masked clear);
  `functional.color_clear` 19/19 executed, 8 pass, 11 fail, 0 not executed, 0 timeouts
  (remote pair es2-c96535f1, server built from c96535f1).

### The lost-kick stall: wait_repost on by default (a mitigation; root cause not found)

gl_test case 13 check 9 ("depth cleared mid-frame") was not a depth defect: in the failing run
the kick after the mid-frame clear logged `pvr_backend: kick 85 did not complete (1)` twice
(2 x 20 s) and the read-back saw the previous kick's picture. Case 13 alone, 20 ms apart,
interleaved arms (Linux path, module d3de621a0964, remote pair):

| arm | wait_repost | wait_rering | runs | check-9 FAIL | timeouts |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | N | N | 26 | 14 | 29 |
| R | Y | N | 30 | 0 | 0 |
| A2 | N | N | 30 | 16 | 32 |
| R2 | Y | N | 30 | 0 | 0 |
| B | N | Y | 30 | 13 | 26 |

Every FAIL had exactly two timeouts and no PASS had any. R+R2 logged 27 re-posts (read from the
kernel ring: the `dmesg -w` capture had died during R, and its "0" was the dead file's).
Re-posting the same KICK clears the stall where ringing the doorbell again does not: the
firmware sits on a posted kick until another command arrives. The rate varies a lot (about
1/40 earlier in the day, about half here). 1f6540bd makes wait_repost the default as a
**mitigation**; the counter is `/sys/module/pvrgpu/parameters/reposts` on Linux and the running
count in the log line on Zephyr. Acceptance at c96535f1 (defaults): case 13 x30 30/30, 0
timeouts, reposts 12; the full gl_test set 34/38, 0 timed out, failing 22 44 46 48 (13 now
passes; 22 fails identically with the gl_test of 8611f478, i.e. before this push: c8f470de's
reset_state raises GL error 0x500 in glGetIntegerv, then "default VAO attr0 disabled = 1 want 0").
68e11147 makes a case during which a fence wait timed out its own outcome, TIMEOUT. (The backend's
`wait_timeouts` counter that it reads went in with b16c13f5, the shape-2 commit, because both
edits were in backend.rs; 68e11147 only uses it.)

### Also measured

- **gl_test 83 pointcoord**: Linux path, remote pair d3de621a: PASS 5/5 (it read s = t = 1.0
  everywhere at 63b50b3; e00ada6c's point-sprite iterator). Zephyr, online, 151bdd7a: PASS.
- **gl_test 63 / 98 / 100 on Zephyr, online, 151bdd7a**: 63 matattr PASS; 98 uniloop PASS
  (count 0/1/7/4097 = ff000000/ff000010/ff000070/fff00000, the cap, as predicted); 100 idxtex
  PASS (4db233cc within 3 of 4db333cc, b34d9966). 98 and 100 need the default shader set: the
  ES 1.00 set skips them by name.
- **DSS negative VID_ROW_INC** (Zephyr, AM62P, a build-tree probe on d3de621a): BA = last row,
  ROW_INC = 1 - width*cpp - stride gives a clean vertical mirror at scan-out, 9 toggles, no
  tearing (VID plane only; VIDL1 not tried). The default framebuffer can be rendered y-up and
  flipped by the DSS.
- **Qt and ENFORCE_ZEPHYR_STDINT**: the Qt images keep `=y`. All 78 archives of the Qt install
  import 65 `std::` symbols from libstdc++; the SDK's libstdc++.a defines every one and none has
  a `long long` (x/y) parameter (the filter was checked against `seekg(long long)`). On LP64
  `long` and `long long` have the same size and calling convention, so the mismatch can only be
  an undefined symbol at link time, never a silent miscompile, and the Qt images link. dEQP keeps
  `=n`: it calls `seekg` and `sleep_for` with `int64_t`.
- **Qt main stack**: the Zephyr QPA reports no ThreadedOpenGL, so Qt Quick runs the basic render
  loop and every GL call, glCompileShader included, is on main (1 MiB in every Qt image). The
  online compiler peaks near 74 KB; Qt's own peak there is unmeasured: the first online-compiling
  Qt image gets THREAD_ANALYZER and STACK_SENTINEL.

## `uniform_api.random.23` compiles on the GC7000: the allocator encodes as it builds (2026-09-24, gc-backend, HOST-ONLY)

The fix planned in "`uniform_api.random.23`: refused by name" above. Measured on the host, on
the product compile path (the online back end, GC7000), random.23's fragment shader in a lent
16 MiB arena so every step could finish, with `arena.used()`/`peak()` read after each codegen
step (a probe, not committed):

| step | added (bytes) | used after | note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| front end + `lower::relocate` | 337,995 kept | 348,932 | front-end high-water 1,977,592, given back by relocate |
| selection | 584,314 | 939,536 | 2,970 selected instructions |
| `Instr` array, (n + 64) x 160 B | 475,200 | 1,414,736 | **removed** |
| selection-list copy, (n + 64) x 60 B | 178,200 | 1,592,936 | |
| dead-code, sinking | 24,994 | 1,617,930 | |
| copy coalescing | 118,613 | 1,736,543 | |
| allocation + build | 468,777 | 2,205,320 | |
| encoded words | 46,576 | 2,251,896 | peak, 154,744 over 2 MiB |

The `Instr` array held every instruction decoded (160 bytes) only to be encoded into 16
afterwards; each is built exactly once. At 41798780 the allocator writes the encoding as it
builds (`allocate_and_encode_placed`) and the identity-copy pass works on the encoded program
(`drop_identity_movs_encoded`):

| | before | 41798780 |
|---|---:|---:|
| back end, end of compile | 2,251,896 | 1,776,712 |
| compile high-water | 2,251,896 (back end) | 1,977,592 (front end, before relocate) |
| product result (2,097,152-byte scratch) | refused: out of compiler memory | compiles: 2,888 instructions, 4 temps |

Byte-identical over the 382-source corpus: all 322 compiled programs hash the same words
(11,668 instructions, 1,879 temps). The high-water is pinned in `tests/deqp_repro_shaders.rs`
(1,000,000..=2,000,000). Not done, because it no longer moves the peak: handing selection's list
over instead of copying it (178,200 bytes of back end). The front end's 1,977,592 before
relocate is now what sets it, 119,560 bytes under the arena. HOST-ONLY: the board has not run
random.23.

DEMO3, build f5f28256 (a copy benchmark in each report, and the ARM clock asked at boot: N = the default, Y = the
maximum). Both PASS, 0 MMU faults, 0 recoveries: N `180 s, 844 frames`, Y `180 s, 1028 frames`. The clock lines, 19
each: N `arm 600 MHz, v3d 500 MHz`, Y `arm 1500 MHz, v3d 500 MHz`, `throttled 0x00000` in all.
- The first 60 s are the same at both clocks: 5.6 to 5.8 fps (N) and 5.5 to 5.7 (Y), copy mean 113 to 114 ms. So
  2.5 times the ARM clock does not make the copy faster.
- After 60 s, N steps down as DEMO1 and DEMO2 did (4.1 to 4.3 fps, copy mean 155 ms); Y does not step at all (5.5 to
  5.7 fps and 113 to 114 ms to the end). The benchmark shows the step in every copy at 600 MHz, not only the one to
  the framebuffer: N's five reports before 60 s against its 13 after: window->cacheable 19.2-19.4 ms -> 26.2-26.3,
  cacheable->fb(device) 26.7-27.1 -> 33.6-33.7, cacheable->fb(normal NC) 1.9-2.0 -> 2.5-2.6, the real copy 114 -> 155.5;
  Y's stay at 19.2-19.5, 26.7-27.0, 1.9-2.0 and 114 throughout. The step's likely cause, from the firmware's own
  configuration (not yet a runtime measurement): `initial_turbo=60`, which runs the ARM at its maximum for the first
  60 s after boot and then at the set rate, while GET_CLOCK_RATE reports the set rate (so the clock line stays flat over
  a real change). The raw lines, from the board under Linux: `vcgencmd get_config int` gives `arm_boost=1`,
  `arm_freq=1800`, `core_freq=500`, `core_freq_min=200`, `initial_turbo=60`; /boot/firmware/config.txt has `arm_boost=1`
  and no `initial_turbo` line, so 60 is the firmware's effective value (the lead's ssh reading at 21:59:47, after
  CLUSTER5; the same values in the 2026-09-24 02:43 capture rpi4-linux/linux_facts.txt, which I read). The lead also
  read `measure_clock arm` 1100302720 and throttled 0x0 under Linux then. Two limits: these readings are from boots
  into Linux (config.txt), while the Zephyr images boot through tryboot.txt (no `initial_turbo` line there either, per
  the lead), so the value in a Zephyr boot is expected, not read; and the proof in the run itself is tomorrow's
  instrument, GET_CLOCK_MEASURED in the clock line before and after 60 s. A question for v3d-glue, not a claim: the
  firmware says `arm_freq=1800` with `arm_boost=1`, while DEMO3Y asked for and was granted 1500 MHz.
- The framebuffer's mapping matters for writes to it: a 1920x720 copy from a cacheable buffer takes 26.7 to 27.1 ms to

  numbers do not say what the real 114 ms copy would become; that is not measured.

gl_test 46 es3size, every GPU on the online compiler: **refused: invalid shader (4.5.4)**. es300/texsize.frag declares a
sampler2DArray with no precision; GLSL ES 3.00 rev 6 section 4.5.4 (p.55) gives that type no default precision, so the
online front end's refusal is right ("this sampler type has no default precision (section 4.5.4)"), and the offline and
remote paths accepting it is a leniency. The same refusal is the AM62P's and the i.MX8MP's "46 es3size" in their online
regression sets. On the V3D the case has not been run; its expected verdict is this refusal. The shader fix (highp) waits
for the next regeneration of both offline tables (the lead's decision, 2026-09-26; gl_test.c case 46 note).

an EGL window surface; each frame is drawn into the hidden half and SET_VIRTUAL_OFFSET pans to it; no copy, no SET_VSYNC).
Build 1f68ba0a, an experiment arm, not on origin: origin/main e13be818 + v3d-tex's flip helpers 96a02d67 + 55102661 (the
virtual allocation mapped Normal NC) + 74a49634 (the sample). ARM_CLOCK_MAX=y, DEMO_S=180. Third-party trees, from main's
patches exactly: Slint 1007c032 + `slint-nostd.patch` 759e6579 (no fix A), FemtoVG 0.26.0 + d561a600 (no pool), glow 0.18.0 +
d17a60c7; rust Cargo.lock 1a5f8df7. Image sha e048cfe0 (queue1.log `STAGED cluster_demo12_1f68ba0a.bin`),
`records/pi4/record_DEMO12_cluster_demo12_1f68ba0a.txt` (sha256 0cd31960acb8bdbd, 805 lines).
**FAIL**: `demo: FAIL: demo frame 853 at t=47031 ms: rc 0, GL error 0x505, 82 ms`, after `texture 47x111 x1 fmt 0 (1 levels,
21312 bytes): out of GPU memory`. The check before it passed: `screen: asked 1920x720, virtual 1920x1440: rc 0, granted
1920x720 virtual 1920x1440 pitch 7680`, half 0 at phys 0x3e16e000, half 1 at 0x3e6b4000; crc32 0xfec9a1d7 read from the shown
half, guard rows (half 1's first) 0 of 15360 changed, probes 34 of 34. MMU faults 0, recoveries 0, nothing hung.
The cause is the second half's depth/stencil buffer. The window's buffer is keyed by the surface's address
(`src/gl/draw.rs:1375`), so half 1 needs its own 5,533,696 bytes. The backend retries the allocation at every job
(`src/v3d/backend.rs:924-936` logs only the first failure). The record has 423 `osal(v3d): out of GPU memory for 5533696
bytes` lines, about one per half-1 frame, and twice it gave up a Slint FBO's depth/stencil buffer for it (`id 6`, `id 7 ...
its contents are lost`). The carve-out's longest free run was 5,178, 5,226, 5,074 and 5,399 KiB at t=10 to 40, against
5,404 KiB needed. Between t=40 and t=47 a large enough run appeared and the allocation succeeded: the failures stop, and
usage went from 43.90 MB to 49.38 of 49.80 MB (`carve-out: 49379584 bytes used now`). Then 32-38 KiB tiled copies and a
21 KiB text texture found no memory. Predicted was "fails, and stays on-chip"; the worse case is that it eventually fits.
What worked, t=10 to 40 (4 reports): `present: direct (pan, no copy)`, pans 158, 180, 189 and 193 (failed 0, not echoed 0),
mean 99-116 us, eglMakeCurrent mean 1 us, `copy mean 0 ms` in each report, frames with more than one job 0-1 per half.
`demo: frame 100 coverage: half 0 filled with the sentinel before the draw, 0 sentinel pixels left of 1382400, 0 with alpha
!= 255`: Slint covers the whole window every frame, so a picture two frames old cannot show through. The lead's display
captures at 11:40 (`capture_DEMO12_1f68ba0a_frame1.jpg`, `_frame6.jpg`) showed the cluster drawn correctly (both captures lost in
the 17:19 records deletion; the row's numbers rest on the record file). fps 15.7, 17.9, 18.8,
19.3, frame mean 48-51 ms, split draw 22.9-26.5 ms (new textures 4.4-8.1 per frame: neither fix A nor the pool), swap
25.0-25.6 ms. These frame times are not a performance result: every half-1 frame also paid the failed 5.5 MB search and a
UART line (`demo: 853 frames in 47 s, 18.1 fps, worst frame 135 ms`). So DEMO12C (this build, DIRECT=n) is the copy-path
baseline, and DEMO12 is rerun only after the depth/stencil fix. That fix is v3d-tex's, in `src/v3d/backend.rs`: a live
buffer of the same size whose depth and stencil are both Untouched is lent to the other half, and a failed large allocation
is no longer retried at every job. A window depth/stencil buffer allocated only when a frame splits into several jobs is
filed as the follow-up (it would also free today's 5.5 MB). The two capture files kept are frame 1 and frame 6 of the lead's
burst (no tear seen in the frames captured, per the lead; the card's rate is unknown).

TFU140, gl_test case 140 tfuprobe (v3d-tex's TFU probe, build 9b55d8df, an experiment arm, not on origin; image sha
446fdf30, queue1.log line 999; `records/pi4/record_TFU140_gl_test_tfu140_9b55d8df.txt`, sha256 5132047c33a92b09, 102 lines):
`v3d_gl_test: case 140 PASS`, `250 TFU jobs run`, MMU faults 0, recoveries 0, `resets 0` on every line. `HUB_IDENT1 says TFU`.
Part 1 is 40 variants: RGBA8 (converted as R32F and as RGBA8), RG8 (as R16F and as RG8) and R8, each at 8 sizes from 3x5 to
95x419, covering every output layout (LT, UB-linear 1 and 2 columns, UIF, UIF XOR) and output padding 0 and 5. Each variant
is tried with 6 source shapes: a 64-byte-aligned stride or the tight row stride, at source offsets +0, +64 and +4 bytes.
Every one of the 40 lines reads `s64+0:ok s64+64:ok s64+4:ok tight+0:ok tight+64:ok tight+4:ok` (240 jobs), and the summary
line is `Mesa's shape (s64+0) 40 of 40 equal (planned 40)`. So on this board the TFU also takes a source stride that is not
64-byte aligned (our pair-padded rows) and a source 4 bytes off a 64-byte boundary. These were the two risks in v3d-tex's TFU
note (every Mesa use has a 64-byte stride). The whole window, 1920x720 RGBA8 to UIF (5,529,600 bytes): TFU 2,228-2,253 us
as RGBA8 and 2,244-2,246 us as R32F, `0 of 1382400 texels wrong (unwritten 0)`. The CPU tiling of the same image takes
22,067-22,097 us from cacheable memory and 144,882-144,909 us from V3D (non-cacheable) memory. Reading: the TFU tiles a
window-sized image 10 times faster than the CPU from cacheable memory and 65 times faster from GPU memory. It helps the
first frame (the 5.5 MB backdrop) and any large upload or re-tiling. The steady frame's tiling is under 0.7 ms (DEMO11), so
there it wins at most that.
v3d-tex's reading of the same record: no wrong texel, error or refusal anywhere in part 1. The unaligned rows were R8 95
bytes, RG8 190 and RGBA8 380. `pad+N` means the TFU wrote every padding byte of the slice. That is harmless, since the TMU
never reads padding, but the destination must be the layout's full padded size. The job's completion (TFUC) was seen with
the hub interrupts masked. The caller rule, as accepted by the lead: any whole number of texels as the source stride; the
source 4-byte aligned (+0, +4 and +64 measured; a 1-3 byte offset unmeasured); the destination 64-byte aligned with the whole
padded slice writable. Measured only for RGBA8, RG8 and R8, one level, with no render in flight. Unmeasured: other formats,
mipmap generation, the TFU running beside a render, and timing at small sizes.

(DEMO12U: about 43.9; the second arena set is about 2.6 MB). 1500 MHz held, 48.1-51.5 C, counters 0, no "out of GPU memory"
line, no GL error. `render bench: skipped, a frame in flight (unpaced)` in all 18 reports, by design. Reading: the CPU's
draw of frame N+1 now overlaps the GPU's render of frame N. The frame falls from 46-51 ms to 25-29 ms, about the longer of
the draw (20-25 ms) and the render (about 24-25 ms in the synchronous records), plus the copy. v3d-tex predicted 37-40 fps.
DEMO13, the direct present (image sha 9db36c32, line 1105; `records/pi4/record_DEMO13_cluster_demo13_4ed1c629.txt`, sha256
e754735e3113b1fa, 300 lines): **no verdict**. The record holds the check (crc32 0xfec9a1d7 on half 0) and the t=10 s report only:
24.6 fps, the fence wait mean 8.8 ms (max 26.8), 162 of 246 fences already signaled at the first look, pans 246 (failed 0), the
carve-out 46.70 MB. Then the UART is silent: the lead's raw log has no line between 13:50:47 and the firmware's reboot at
13:55:15. The demo hung, and the board's watchdog ended the run. `demo: frame 100 coverage: half 0 filled with the sentinel
before the draw, 1382400 sentinel pixels left of 1382400`: frame 100's half was untouched when its fence was seen as done.
The cause, read in the code built: eglClientWaitSync, on a fence not yet signaled, calls the backend's finish, and the
V3D's finish is flush_job + wait_in_flight (`src/v3d/backend.rs:3457-3469` at 4ed1c629). So it submits the frame being
recorded and waits for it too. The direct loop waits for frame N's fence after frame N+1's draw was recorded, so each such
wait rendered N+1 into the half still on screen, before the pan. At frame 100 that render came before the sentinel fill,
which then covered it. The copy path waits after its swap, with nothing recorded, and its fences were always already
signaled, so it never reached this. The hang is not explained by the record. The fix belongs to the library:
eglClientWaitSync waits only for its sync's job and never submits the open recording (the fence already flushed at
creation). The hang is not explained; DEMO13 is rerun as DEMO13R (5e44cd77: the fence polled through EGL_SYNC_STATUS, which
submits nothing, bounded at 2 s, and a progress line every 100 frames). The watchdog's timing narrows it. A frame
running past the 1000 ms budget stops the feeding, and the reset follows within 10 s. The reset came instead at the
image's lifetime bound (about 13:55:11 by the bootloader's stamp). So frames kept starting less than 1 s apart, or the
demo loop had exited, while nothing reached the UART, and none of the OSAL's bounded 4 s waits fired. No display capture
exists for DEMO13 (the capture card showed another HDMI source at 13:53).

gl_test case only; an experiment arm, not on origin). Stripe textures (R alternates 0/255 with the column, G with the row), W x 16
drawn 1:1 into a W x 16 FBO; per width LINEAR, NEAREST, and a control (LINEAR shifted by half a texel must read a 50/50 blend).
Image sha 4c9b1a3c (queue1.log line 1271), `records/pi4/record_TEXCENTRE_gt_texcentre.txt` (sha256 ebb461d9f231b59c, 67 lines):
build 5cd75096, `case 146 texcentre: FAIL`, 0 of 1 passed (228 ms), MMU faults 0, recoveries 0, slow jobs 0.
W = 64: LINEAR 1024 of 1024 exact, NEAREST 1024 of 1024 exact, control 945 of 945 read the blend.
W = 600: **LINEAR 1009 of 9600 exact; the other 8591 are off by 1 in R** (max |dR| 1, |dG| 0; max |dR| 1 in every quarter of x);
first differing pixel (1,0) = fe 00 80 ff (expected ff: the odd column took 1/255 of its neighbour). NEAREST 9600 of 9600 exact;
control 8985 of 8985 read the blend.
**The 1920-wide and the window (64 x 64, flipped) arms did not run**: the case stops at its first failing width (`for (...; ok &&
...)` over the widths, and the window arm is under `if (ok)`), so the record has nothing on the backdrop's width or the flipped
target. Reading: at W = 600 the V3D's LINEAR does not return the texel at the texel centre for most columns; the error is 1 of 255,
in x only (G, the 16-row axis, is exact). The per-quarter figure cannot separate an offset from a precision error here: both
round to 1 LSB. W = 64, where the centre (x + 0.5) / 64 is exact in float, is exact; that fits a coordinate or weight precision
cause, but it is not shown. This is consistent with DEMO14G's crc move (NEAREST for the 1:1 images moved the crc against
LINEAR), since a 1-LSB LINEAR error is enough to move a crc and stays well inside the probes' tolerance of 12; the cluster's own
images were not measured, so it is not yet the proof. What would close it: the case run on all arms (every width and the window,
not stopping at the first failure), and the DEMO14G question's own proof (a LINEAR check whose crc equals the NEAREST arm's).
TEXCENTRE2, the same case rebuilt as TEXCENTRE asked: v3d-glue's 925ecd60 = 5cd75096 + da4a6a2d (every target runs after a
failing one) + b55de77a (a fourth draw per target: LINEAR 1:1 shifted by 1/512 texel) + 925ecd60 (1920 wide drawn 1:1 from a
2048-wide texture, the lead's arm); `git diff --stat 5cd75096 925ecd60`: gl_test.c only. An experiment arm, not on origin. Image
sha 25a5e8c2 (queue1.log line 1323), `records/pi4/record_TEXCENTRE2_gt_texcentre2.txt` (sha256 adeeacabc8737457, 83 lines): build
925ecd60, `case 146 texcentre: FAIL` (its rule: LINEAR must be exact everywhere), 0 of 1 (496 ms), MMU faults 0, recoveries 0;
every target and every draw printed.

| target, texture | LINEAR 1:1 exact | its errors | NEAREST | control (50/50) | LINEAR + 1/512 texel |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fbo 64x16, tex 64 | 1024 of 1024 | none | 1024 of 1024 | 945 of 945 | 1024 of 1024 |
| fbo 600x16, tex 600 | **1009 of 9600** | 8591 at \|dR\| 1, every quarter; first (1,0) = fe 00 80 ff | 9600 of 9600 | 8985 of 8985 | 9600 of 9600 |
| fbo 1920x16, tex 1920 | **4067 of 30720** | 26653 at \|dR\| 1, every quarter; first (1,0) = fe 00 80 ff | 30720 of 30720 | 28785 of 28785 | 30720 of 30720 |
| fbo 1920x16, tex 2048 | 30720 of 30720 | none | 30720 of 30720 | 28785 of 28785 | 30720 of 30720 |
| window 64x64 (flipped) | 4096 of 4096 | none | 4096 of 4096 | 3969 of 3969 | 4096 of 4096 |

The 600-wide line repeats TEXCENTRE's to the pixel. Every |dR| error is exactly 1 and |dG| is 0 everywhere.
Reading: LINEAR at a texel centre is off by 1 of 255 when the texture's width is 600 or 1920, and exact when it is 64 or
2048, including 1920 pixels drawn from the 2048-wide texture; the texel centre (x + 0.5) / W is exact in float for a power
of two W and not otherwise. Shifting the coordinate by 1/512 texel makes every width exact, which is consistent with the
sampled position falling just short of the centre at the non-power-of-two widths, by less than the filter's weight step
(the case does not measure the direction of the other side: no -1/512 draw). The flipped window target changes nothing.
The lead's reading (not measured here): the TMU's sub-texel bits truncate a coordinate that lands just under the texel
centre at non-power-of-two widths; a V3D fact, 1 LSB, within dEQP's thresholds, with no GL-core fix. Case 146's criterion,
every pixel exact, is stricter than GL requires of filtering, so its FAIL means "LINEAR 1:1 is not bit-exact at these
widths" (by 1 of 255, at most pixels), not a conformance failure. v3d-glue's note: a -1/512 draw would tell truncation (off
at every width, 64 included) from rounding (exact) and goes in first if the coordinate fix is pursued.
So the DEMO14G crc move has a measured mechanism at the backdrop's and the rings' widths: their 1:1 LINEAR images are 1 LSB
off at most pixels, and NEAREST (or a power-of-two texture, or the 1/512 shift) is exact. Which fix to take is v3d-glue's
and the lead's.

Render best / mean, us (ns a pixel): clear 1003 / 1003 (0.7); flat colour 1757 / 1759 (1.2); RGBA8 NEAREST 2889 / 2890, LINEAR
2891 / 2893, LINEAR + femtovg's blend 2893 / 2896 (2.0 each); LA8 LINEAR 2876 / 2882, L8 LINEAR 2871 / 2873 (2.0); with a D24S8
renderbuffer: colour cleared only 2893 / 2893 (2.0), all cleared 3850 / 3860 (2.7), all cleared then depth and stencil
invalidated 3857 / 3861 (2.7). Bin 56-89 us in every arm. Every pixel check but one is ok.
**The FAIL is the rgba8-mip arm, and it is the case's, not the GPU's**: `pixel 0xff000000 want 0xff6068c0 MISMATCH`, after the
GL core's line `a texture on unit 0 is incomplete and samples (0,0,0,1): a mipmap min filter, but a level of the chain has no
image (target 0xde1, 1920x720, levels 1 of 1, ...)`. 1920x720 is not a power of two. glGenerateMipmap lays out no chain for it
(src/gl/texture.rs on main: INVALID_OPERATION under an ES 2.0-reporting build, else a no-op), so under LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR the
texture is incomplete and samples black, as ES 2.0 requires. The arm's time (2847 us) is that of an incomplete texture, not
of a mip chain, and is not a measurement of mipmapped sampling. A mip arm needs a power-of-two texture.
Reading, from the arms that passed: a textured full-screen quad costs about 2.0 ns a pixel whatever the texel size (4, 2 or 1
bytes), the filter (NEAREST or LINEAR) or the blend, so at this size texel bandwidth, filtering and blending are not what
it costs. Clearing depth and stencil adds about 0.96 ms (2.7 against 2.0 ns a pixel), and invalidating them after the clear
saves nothing measurable (3857 against 3850 us). Against the cluster's backdrop (about 12.7 ms, 9.2 ns a pixel, DEMO14D per
the commit) this floor is about 2.9 ms; the rest of the backdrop's cost is not in any of these arms.

ran on that panel, whose mode and rate their own pan-sync lines give.
Part 2, 20 pans in each arm on a 1280x1440 virtual framebuffer, every pan answered (20 of 20), every address found in the
channel's display list and every latch seen (20 of 20):
Before the pans the case printed `fb 0x3e4f2000 pitch 5120; its address at display-list word -1 (list 1636), the second
half's at 6`: the first half's address was not found in the list at that point, so for pans to it the case's "address in
the list" can only have come from its other test, DISPLIST changing (`list != list0`); the record does not say which of the
two fired per pan.
- issued at the frame counter's step (0 us after it, line 0): mailbox 153 us mean (max 1307); the new address appears in
  the display list 31,005 us after the pan (mean); latched 33,333 us after the pan (mean and max), at frame +0 in 5, +1 in 15.
- issued half a frame later (16,666 us, line 1038): mailbox 142 us mean (max 1138); the address in the list after 14,338 us;
  latched 16,666 us after the pan (mean and max), at frame +0 in 2, +1 in 18.
Reading: the pan call returns in about 0.15 ms and does not wait for the display. The firmware writes the new address into
the display list about 2.3 ms before the next frame starts, in both arms (31.0 of 33.3 ms, and 14.3 of 16.7 ms), and the HVS
takes it at that next frame's start, never later ("later 0" in both). So a pan switches halves at a frame boundary, within
one frame. The latch times are identical to the microsecond in all 20 pans of an arm, as a frame edge at a fixed period would
make them; the case does not check that independently. What it implies for the direct present (not measured here): after a
pan, the half that was on screen stays on screen until the next frame starts, up to one display frame (33 ms at 30 Hz), so
a loop that starts drawing into that half right after the pan can draw into a half still being scanned out. At 125 fps
(DEMO15) against a 30 Hz display, that is the tearing risk to measure next; the visible rate on this display is at most 30.

Reading (measured as far as the registers go): the firmware drives the HDMI output at 800x600, not the panel's native
1920x720, and composes our 1920x720 framebuffer into it scaled to 800x300 at y 150, letterboxed. The panel stretches the 800x600
signal to its 1920x720, so the picture fills half its height: the user's report, now with its mechanism. The GPU renders the
full 1920x720 (the crc and probes read that target and are unaffected). The fix is the HDMI mode the firmware sets at boot
(for example `hdmi_cvt`/`hdmi_group` in the tryboot config); the user's decision, asked by the lead.

**The cause (v3d-glue's, 2026-09-26 evening; consistent with the code and with every record's timing, the watchdog's own
line not yet recorded: WDOG1 is queued for it).** `driver/samples/zephyr/v3d_clear/src/rpi_wdog.c` at 188dfa5c: a timer feeds
the PM watchdog every 3000 ms (`FEED_EVERY_MS`), each feed arming 10 s (`WDOG_PERIOD_S`), and it stops feeding for good the
first time `rpi_wdog_alive()` says no; the cluster's override (`v3d_gl_cluster/src/main.c:826-834`) says no while a demo frame
has run longer than the 1000 ms budget. The demo's coverage check at frame 100 runs longer than that inside the frame (STRESS1B:
`demo STALL: frame 101 in "complete the frame in flight (fence wait, pan)" for 677 ms`, then `for 1677 ms`). If the feed tick
at 6.0 s of uptime falls in it, the last feed was the one at 3.0 s, and the SoC resets about 10 s after that (WDOG1, below,
reads the PM counter at 452 ms left at 13,011 ms: about 13.46 s), where the four stop; one tick later (last feed at 6.0 s,
feeding stopped at 9.0 s) the reset comes about 16.5 s, where DEMO20 stops. (The first version of this paragraph put the
ticks at about 3.3 s plus multiples of 3 s, inferred; WDOG1 prints them: 0, 3000 and 6000 ms of uptime.) The uptime of frame 100's
`demo progress` line in each record:

| stopped (uptime of the stop) | frame 100 at | ran through | frame 100 at |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| STRESS1 (13.2-13.5 s) | 6,318 ms | DEMO15 | 6,698 ms |
| STRESS1B (13.2-13.5 s) | 6,344 ms | DEMO15R | 6,751 ms |
| DEMO22 (13.3-14.0 s) | 6,587 ms | DEMO18 | 6,785 ms |
| DEMO23 (13.3-14.0 s) | 6,599 ms | DEMO17 | 6,901 ms |
| DEMO20 (about 15-17 s) | 9,456 ms | DEMO19 | 7,603 ms |
| | | DEMO20B | 7,846 ms |

Every image whose frame 100 came at 6.32-6.60 s stopped at about 13.3 s, and every one at 6.70 s or later ran on; DEMO20, whose
frame 100 came at 9.46 s, just after the 9.0 s tick, stopped one period later. So the stops are the watchdog ending a run whose
100th frame straddled a feed tick, not a GPU or CPU hang; STRESS1B's 500 ms reporter printed nothing because the SoC reset,
not because its timer died. The fix is v3d-glue's, in the sample: work done outside a frame (the coverage check) restarts the
frame clock the watchdog reads, and the check reads through a cached row buffer. DEMO15R, frame 100 at 6.75 s, is in the band
that runs on, so tonight's environment behaves as at 18:02.

- pass 1 (rows 0-63, the copy made at the draw): `job 1 running at the write: no`, `pass 1 NOT EXERCISED: job 1 was not running
  at the write`. Its pixels are right (0 of 2048 wrong, left and right), but job 1 had ended, so they say nothing about the

case does not tell 4a8cbd26's change apart from its absence: the control arm reports the same "running at the write: yes".
TFU143H / TFU143CH, the same case rebuilt so the arms can separate (v3d-tex's second commit, "a heavy job 1, and the line that
separates the arms": job 1 draws 64 times with a fragment shader looping 256 times, and each pass prints "write waited", the
backend's waits for a job in flight across the update, and the update's wall time). TFU143H = c2f7795e (with 4a8cbd26),
TFU143CH = 2dd2b35b (without). `git diff --stat 2dd2b35b c2f7795e`: 9 files, 125 insertions, 5 deletions, exactly the stat of
4a8cbd26 itself, and no difference in gl_test.c. Experiment arms, not on origin. Images 543336c2 and 65988fbd (queue1.log lines
1287, 1291); `records/pi4/record_TFU143H_gl_test_tfu143_c2f7795e.txt` (sha256 ffe1c969351f354f, 70 lines) and
`record_TFU143CH_gl_test_tfu143c_2dd2b35b.txt` (sha256 307f167312a6d5ac, 70 lines). Both: `case 143 tfuorder: PASS`, 1 of 1,
TFU jobs 1 and failed 0 in each pass, MMU faults 0, recoveries 0, resets 0, and 0 of 2048 pixels wrong on both sides of both
passes.
- Pass 1 (rows 0-63, the copy at the draw), now exercised in both (`job 1 running at the write: yes`): **with 4a8cbd26 `write
  waited: no (backend waits +0, kicks +0), 223 us`, job 1 still running after the write; without it `write waited: yes
  (backend waits +1, kicks +0), 76272 us`**, job 1 ended by then. So 4a8cbd26 removes a 76 ms wait for job 1 from this update,
  and the pixels stay right: the texture write does not disturb the job that sampled the old texels.
- Pass 2 (the whole image, the copy in the call): with 4a8cbd26 `write waited: no (backend waits +0, kicks +0), 73087 us`;
  without it `write waited: yes (backend waits +1, kicks +0), 73482 us`. Both arms take about 73 ms and job 1 has ended by
  the end of the update in both. With 4a8cbd26 that wait is not counted by the backend's counter, so the pass's "waited: no"
  is not what it took: the update still waits for job 1, by a path the counter does not see. v3d-tex's reading, from the design: a whole-image
  update takes fresh storage (it never waits in settle_texture), and its TFU copy runs inside glTexSubImage2D, where
  `osal_v3d_tfu` first calls `finish_inflight` (`src/osal/zephyr_v3d.c` line 895 in c2f7795e, 886 on origin/main) and then polls
  the TFU job to its end; that is the ~73 ms in both arms, outside the backend's wait counter.
  Pass 2 does not separate the arms.
The claim for 4a8cbd26 rests on pass 1: the write no longer waits for a job that only sampled a copy, with every pixel right.

Corroboration (the user's rule of 2026-09-25, 15:45: a constraint cites outside sources):
- Mesa's v3d has no seamless control. `src/gallium/drivers/v3d/v3d_screen.c` and `v3dx_state.c`, the Vulkan
  `src/broadcom/vulkan/v3dv_device.c` and `v3dvx_device.c`, and the packet description `src/broadcom/cle/v3d_packet.xml`
  contain no "seamless" at all (GitHub mirror `mirror/mesa`, main at e24dc5bd, 2026-05-29). In `docs/features.txt`
  (same tree) `VK_EXT_non_seamless_cube_map`, the Vulkan way to turn seamless filtering off, is DONE for anv, hasvk,
  hk, lvp, nvk, panvk, pvr, radv, tu and vn, and not for v3dv; `GL_ARB_seamless_cubemap_per_texture` does not list
  v3d either. v3d is listed for GLES 3.1, which requires seamless cube filtering. So Broadcom's own open driver offers
  no non-seamless mode on this GPU. This agrees with the hardware claim; it is not a Broadcom document (none found).
- The non-seamless rule: ARB_seamless_cube_map (registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_seamless_cube_map.txt)
  describes the old behaviour as "Each face of the texture is treated as an independent two-dimensional texture".
  The OpenGL ES 3.0.6 specification (registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/es/3.0/es_spec_3.0.pdf), Appendix F.2
  "Differences in Runtime Behavior", p. 333: "OpenGL ES 3.0 requires that all cube map filtering be seamless.
  OpenGL ES 2.0 specified that a single cube map face be selected and used for filtering. See section 3.8.9.1"
  (Seamless Cube Map Filtering, p. 152).
- dEQP chooses its reference by context, not by ES version alone: `sampler.seamlessCubeMap = m_isES3Capable`
  (es2fVertexTextureTests.cpp:1154), `glu::IsES3Compatible(gl)` (es2fShaderTextureFunctionTests.cpp:633,
  es2fTextureMipmapTests.cpp:658), and `IsES3Compatible` is true when `glGetIntegerv(GL_MAJOR_VERSION)` raises no error
  (gluContextInfo.cpp:64-73; VK-GL-CTS 93bca01). Our images report ES 2.0 (`CONFIG_YAKOGL_REPORT_ES2=y`), so the query
  errors and dEQP compares against a non-seamless reference. A driver that answers `GL_MAJOR_VERSION` (Mesa's v3d
  exposes GLES 3.1) is compared against a seamless reference, so on that driver these cases are not expected to show
  this difference. The constraint is therefore "V3D cannot filter non-seamlessly, and an ES 2.0-only context is judged
  non-seamless"; it was not measured with a context that answers `GL_MAJOR_VERSION`.

**Experiments (not a conformance configuration): the 19, then the 6, with the context reporting ES 3.0.** The image turns off both
`CONFIG_DEQP_REPORT_ES2` and `CONFIG_YAKOGL_REPORT_ES2` (v3d_deqp's prj.conf sets the latter directly); against the
758a3123 `texture.vertex` build its .config differs in exactly those two lines. `GL_MAJOR_VERSION` is then answered,

The 23 F have one cause: **a loop in the shader.** It is confirmed on the board for
`flush_finish` (below), and inferred for `light_amount`. The V3D back end
refuses loops by name (`src/shaderc/online/v3d/prepare.rs:474`, `NotYet("loop")`; v3d-backend.md
"Control flow, step 1"), so the program does not build and the case fails before it draws
(R 0: no draw refusal).
- `flush_finish` (all 5): `init()` compiles `for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) color = sin(color);` and
  calls `TCU_FAIL("Compile failed")` when that fails (es2fFlushFinishTests.cpp:185-205). **Board,
  823d20fb image (sha 057916c2): `5 cases in 136 ms`, P 0 F 5 R 0, each case's reason
  `Compile failed at es2fFlushFinishTests.cpp:201`.** The loop is the construct in that shader the
  V3D compiler refuses by name. The
  test's timing checks give only Pass or CompatibilityWarning (:433, :459), so an F is not a
  flush/finish timing result, and the synchronous submit is not what these five measure.
- `light_amount` (18 of 19): the shaders loop over the lights (es2fLightAmountTest.cpp:107,
  :109). The one that passes, `none`, has zero lights.

fix proposed (v3d-glue: report [1, 512] on the V3D) is a GL-core change and goes to the user.

frees given back 32161792 bytes`. So the block held back is a kept tiled copy that the open job still samples, and
with it given back the 22,376,448 bytes would fit. The fix is to submit the open job and retry the allocation, not
item 22's evict (0 copies were live, as on 76e63ccd).

**T3 on batch 23, 8f2c90a3** (sha 87384e33; read from the UART log): `texture.mipmap` and `texture.specification`,
304 cases, **P 270** F 21, Q 13, no MMU fault.
- `mipmap` 87/112. F 12: `mipmap.cube.{basic,bias,projected}.*` (4 filters each), `Image verification
  failed`; each of these cases also logs `GL error 0x500 in glGetIntegerv`. That is dEQP asking for
  GL_MAJOR_VERSION to learn whether the context is ES3-capable (gluContextInfo.cpp:64-73), and GL_INVALID_ENUM
  is the right answer for ES 2.0 (4 passing `specification.basic_copyteximage2d.2d_*` log it for the same
  reason). Q 13:
  every `mipmap.cube.generate.*` case except `a8_fastest`, `rgb888_fastest` and `rgb888_nicest`, which pass:
  `QualityWarning (Low-quality method used)`.
- `specification` 183/192. F 9: `random_teximage2d.2d_5`, `2d_7` and `cube_1` to `cube_6`, `cube_8`, `Image
  comparison failed` (the levels sent out of order; tex's GL-core level-order report, item 15).
The cube, ETC1 and 2D groups that failed through 651755c7 pass now.

v3d-tex's reading (a hypothesis; the record has no pixel data to decide it). On an ES 2.0 context dEQP
judges the cube mipmap cases against a non-seamless reference (es2fTextureMipmapTests.cpp:658), and the
V3D always samples cube maps seamlessly (Mesa's v3d has no seamless control). The LOD tolerance differs
from ES3 only for the projected cases: every non-projected cube look-up uses lodBits 6 (:669). So for
`basic` and `bias` the difference is seamlessness alone, and since NEAREST never reads across a face,
the `nearest_nearest` failures are not a tolerance or seamless effect. Two candidates remain for those: a
level stored where the texture unit does not read it (batch 23 moved the cube levels), or the texture
unit's cube LOD. (An earlier version of this note blamed the ES2 tolerance for all three groups: wrong for
`basic` and `bias`.) The error masks decide it: errors only along face edges in `linear_linear` point at
seamlessness; in `nearest_nearest`, a region showing another face's colour points at placement, and the
same face's neighbouring level at LOD. gl_test 133 (fe5cc787) names the face and level each draw reads.

**The masks decided it: LOD at the cube face edges** (v3d-tex's reading of the QPA8 run, 4b714e79, which
copies the QPA with its images to the UART; the first QPA run, 3632b78e, had empty image sets because
the deqp sample's command line turns images off). In `mipmap.cube.basic.nearest_nearest`, 270 pixels
fail, on cell 14's last and cell 15's first column (x 86 and 87, full height); tex rebuilt dEQP's grid
with a port of its random generator, and it matches the Reference. The failing pixels show the same
face, one level finer, in exact colours. In `linear_linear`, 1,259 of the 1,701 invalid pixels are on a
cell's first or last column or row. Each cell draws a whole face, so these are face edges, where the
implicit LOD comes out too fine. So it is not a misplaced level and not seamlessness. **The cause is not
settled.** tex first named the missing per-lane cube normalization (Mesa's nir_normalize_cubemap_coords)
and then withdrew it: gl_test 133 passes with helper pixels past the face. The suspect now is the thin
cells (17x128) together with per-quad face selection; a board A/B case is proposed to the lead.
(Settled by that A/B, gl_test 134 on d4fb2127, above: the as-is thin cells fail 24/24, the normalized ones pass
24/24, so the missing per-lane normalization is the cause after all.)
`texture_functions.vertex.texturecubelod` fails for another reason (v3d-tex's reading of its QPA8 images):
the errors are where the LOD is above about 6.5, levels 7 and 8 (2x2 and 1x1) of the 256 cube. The result
colours break G = B and R = A, which every uploaded texel keeps, so it is not the level choice; they
match bilinear sampling that blends in the neighbouring faces (at one checked pixel R = 0 exactly as
predicted, G, B and A within 22). That is the seamless hardware against dEQP's non-seamless ES2
reference, the same row as `texture.vertex`'s cube failures. Its 2D twin `texture2dlod` passes. The 9
`random_teximage2d` F are GL-core level-order cases (tex's item-15 follow-up): `2d_5` (la16f 32x4) and `2d_7`
(rgb16f 256x64) start with a 1x1 level, which the before-level-0 rule reads as a square chain; the 7
cube cases upload a face above level 0 before any level-0 face, and the rule (53bf84b7) covers
GL_TEXTURE_2D only. That report goes to the GL-core owner.

**Batch I, 2a472ede** (sha 81540e3b): `depth_stencil_clear`, `polygon_offset`, `lifetime`,

`depth_stencil_clear`, and all of `polygon_offset`, `lifetime`, `multisample`).
- Case #4, `depth_stencil_clear.depth_stencil_masked`: R. The draw logged the refusal `the draw
  reads stencil an earlier job wrote, and stencil is not kept between jobs yet` (2 draws not
  recorded). dEQP's reason: `After clears: glGetError() returned GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY at
  es2fDepthStencilClearT...`.
- **Why the whole run stopped.** A refused draw is reported as `GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY`
  (`src/gl/draw.rs` `submit_draw`). dEQP's `glu::checkError` turns that into
  `glu::OutOfMemoryError` (`gluDefs.cpp:77`), a `tcu::ResourceError` whose `isFatal()` is true
  (`tcuDefs.hpp:129-131`). The executor then ends the session
  (`tcuTestSessionExecutor.cpp:384`). So on the V3D, any refused draw that a test follows with a
  `glGetError()` check ends the image. The cases after it never run, and no outcome is recorded
  for them.
- The fix is v3d-glue's: keep stencil (and depth) across jobs (step C), or report a refused
  draw some other way. Until then, groups that may hit a refusal get their own image.

### The scissored-clear defect: a colour clear joined a frame that began by loading colour

color_clear.scissored_rgb, scissored_rgba and short_scissored_rgb (no colour mask) failed on both
paths. short_scissored_rgb, Linux path, c96535f1, 3 of 3: result flat 95fec7, reference flat
c89183. dEQP's own deRandom (seed deInt32Hash(iteration)), compiled on the host, gives the
failing iteration: 4 (a full clear of c89183, then a box missing the target); 95fec7 is iteration
3's picture. Replays of those calls read correctly until the real stream was captured on the board
with a scratch libGLESv2 that forwards all 298 entry points and logs them: between iterations
dEQP's framework clears (0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1) **with the scissor test still on and the previous
iteration's box**, which misses the target. That empty clear opened the frame, which then began
with a quad reloading the old colour; the full clear that followed became the frame's background
and the reload, drawn first, painted over it. `glColorMask(0,0,0,0); glClear(COLOR|DEPTH)`
before a colour clear does the same without any box. Both minimal sequences read red where
green belongs on the board. Fix ad9c54c9: such a frame ends when a colour clear arrives, and an
empty-box clear quad opens no frame; gl_test 107 "clearload" and two rig tests.
85ae2d49 corrects the empty-box check: it must judge a clear quad against the whole target, not the
application's viewport (a clear is not bounded by it); the gate caught that with
a_clear_quad_spans_the_surface_and_not_the_applications_viewport, which reads the global
load_draw and so had passed in some rows on another test's leftovers.

## AM62P, 2026-09-24 evening (am62p-board): texture, fragment_ops, the min/mag sampler fix, the 2048 L8 OOM

- **Zephyr, 5af49017, UART:** gl_test 82 fragcentre, 84 fragcoord (ES 1.00 set) and 49 es3facing
  (default set) pass. dEQP builtin_variable.frontfacing and every faceforward case pass;
  fragcoord_w and fragcoord_xyz fail: the online compiler refuses gl_FragCoord.z/.w by name
  (usc-backend's z/w planes, not on main at the time). info prints GL_VERSION "OpenGL ES 2.0
  YakoGL" and "OpenGL ES GLSL ES 1.00" (DEQP_REPORT_ES2, 5af49017's print).
- **Zephyr, ba0966d7, UART:** fragment_ops.* pass 1,325 · fail 598 · n/s 0 (Linux remote row:
  1,804/119). blend.equation_src_func_dst_func: add 210/210, subtract 15/210, reverse_subtract
  14/210; rgb_equation_alpha_equation: only add_add passes; random 0/100, interaction 1/100.
  subtract_one_one passes with pco and fails online on one module (Linux path, 44b76e1e): the
  online compiler's subtract blend variants (usc-backend). texture.* stopped at 445 cases
  (262 pass): dEQP aborts a run on the ResourceError of size.2d.2048x2048_l8 (GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY).
- **The 2048x2048 L8 OOM at 64 MiB** (Linux path, 9a484906, the case alone on a fresh module):
  "render pool exhausted: 21848 KiB requested, 8480 KiB left". The GL core stores L8 as RGBA8
  (4x) with its chain; only 8.3 MiB of the ~57 MiB pool was free before the first texture of a
  fresh process, so it is not fragmentation or a leak across cases but the standing footprint.
  The deqp image now takes a 256 MiB carveout (c2adb803); storing L8/A8/LA8 narrow and trimming
  the footprint stay driver items (am62p-board).
- **min != mag filter** (f6cb4154): the TPU picks min/mag on the CLAMPED LOD (Mesa
  pvr_arch_sampler.c:88-97); a single-level texture had maxlod 0, so it always magnified.
  filtering.2d linear_nearest/nearest_linear failed with the online and the pco compiler on one
  module (Linux path, 44b76e1e). Now maxlod LOD 1.0 when the filters differ.
- **texture.* on the Linux path, online, carveout 256:** 44b76e1e pass 573 · fail 234 (ETC1 51,
  cube 129, min≠mag ~32, completeness.2d 11, the rest); 9a484906 pass 672 · fail 135, every
  non-ETC1 min≠mag case passing (the gain includes main's other fixes). Remaining: filtering.2d
  36 (ETC1), mipmap.cube 28, size.cube 23, mipmap.2d 12, filtering.cube 12,
  specification.random_teximage2d 11, vertex.cube 6, completeness.cube 4, format.etc1 3.
  gl_test ES 1.00 set 29/29 at 9a484906.
- fragcoord_xyz with pco renders but mirrors y on the flip_y pbuffer (x and z match): the
  default-framebuffer orientation item (am62p-board).

WDOG1 confirms the 13.3 s silent stop as the PM watchdog: v3d-glue's probe build 2e166c27 (probe-wdog)
adds no fix, only heartbeat logging around the existing feed. queue1.log STAGED/BOOTED_WDOG1/
WDOG1_READY at lines 1437/1438/1439. `records/pi4/record_WDOG1_cluster_wdog1.txt` (sha256

## i.MX8MP: the uniform_api hang fixed by the descriptor write order (2026-09-29, imx8mp, cc04ba32)

The cause: a texture slot that a draw rewrote was sometimes read with the previous draw's descriptor, because each
slot's NTE_DESCRIPTOR_INVALIDATE followed its own ADDR write, interleaved with the next slot's. The vertex sampler then
sampled a stale texture, and uniform_api's two `value.assigned.by_pointer.render.{array_in_struct,struct_in_array}.
sampler2D_samplerCube_both` cases hung the GPU (MMU fault at address 0, then a recovery). Mesa writes every address of
the draw first, then every invalidate (etnaviv_texture_desc.c 605-610, Mesa main c8ce6c8bdfbb). The fix, cc04ba32
(branch imx8mp/desc-seq-land on origin/main de076373), makes that order the default (`gc_debug_desc_seq` = 1); the knob
stays for A/B (`YAKOGL_GC_DESC_SEQ`, `CONFIG_GC_GL_TEST_DESC_SEQ`; 0 = the old order). The A/B that found it (gclab
sampler_split, 2026-09-29 00:12-00:30, `records/imx8mp/sampler-desc-seq/table.txt` sha256 83df2f1cf99ddc8e): old order
vec4w 0/5 right with 5 recoveries; Mesa's order F3V1 240/240, F4V1 150/150, 0 recoveries; a descriptor-cache flush
after the writes (bit 4) did not fix it, an FE-PE stall (bit 8) did by stalling.

Board regression on the landing commit (module gcgpu.ko 15dde8082fbb from sysfs; records
`records/imx8mp/desc-seq-land/`: table.txt sha256 de3e3724bebcdf71, 44 lines; PREDICTION.txt a6b0206b924912d4, 34
lines, written before each phase; SHA256SUMS bb671d12e482645f, 59 files):

| check | predicted | result | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| dEQP uniform_api, Linux harness, default (pair cc04ba32) | 1252 / 0 / 15, 0 recoveries | **1252 / 0 / 15**, 0 recoveries, 0 MMU faults; the log shows sequence 0x1 and its counter moving | held; was 1250 / 2 / 15 on main 15dde808 (the 2 hang cases now pass); per case = the 00:36 bit-1 run in all 1267 |
| gl_test chunk 96..143, x3 default / x3 control (DESC_SEQ=0) | 0 resets on the default | 0 lost work / resets / fence timeouts in all 6 | held |
| case 100 (idxtex) in chunk 96 | 0/3 fails on the default | fails 2/3 on the default AND 2/3 on the control, each time with 113 | FALSIFIED for the default, and not bit 1's: a separate in-chunk defect (100 alone passes 4/4 on both arms) |
| case 85 (cubetail) alone x20, default | 20/20 | **20/20** | held alone (in chunk it failed in both r2 baselines); in chunk 48 it passed 1 of 2 default runs this session, 2 of 3 with the 00:52 run |
| chunk 0..47, default | = the 00:46 bit-1 run | 031f f9feff7f, 0/0/0, identical | held |
| chunk 48..95, default x2, control x1 | = 07ff | run 1 07d7 (83 and 85 not passed), run 2 07ff; control 07ff; 0/0/0 all | case 83 (pointcoord) missed once in chunk; alone 3/3 on both arms; it samples no texture, so its own draw is the same on both arms: a new in-chunk flipper, not attributed |

This is the third board for 3782b522 (Pi 4 1267/1267, AM62P 1252/0/15): no regression |

## Pi 4: packet skip by input compare (batch 94, landed) verified by gl_test and the DRAWPROF probe A/B (2026-09-29, rows-2026-09-29f)

GTPACK is gl_test's 18-case run (the same list as GTH1/GTF1/GTD1: 5, 58, 59, 66, 67, 102, 3, 9, 11, 12, 13, 4,
70, 71, 55, 142, 106, 148) on fe260113 (v3d-tex/pack-skip, on origin/main 6ee82953), one change against GTH1
(73632a6e, step (h)): `driver/src/v3d/v3d_job.c` now groups the state packets into 11 groups (CLIP, CFG,

1b63f0742398a49f, gl_test_user eb9ba1b23122c430 (4 warnings, the four unused-case ones, 0 new), staged

`completeness.attachment_combinations` set in both (an unrelated attachment-kind gap). Diffing the two fail
lists case by case: **exactly one case differs** — `dEQP-GLES2.functional.fbo.render.color.blend_tex2d_rgb` is
`Fail` with the knob on and `Pass` with it off; every other of the 56 failing cases (`render.color` 6,

These 56 (57 with the knob on) common failures are all inside `fbo.render`, the group this RESULTS.md's
mustpass sweep (line 8649, commit `2c87c2e4`, batch 28) recorded at **319/319** — a full pass. **This is a
regression against that baseline, present with the S8 knob both on and off, and neither explained nor fixed by
this batch.** `6032f456` therefore lands **opt-in, default `n`**: the S8 stencil-only path is proven correct
for the cases gl_test and the cluster demo exercise (GTDS2, GTDS3, DEMODS2 above), but the pre-existing
`fbo.render` regression stays open and blocks turning the knob on by default; the one-case blend_tex2d_rgb
difference between the two arms is likewise unexplained, with a determinism rerun pending. **Nothing the suite
covers regressed by turning the S8 knob on or off — but the fbo.render group itself is NOT "nothing regressed"
against the 2c87c2e4 baseline; that regression is open, being bisected.**

cap — the render pool runs out first.** dmesg: `pvrgpu: render pool exhausted: 1444 KiB requested, 1356 KiB
left` (DSS2 168; DSS 168: `780 KiB left`), after the process holds 27,904 KiB at close (`close: reclaimed 77
allocations (27904 KiB) ...`); gl_test's other processes hold 20,854-21,117 KiB at their own close. The pool the
client sees is ~27,904 + 1,356 = **29,260 KiB of the 64 MiB carve-out** (the rest unaccounted by any line read
so far). Arithmetic against a hypothetical 16-slot cap (raised from 8, mirroring the Pi 4's DS-cap fix): a
1024x600 slot is 1024x608x4 = 2,490,368 bytes; 8 slots = 19.0 MiB, 16 slots = **38.0 MiB — more than the ~29 MiB
client-usable pool holds**, so raising the slot count changes nothing on this board until the render pool itself
grows: **the render pool binds before the 8-slot cap does.**

### AM62P finding (open, no fix): MMUCACHE ack not seen after a 167 -> 168 sequence

`records/am62p/mmuack-e6a44220/` (154 files + INDEX.txt, sha256 -c OK; martian-packet IPs redacted `<ADDR>`),
module `e51d057fb94a`, `do_boot=1`, params as the DSC/DSS row, pair `e6a44220` staged fresh (board sha256 =
host) each session, holders clear before and restored after (`pvrgpu` out, `pvrsrvkm` in, refcnt 0). Three
sessions, one continuous `dmesg -w` capture each:

- DSM (07:05-07:07, one module load, 168/162 alternated x20): `render: MMUCACHE ack not seen (sync=10 want=11)`
  **0/20 on 168, 0/20 on 162** — not an exposure measure, since the 600x600 HWRT pair is made once per load (2
  "HWRT 600x600" lines in the whole session; runs 2-20 reuse it).
- DSX (07:08-07:15, **20 fresh loads**, each running 162 -> 167 -> 168 in order): **20/20 on 168** (every one
  `sync=10 want=11`), **0/20 on 162, 0/20 on 167**.
- DSY (07:16-07:18, 6 fresh loads): 162 -> 168 **0/3**; 167 -> 168 **3/3** (`sync=7 want=8`).

Rate: the miss is deterministic exactly for a case-167-then-168 sequence in a fresh load (23 of 23 such
sequences across DSS/DSM/DSX/DSY combined), and never fires for 162-then-168 or for 162/167 alone. Timing (DSX,
20/20): the miss lands 100.7-100.8 ms after the first `HWRT 600x600` line (the full 100 ms wait) and 12.4-13.4
ms before the case's own `render pool exhausted` line, so the render-pool path is not the cause (the pool line
follows because the case then allocates its next layer). All 23 of these runs PASS and read back their layers
correctly (0 MISMATCH); **0 MMU faults, HWR counter 0 at every load, every close line `dropped 0 KiB`.**

Mechanism (source of the loaded module, `e51d057f:driver/src/pvr_render.c`, unchanged at `d7e09db3`/`e6a44220`):
`mmu_cache_sync()` (1197-1236) takes the dirty flag (1201), gates on it (1207), posts a KCCB `MMUCACHE`
invalidate naming the next sequence number `want` (1210-1219), waits up to 100 ms (2000 x 50 us, 1224-1233) for
the firmware to write `want` into the sync word, then `LOG_WRN`s and **returns regardless** (1235); the caller
(1370) posts the GEOM/FRAG kicks next (1424-1429) — **the kick proceeds after an unacknowledged invalidate.**
`sync=10 want=11` means the firmware wrote the previous sequence number and not this one inside the 100 ms
window. What 168 does that 162 does not: it is the load's first 600x600 target (a fresh HWRT pair — TPC, VHEAP,
region headers, macrotile, MList all newly mapped, so its kick's invalidate is actually sent) with the render
pool nearly full; but 168 alone after a load, and 162 -> 168, do not miss — the trigger needs a case-167 process
(stencil-only `STENCIL_INDEX8` framebuffers, `INCR` stencil, scissored clears) earlier in the same load, and
which part of that shape triggers it is not yet known. **Under investigation; no fix proposed yet** (a minimal
repro — two processes per fresh load, a stencil-only prep then a single big 600x600 kick — is sketched but not
written).

## Batch 100: V3D step (m) filter_image vs Mesa + step (o) hoist-window count; AM62P MMUCACHE ack instrument (origin/main 222cfba6)

`origin/main` 222cfba6 = `v3d-m5/stepm` `68a83016` (V3D: step (m), narrows femtovg's `filter_image` against Mesa's
fixture program word by word — a plain MOV that ends its source gets that source's register directly, a uniform
load defers into the loop instead of the block, and a back edge's flag push moves ahead of the work its delay
slots can take) + `91714d01` (V3D: step (o), instruments `sched.rs` hoist's 32-word window with a
`hoists`/`window_cuts` counter, host-test builds only; base `4ed373eb`) + `am62p/ds-slots` `0fc16c73` + `d3acec27`
(PowerVR: `mmuack_probe`, a two-process host tool built to reproduce a MMUCACHE-ack-miss shape) + `c7877c15`
(PowerVR: `pvr_render.c` module parameter `mmu_ack_probe`, print-only, logs every MMUCACHE post's ack timing and
