`records/pi4/record_FBOR1_deqp_fbor1.txt` (sha256 a1848b32cee613ca, 1679 lines), the same filter on `b685bbb9`
(batch 77b, *after* the async-swap commit `6b6ec1e1` — "two arena sets, submit without waiting"): also **319
passed / 0 failed / 0 not supported**, 0 MMU faults, 0 recoveries.

**This rules out `6b6ec1e1`'s async swap as the regression's cause**: `b685bbb9` already carries it and still
passes `fbo.render` in full. The flip to the 56-failure shape therefore lies somewhere between `b685bbb9` and the
batch 99 tip `99c95c07` (candidates: batch 83, 94b, or 99) — bisect continuing (FBOR2..FBOR4 queued).
**`ef975a69` (`v3d/fbo-render-wait`, `tex_state_for` waits for a pending `target_kick` before tiling) is a real,
host-pinned latent race in the V3D texture-tiling path, proven on the host rig, but has NOT been shown to be the
cause of this regression** — it was proposed on the theory the async swap was the cause, and that theory is what
FBOR0/FBOR1 rule out; `ef975a69` remains unconfirmed on the board either way.

### AM62P: the MMUCACHE ack arrives with the next doorbell (instrument `c7877c15`, module `222cfba6bf47`)

`records/am62p/mmuack-probe/` (module e51d057fb94a, libraries = `e6a44220`'s; sessions MAP 07:26-07:33 and MAI
07:37-07:46, `0fc16c73`/`d3acec27`, 207 files + INDEX.txt, sha256 -c OK) built `mmuack_probe`, a host tool with two
arms: A = n framebuffers (stencil|depth|colour) of a given size, clear + one draw each, glFinish per FBO or not;
B = one colour+`STENCIL_INDEX8` framebuffer, clear + `INCR` draw + glFinish, at a chosen size. 0 MMU faults, HWR
counter 0, every close line `dropped 0` across all 66 fresh loads in both sessions. Arm table (misses per fresh
load): A of any single size/kind repeated x2 through x7 into B never misses (0/3 in every such row); **A run
exactly once (x1) into a *new* render-target size (B) misses 3/3 every time**, independent of attachment kind, B's
size, or glFinish in A (`stencil x1 -> B600` 3/3 twice, `depth x1 -> B600` 3/3, `colour x1 -> B600` 3/3,
`stencil x1 -> B128` 3/3, `stencil x1 no finish -> B600` 3/3); gl_test's own `167 -> 168` sequence also misses 3/3
(`want=8`). Not a factor: attachment kind, target size, `glFinish`, pool pressure (x1 misses with no pool
failure). A factor: A's *count* specifically, and not monotonically (x1 misses; x2..x7, and gl_test 167's 7
framebuffers, do not) — something counted (a KCCB position, a sequence number), not the GL shape.

`records/am62p/mmuack-instr/` (module `222cfba6bf47`, sha256 afa60d4a002d192b..., 9 build warnings matching the
tree's baseline, 0 in the changed files; session MIA 08:03:06-08:06:55, one continuous dmesg capture, 46 files +
INDEX.txt, sha256 -c OK, `mmucache_lines.txt` = every MMUCACHE line with its marker) ran `pvr_render.c`'s own
`mmu_ack_probe` module parameter (default 0, print-only: every MMUCACHE post logs `want=N slot=S acked after U
us`; a miss adds the KCCB read/write offsets and the sync word at +10 ms/+50 ms, plus a read after the following
kick's doorbell) against the same arms, fresh load per trial (n1/n2/n5 = probe A stencil xN 64x64 -> probe B
600x600, x3 each; G167->G168 x3; G162 alone x1). Every process exit 0; 0 MMU faults, HWR counter 0 at 13/13 loads,
0 fence timeouts, every close line `dropped 0`. Misses: n1 3/3 (`want=2`, slot 5), `G167->G168` 3/3 (`want=8`,
slot 24); n2 0/3, n5 0/3, `G162` alone 0/1 — the same shape as the probe-only session. Every miss reads, verbatim:

```
render: MMUCACHE ack not seen (sync=1 want=2)
render: MMUCACHE probe: miss want=2 slot=5: KCCB r/w=6/6 rtn[slot]=0x0
render: MMUCACHE probe: want=2: sync +10 ms=1 +50 ms=1; want NOT seen within 50 ms; KCCB r/w=6/6
render: MMUCACHE probe: want=2 after the kick doorbell: sync=2 (seen, 1 ms)
```

(`G167->G168`: the same shape at `sync=7 want=8`, slot=24, r/w=25/25.) The firmware had *taken* the command (read
offset = write offset) but not executed it — no return flag, sync unchanged after 150 ms — and executed it within
1 ms of the *next* doorbell (the following kick): **late, not lost; released by the next doorbell, not by a
timer.**

Second finding, across every process in the session: the first invalidate of a process is acked in 50 us (19 of
25) or missed (6 of 25); **every later invalidate in the same process is acked 98.0-98.6 ms afterward, in 42 of 48
cases** (the other 6 at 7.4-77 ms, right after a miss). Example (`G162` alone): `want=1` at slot 3 acks in 50 us,
then `want=2..10` (slots 5..21) each ack 98.2-98.55 ms later — about 0.9 s of accumulated busy-wait inside one
gl_test case. 98 ms sits just under the driver's own 100 ms wait timeout, and the runtime's `ActivePMLatency` is
also 100 ms (`e51d057f:driver/src/pvr_fw_boot.c`, `ui32ActivePMLatencyms = 100`); the (untested) hypothesis is
that a command posted while the firmware is in its post-activity idle window is not acted on until that window's
own ~100 ms timer or a new doorbell, and a miss is the case where the timer doesn't release it either.

DDK facts, read for ABI comparison only (`ti-img-rogue-driver-25.2`, nothing transcribed): the DDK's pre-kick path
posts `MMUCACHE` with `bInterrupt FALSE` and kicks immediately after, **never waiting on the host**
(`RGXPreKickCacheCommand`, `services/server/devices/rgxmem.c:351-374`; caller `rgxfwutils.c:4604-4608`); where the
DDK *does* wait, its test is "counter advanced" (`PVRSRVHasCounter32Advanced`, `>=`, wrap-aware,
`rgxmem.c:316-319`), never equality — ours tests `*mc_sync == want` (`e51d057f:driver/src/pvr_render.c`
`mmu_cache_sync`, 1197-1236, 1229). `mmu_cache_sync` takes the dirty flag, posts the invalidate naming the next
sequence number, waits up to 100 ms, then `LOG_WRN`s and **returns regardless** (1235) — the kick proceeds after
an unacknowledged invalidate either way.

Why we wait at all: `driver/docs/HANDOFF.md` ("The render stall: the MMUCACHE acknowledgement wait
(2026-09-22)", 775-800) records that the wait had once been deleted (`06bbb93`) on the claim that "the firmware
runs its command queue in order, so a command posted before the kicks is finished before them", and quotes the
refutation: **"The first claim is false — posting gets a KCCB command *accepted*, not *completed*, and the kick
does not travel that path all the way to the hardware, so the fragment phase can start against a stale TLB and
its fence never signals."** Reverting that one deletion took gl_test case 7 "from 7 fence timeouts / 0 passing
cases to 0 timeouts / 31 passing" (`pvr_render.c` comment, 1178-1186). HANDOFF's own matrix (a separate
measurement, `driver/docs/HANDOFF.md` 814-828, workload `hwrt_thrash 5 4`) isolates the wait as the decisive
variable: with a combined kick, flipping only `mmu_ack` moves fence timeouts **0 against 18**; on the two-kick
path, flipping only `mmu_ack` moves them **4 against a total wedge**.

This leaves a tension the STATE records but does not resolve: the DDK's firmware relies on exactly the in-order
guarantee HANDOFF calls false for our driver — either the DDK's firmware path differs from ours (something sent
with the kick that we don't send), or the in-order claim is true and our fence timeouts had a different cause the
wait also happened to hide. **Open, no fix proposed**: the options once this instrument's late-vs-never answer was
in hand were to keep equality, switch to `>=`, or find the reason our driver needs the wait that the DDK doesn't
— this batch answers late-vs-never (late), but does not pick among those three; **no behaviour change in this
batch**. Every miss case across both sessions still reads back correctly (0 MISMATCH), 0 MMU faults, 0 recoveries
throughout. Also noted: independent of whether a miss ever fires, this ~98 ms deferral costs every later MMUCACHE
invalidate on this board roughly 98 ms today.

### i.MX8MP: batch 1 of the dEQP-GLES2 residue, whole tree on Zephyr at `04a0e2c2` (2026-09-30, gc-es2)

Branch gc/es2-batch1 = merge `04a0e2c2` of gc/points-frontfacing-interaction (336edcf5, 69ee9565, 6e0a7975 on
703c10c4) and gc/loops-tmparray-invariance (7e2431fc, 55453e43), both on origin/main 2362422d. Not pushed.
Evidence: records/imx8mp/batch1-04a0e2c2/ (SHA256SUMS sha256 d878bf359e5d0589, 94 lines: jump logs, predictions
written before each run, tables, the per-entry mustpass counts, rows logs, the host dumpers and their shaders).

**Causes, one line each:**
- rasterization.limits.points (336edcf5): the GC7000 does not clamp a point to the reported maximum (64); dEQP's
  size-80 point was drawn at 80. Mesa etnaviv reports 8192 and relies on the hardware clamp, which the case can reach
  only through an 8200-wide framebuffer (ours stop at 4096). The online compiler now clamps gl_PointSize to [1, 64].
- builtin_variable.frontfacing (69ee9565): gl_FrontFacing's sense is compiled in, one binary per winding
  (f490f24b), but only the offline table had the twins; the online compiler never set reads_front_facing and refused
  the SHC_VIV_KEY_FRONT_FLIPPED key, so both windings read one way. The flipped key now compiles cmp.eq for cmp.ne.
- fragment_ops.interaction.basic_shader.16/61/63/84 and random.all_features.fragment.98, random.conditionals.vertex.67
  (6e0a7975): a store whose value already sits in the output's register (`d = e`, `gl_FragColor = v`) emitted
  nothing; with a second store to the same output the register was not kept to the end (`d = f; d = e;` compiled to
  `mov t1, t2`). Found by generating the cases' shaders on the host with dEQP's own rsg generator and running them
  through tests/backend_differential: exactly these shaders differ from their IR (plus interaction 76/98, which draw
  right by luck); with the guard all agree, and with it switched off fragment.98 and vertex.67 differ again.
  fragment.98 also evaluates `cos(0.0)` at run time (constant transcendentals are not folded on the GC7000 path);
  on this shader that value does not reach the output, so it is not the cause -- a latent risk, not fixed.
- tmp_array vec2/vec3_const_write_static_loop_read_vertex (7e2431fc): vec2/vec3 literal seeds (masked writes) were
  not folded into immediates; 45 temporaries against the vertex stage's 21, "Failed to compile".
- invariance.{highp,mediump,lowp}.loop_2 (7e2431fc): a placed output written only in a loop arm was not live across
  the back edge; the loop-top copy took gl_Position's register.

Merge check: the two changes do not meet (folding rewrites reads of virtual seeds after selection; the single-store
guard decides stores of input registers to fixed outputs during selection). On the merge the 200 interaction shaders
and the 6 minimal shapes still agree in the differential. No pin moved from the combination: backend_differential
228 / 138 and lane_move_equivalence 123 hold as each branch set them.

Rows on 04a0e2c2: fmt ok; clippy -D warnings 0 on host-test+gpu-vivante, +shaderc-online, +shaderc-online+report-es2,

### i.MX8MP: Sixteen vertex texture units on the i.MX8MP, and uniform_api.random.3's constant file (2026-10-01, gc-vsunits)

Branch gc/vs-units16-on on origin/main fe5e8e73: e730b844 (YAKOGL_GC_VS_UNITS16=0|1 in the linux and gcgpu OSALs, so
the host pair and the board's Linux harness can set the switch), **1d4c899a** (the fix below), f45c758f (clippy),
**5613f379** (16 by default). Background: 9ca5c0e5 / f1114761 / 045a118d put 16 vertex units behind
`gc_debug_vs_units16` (off). An earlier switch-on board run (agent ae7038a3) had case 149 PASS in ten runs and
uniform_api 1,266 / 1 / 0 with `uniform_api.random.3` failing; its notes and image hashes were no longer on disk, so
the ten 149 runs were repeated below at 5613f379.

**random.3's cause.** With 8 units the case is NotSupported ("13 vertex texture units required, 8 supported"), so its
program had never been compiled on the GC7000. Host (tools/cts/host-deqp-run.sh with YAKOGL_GC_VS_UNITS16=1; the
.qpa has the sources): the vertex shader samples 13 samplers in structs and arrays of structs (cubes on units 0 and
7..12, 2D on 1..6), no fragment sampler, and compares about 150 uniforms against literals. Compiled by the online
back end it is 2,879 instructions, 5 temporaries, and a constant file of **1,100 dwords = 275 vec4 registers** (696
dwords of uniforms, 404 of literals). `emit_stage_uniforms` (vivante/shader.rs) cut the file at
`GC_MAX_UNIFORM_DWORDS` = 1024 in one LOAD_STATE, so registers 256..274 were never written, and the compares that read
them failed: the Linux harness (pair e448c868c9dfc087 at e730b844, module e730b84466b3, switch on) drew the 32x32
result all black, "FAILURE: image comparison failed, got 1024 non-white pixels", 0 fence timeouts, 0 recoveries.
(A count of 1024 also does not fit the header's ten-bit count field: it sets the FIXP bit instead.) Not a sampler
mapping error (TEX_ID 0..12 in order, VS_SAMPLER_BASE 0), not the temporaries, not the instruction count. Mesa gives
each stage 256 registers on this core (min(512, 320 - 64), etnaviv_screen.c:821-823) and would refuse this shader; the
hardware file is 320 registers for both stages (hwdb gc7000ULN_v123 NumberOfConstants 0x140).

**Fix (1d4c899a).** `GC_MAX_UNIFORM_DWORDS` is the shared file, 320 x 4; each stage writes its share in LOAD_STATEs of
at most 256 dwords; the link (shaderc/online/backend.rs) refuses a program whose two constant files exceed 320
registers ("the constant registers the two stages need (vertex V, fragment F: uniforms and literals) exceed the 320
this GPU has") instead of a draw dropping registers. Host tests: `a_vertex_constant_file_past_256_registers_is_written_whole`
(every one of 1,100 dwords, the counts, PS_UNIFORM_BASE 275; fails with the old 1024),
`a_vertex_shader_with_more_than_256_constant_registers_links`, `a_program_whose_constant_files_exceed_the_gc7000_file_is_refused_at_link`.

## Batches 102-104: AM62P MMU-cache ack instruments and the ActivePMLatency finding

`am62p/pm-latency` `ba51b565` (pm_latency_ms parameter + in-order instrument) lands as `origin/main` `1f674faa`
(batch 102); `am62p/ack-advanced` `293b39ed` (wrap-safe `>=` ack test, fence-based in-order marks,
`mmu_ack_reping`, pm default 100) lands as `8dcc8603` (batch 103); `bffd18e7` ("pvr: ActivePMLatency default back
to 100 ms (293b39ed flipped it by mistake)") is batch 104, a direct fix on top of `8dcc8603` restoring the
intended default. **`ba51b565`, `293b39ed` and `bffd18e7` are all on `origin/main`; `ff062a35` (the 5 ms default +
Zephyr Kconfig plumbing) is NOT.**

### pm_latency_ms + no-wait arms, and the design recommendation

`records/am62p/pm-latency/` (77 files + INDEX.txt, sha256 -c OK). Module `1f674faa7d4e` (27/27 loads), gl_test_user
+ `mmuack_probe` pair, one dmesg capture per arm, 3 fresh loads per arm. Whole session: 0 MMU faults, HWR counter
0 at 27/27 loads, 0 fence timeouts, every close `dropped 0`, every process exit 0. The measured table: a process's
first invalidate acks in <1 ms or misses 3/3 (unaffected by latency); **every later invalidate's ack is deferred by
almost exactly `ActivePMLatency`: median 98.45 ms at 100 ms, 18.95 ms at 20 ms, 4.10 ms at 5 ms** (minus ~1-1.5 ms).
The miss itself (n1: A run once into a new render target) stays 3/3 at every latency — the deferral tracks the PM
window, the miss does not. Instrument limit found and stated as such: the KCCB return slots are never set for
MMUCACHE or KICK (rtn 0 in 66/66 loads), so the in-order verdict is "unknown" in the miss cases; the earlier
inference that "the render very probably ran before its invalidate completed" could not be confirmed from this
session alone (withdrawn below). Recommendation written down (no behaviour change in this batch): keep the wait
(`mmu_ack=1`); lower the default `pm_latency_ms` (opt-in first, default only after a regression set); switch the
ack test to `>=` (harmless, matches the DDK's `PVRSRVHasCounter32Advanced`); leave the miss itself open (candidate:
re-ring the KCCB doorbell during the ack wait).

### Regression set at pm_latency_ms=5

`records/am62p/pm5-regset/` (22 files + INDEX.txt, sha256 -c OK). Module `1f674faa` (sysfs `1f674faa7d4e`), default
pair plus a `YAKOGL_PENDING_FREES_WAIT=1` pair, three fresh loads per latency (`pool_frag 256`, `gl_test_user 7`,
`hwrt_thrash 5 4`, `pending_thrash` default and wait arms) at `pm_latency_ms=5` against a `pm_latency_ms=100`
control in the same session. Nothing the set covers moved: `gl_test_user 7` 37/38 (46) at both latencies, 0 lines
differ per-line against the DSC-7 baseline (6 lines are stdout/stderr interleave timing, not content); `hwrt_thrash
5 4` PASS (5 rounds, 0 wrong renders) at both; `pending_thrash` default/wait rows identical; 0 ack misses, 0 fence
timeouts, HWR counter 0, 0 MMU faults at both latencies. Elapsed time: gl_test 7 ran in ~2 s at pm 5 versus ~5 s at
pm 100. **Verdict: DEFAULT-READY for the Linux harness** — power/thermal cost of the shorter latency and the n1
miss (unchanged by latency) are explicitly not covered.

### mmu_ack_reping + fence-mark in-order arms

`records/am62p/reping/` (68 files + INDEX.txt, sha256 -c OK). Module `8dcc86034c20` (21/21 loads, every insmod
passed `pm_latency_ms=100` explicitly so the rows do not depend on main's default), 3 fresh loads per arm. **Re-
ring releases nothing**: the misses stay 3/3 at both 1 and 5 rings, and the ordinary deferrals still end at the
same ~98 ms whether 19 or 98 rings came first before it; the instrument's "released by re-ring after K ring(s)"
wording over-claims (it prints whenever rings > 0, not causally). What does release a miss is the kick's own post
(a new KCCB command), not a bare doorbell. **In-order, using the render service's fence as the kick mark: wherever
both marks were seen (38 kicks), the invalidate's sync came first, ~30 us after the post, the geometry fence
~120 us later — yes in 38/38.** The remaining 28 kicks are "unknown" (no fence appeared within 200 ms although
every process completed with no timeout — the whole kick ran past the 200 ms window). In the 6 miss cases the
kick's fence was ALSO absent for 200 ms, so **the earlier inference from the pm-latency session ("the render very
probably ran before its invalidate completed") is not supported by this data and is withdrawn.**

### Process error: 293b39ed carried the pm_latency default flip

A `git reset --soft` split of one commit into (a)(b)(c)+(d) left `pvr_fw_boot.c`/`pvr_drv.h` staged with the old
content while the working tree was restored by hand; the diff was checked against the working tree, not the
index. Result: `293b39ed` (now `origin/main` `8dcc8603`) actually set `pvr_fw_pm_latency_ms = 5` and `pvr_drv.h`
said "default 5", while `pvr_mod.c`'s own description string still said "(default 100)" — the earlier "modinfo
default 100" row came from a working-tree build, not from the commit. Every AM62P build from `origin/main` >=
`8dcc8603` (Linux module and Zephyr images) booted with `ActivePMLatency 5 ms` until `bffd18e7` ("pvr:
ActivePMLatency default back to 100 ms (293b39ed flipped it by mistake)", batch 104) restored the intended 100 ms
default. **Lesson recorded for next time: after any reset/split, `git diff --cached` before commit and `git show
--stat <hash>` after, and quote rows from a clean checkout of the hash, not a working tree.**

### The 5 ms default and the Zephyr run

`am62p/pm5-flip` `ff062a35` (on `origin/main` `bffd18e7`, **not on main, not pushed**) sets `PVR_FW_PM_LATENCY_MS`
and the matching Kconfig default to 5. Zephyr images built from a clean `ff062a35` checkout: `glt5` (5 ms,
`83fe2945b0ce94e2`) run on the board 09:08:33-09:12:41 (kexec, RUN_BOUND 240 s): firmware logs `ActivePMLatency 5
ms`, gl_test **37/38 (46)**, 1737 gl_test lines, **0 differ against the last Zephyr baseline** (PPM-GLT), HWR 0,
fence timeouts 0, resets 0, ack misses 0; pending-frees high-water 98/128, ds slots peak 3/8. A control `glt100`
image (`80e57df4d843b10b`) was built but **not run**, so the 5 ms/100 ms comparison is not yet side by side on
Zephyr itself. **With the Linux regression set already default-ready, this Zephyr run is the evidence gathered so
far for landing `ff062a35`; it has not landed.**

## Batch 105: AM62P netboot host tooling + Z1 RTI self-arm (origin/main `8b854b9d`)

`am62p/netboot` lands as `origin/main` `8b854b9d`, carrying `driver/docs/am62p-netboot-plan.md` (since 2026-10-11
`tools/cts/log/board-sessions/am62p-netboot.md`; the design and
host tooling; nothing run on the board) and `ed5d47d4` ("am62p Z1: the image arms the RTI watchdog itself", build
only, default off).

### U-Boot facts and the one-shot design

Read from the board (Linux, read-only) and the U-Boot binary/UART log (`records/am62p/netboot/env-2026-09-29.txt`
sha256 `6b62d72f053dc6f5`, 52 lines; `uboot-control-dt-2026-09-29.dts`; `uboot-boot-sample-uart-v16.log`): U-Boot
`2024.04-ti-g11cb0162a795`, one (non-redundant) env copy, `bootdelay=0`, no watchdog driver of any kind, and **no
`tftpdstp` — U-Boot always sends to UDP port 69**. SafeUI's own boot doc had misread a "Could not get PHY" line as
"U-Boot's Ethernet does not work"; the error is on the unused second port (PHY addr 7), not the one in use (`eth0
[PRIME]`, PHY addr 0) — whether `dhcp`/`tftpboot` actually work over it is still unmeasured, the plan's first board
step. The one-shot design (the AM62P netboot runner, `tools/tftp_oneshot.py`, `tools/am62p_netboot_uart.py`): a
`yako_hook` in `bootcmd` that fires only when `yako_once` is set, deletes and saves that variable before touching
the network (so a failed run can't loop), then DHCPs and TFTPs the named image and `go`s it; any fetch failure
falls through to the old `bootcmd` (Linux). Host-side self-tests (all on this host, nothing installed or changed
system-wide): `tftp_oneshot.py --self-test` 17 checks, 20/20 PASS (block sizes, lost packets, stale-file and
re-request refusal); an independent `curl tftp://` client fetched a real 16,107,024-byte Zephyr image byte-equal
at both 512- and 1468-byte blocks; `am62p_netboot_uart.py --self-test` 17-18 checks, 20/20 PASS, plus a replay of a
real saved kexec UART log (295/295 lines stamped, byte-equal).

### Cycle time (measured base + prediction)

Measured (a back-to-back kexec chain, `g3-396d667a`, img5-img23): the next jump starts at Linux uptime **32-48 s,
mostly 32-38 s** — about 35 s of that is the Linux leg (boot + `systemctl is-system-running`), plus ~2.75 s of
firmware before the Zephyr banner. **The one-shot alone does not make a single cycle faster: it still reboots
through Linux on the way back, trading kexec's jump for a reboot, not saving time — the gain is a cleaner hardware
state.** The ~35 s/image saving is reachable only in a designed-but-unwritten **chain mode** (a persistent
`yako_chain` flag + a TFTP queue, ~300-350 lines, about a working day plus one ~30-minute board session), which
skips the intermediate Linux boots entirely: predicted ~5-10 s of boot legs per image instead of ~38 s, about 30 s
saved per image, ~15 minutes over a 30-image dEQP chain.

### Two blockers

**Port 69 needs the user's OK**: this host has no TFTP daemon capable of binding privileged ports as this user
(uid 1000, `ip_unprivileged_port_start=1024`); every option (run the server as root, `setcap` a python copy, lower
the sysctl, or a host-network container) changes something about this host and needs sign-off before it is tried.
**Z1 (`CONFIG_YAKOGL_AM62P_RTI_SELF_ARM`, default n) is built but not run on the board**: under `go`, nobody starts
the RTI watchdog (this U-Boot has no watchdog driver at all), so an image entered by netboot must arm it itself
before any unattended netboot run is allowed — `ed5d47d4` does that (TISCI device 125 on, clock parent set from a
measured 32768 Hz, preload/window/NMI programmed, then fed until `CONFIG_YAKOGL_AM62P_WDT_SECONDS`; any refusal
resets the SoC at once). **The kexec (control) gl_test image is byte-identical (same sha256) before and after the
Kconfig change**, so existing kexec images do not change; deqp/gl_femtovg/gl_slint/gl_triangle configure-only
builds differ by exactly the one new Kconfig line. Board steps (the `probe`/RTI-proof/gl_test-under-netboot
sequence in the plan's section 7) have **not been run**.

1680 lines) were built to test the OSAL change **`679be18d` ("v3d OSAL: the render starts from the binner's
interrupt")** as the candidate cause. **Both pass 319 passed / 0 failed, 0 recoveries** — this refutes the
`679be18d` hypothesis (the commit is already on `origin/main`, part of batch 83, and does not reproduce the
failure by itself or with its parent). **The flip therefore lies in a later commit inside `679be18d..a62527ae`
(the rest of batch 83's ~18 commits); the board bisect continues with FBOR2d and further arms, and the triggering
commit is not yet known.**

### The two fixes

Independent of which batch-83 commit turns out to be the trigger, two host-pinned races in the async-swap-era
texture-tiling path are proven fixes for the failure *shape* itself: `v3d/fbo-render-wait` **`ef975a69`**
(`tex_state_for` waits for a submitted, pending `target_kick` before tiling): FBOR5
(`records/pi4/record_FBOR5_deqp_fbor5.txt`, sha256 `1a61e2cef4bed60a`, 1687 lines) **303 passed / 16 failed** —
**removes 40 of the 56 on the board**. DEMOFW1 (`records/pi4/record_DEMOFW1_cluster_demofw1.txt`, sha256
`044f9a2c8e0c97cf`, 1011 lines): cluster demo 180 s **PASS**, 24043 frames, 133.3 fps, crc32 `0xf59828d6`, 0 GL
error, 0 recoveries — the wait costs the cluster nothing measurable.

The remaining 16 (all 12 `resize.tex2d_*` cases, every colour format with and without depth/stencil, plus 4 of the
6 `color.blend_*_depth_component16` cases) share a second, narrower gap in the same wait: the GL core stamps a
render target with the backend's `kick_id()` before the backend sees the draw; when that draw ends the job the
*previous* target opened, `InFlight` only tracks the job's own kick, so once the job is submitted `kick_pending`
asks about the wrong (already-completed) job and answers false — the wait is skipped exactly for renders whose
draw ended the previous job (a sequence question, not a format one: e.g. `resize.tex2d_*`'s first render follows
the previous case's window-clear job). `v3d/fbo-render-alias` **`02f369a9`** (parent `ef975a69`) is **predicted to
remove the rest** by carrying the alias forward so `kick_pending`/`v3d_wait_kick` answer for the job that stamped
the target, not just the job in flight — proof is FBOR6 (pending, no board result yet). **Both `ef975a69` and
`02f369a9` are host-proven (host-test/V3D-lib rows all 0 failures); `ef975a69` alone is board-proven via
FBOR5/DEMOFW1; `02f369a9` is not yet board-run. Neither is on `origin/main`.**

### Still running

FBOR2d and further arms (narrowing the trigger inside `679be18d..a62527ae`), FBOR6 (`02f369a9`, predicted
319/319), GTFW1/GTFW2 (gl_test on the `ef975a69`/alias tip, predicted 21/21) and DEMOFW2 (cluster on the alias tip,
predicted PASS matching DEMOFW1) are built or queued but have no board result yet — the bisect (which commit
triggers the regression) and the landing case (`ef975a69` alone, then `02f369a9` after FBOR6+GTFW2+DEMOFW2) are
both open.

### i.MX8MP: the 19 QualityWarnings are the GC7000's, not ours (2026-09-30, gc-qw)

Measured on NXP's own driver for the same GPU: galcore + the product image's libEGL/libGLESv2, reporting
`Vivante Corporation` / `Vivante GC7000UL` / `OpenGL ES 3.1 V6.4.11.p2.745085`. The deqp-gles2 binary our Linux
harness uses was run through tools/cts/vendor-deqp.sh (ec0f3537): the product image, a libEGL shim for the GBM display.
Our arm is the same binary on the Linux harness: gcgpu.ko d1350ee9faf8 and the ES2 online pair built at d1350ee9. The
vendor cube run was repeated through the committed script, with the same statuses and faces. Evidence:
records/imx8mp/qw-vendor-d1350ee9/ (summary.txt sha256 8435ba79436c1350, 73 lines; the four qpa files with images,
sha256 905b262b49ca956c vendor cube, 91c351493bdb4e81 ours cube, 40febd6817e68407 vendor interpolation,
fa0eadf3c2c0c070 ours interpolation). No code change follows. The Zephyr results by name stand as measured at 04a0e2c2
(SEL 30, `PP???PPPPP?????P?P??????????`) and are the same names as both Linux arms below.

**A. texture.mipmap.cube.generate (14 QualityWarning, l8_nicest and la88_nicest Pass).**
- What earns what (gluTextureTestUtil.cpp compareGenMipmapResult, cube). Each level and face is read back by
  rendering it with NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST into a viewport of the level's size. dEQP places that viewport at random,
  seeded from a hash of the case name, level and face. Level N is then checked against a bilinear, then a box filter of
  the read-back level N-1. Failing both is a QualityWarning; failing the very-lenient min/max check is a Fail.
- Vendor and ours give the same status for all 16 cases. The warned faces are identical too, e.g. a8_fastest
  +X/+Y/+Z, la88_fastest +Y. Each warned face has exactly one wrong pixel at level 3, which also shows at level 4.
- On both drivers that pixel is (0,0) of the level-3 read-back, in all 28 warned faces. It holds the level-4 50/50 mix.
  dEQP's 8x8 checker on a 64x64 face makes level 3 the only level whose texels differ from the next level's:
  levels 0-2 are pure cell colours, levels 4-6 are all 50/50 mixes. So a corner pixel sampling one level too coarse
  is visible only there. The texture unit's cube LOD at the viewport corner does this, not the generated chain.
  Which faces it hits follows the viewport placement, i.e. the case name. That is why the "format" pattern (two
  nicest cases pass) is the same on both drivers. 2D generate has no face change around a corner and passes.
- The chain itself: every Result image of the five 8-bit formats is pixel-identical to the vendor's (max 1 LSB). The
  16-bit formats differ only in the 50/50 mixes of levels 4-6. There we read back exact 0.5 (128) and the vendor a
  native step (565: 123/36 vs 128/39; 4444: 119/204 vs 128/213; 5551 alpha 0 or 255 vs 128): our chain keeps 8 bits
  for them. dEQP accepts both, and it is not what earns the warning.
- Mesa's CI cannot say either way: deqp-runner counts a QualityWarning as a pass-like Warn, and expectation files list
  only Fail/Flake. etnaviv-gc7000-r6204-{fails,flakes}.txt name none of these cases.

**B. rasterization.interpolation lines (5 QualityWarning: basic.{line_strip,line_strip_wide,lines},
projected.{lines,lines_wide}).**
- The verifier (tcuRasterizationVerifier.cpp verifyLineGroupInterpolation) accepts as strict t = dot(p - a, b - a) /
  |b - a|^2, perpendicular to the line. It then falls back to t = (p - a)[major] / (b - a)[major], weights projected
  on the major axis. That is what a line drawn as a minor-axis parallelogram with triangle interpolation produces.
  Passing only the fallback is "Interpolation was calculated using projected coordinates". Which case warns depends on
  the random line geometry per case, hence the mixed pattern.
- Vendor: the three narrow warnings are the same names (basic.line_strip, basic.lines, projected.lines). The three
  narrow passes are the same (basic.line_loop, projected.line_loop, projected.line_strip). All six wide cases are
  NotSupported there ("Support for line width 5 is required"). Every Result image, lines and triangles, matches ours
  within 1 LSB with identical coverage. Same rasterizer, same interpolation.
- Wide lines: we program what Mesa does on this core (PA_CONFIG WIDE_LINE, PA_LINE_WIDTH and PA_WIDE_LINE_WIDTH0/1 =
  width/2; src/vivante/backend.rs, etnaviv_rasterizer.c:53-54, etnaviv_emit.c:423-437). Mesa's hwdb
  (hwdb/nxp/gc_feature_database.h, ChipID 0x7000 rev 0x6204, both ECO entries) has REG_WideLine 1,
  PA_WIDELINE_FIX 1 and WIDELINE_TRIANGLE_EMU 0. So Mesa too draws wide lines with the hardware path, width up to
  8192 (etnaviv_screen.c:366-368). There is no other line-interpolation state to set (state_3d.xml.h PA_*).
- gl_test 127's model M0 (the one it passes, fit word 9) is the major-axis model, i.e. the projected one, measured
  directly on our stack.

Verdict: both families are GC7000 behaviour. They keep QualityWarning, which dEQP and deqp-runner treat as a
non-failure. Not worked further. Board left on Linux with galcore loaded (its boot default). ~/gcgpu/gcgpu.ko is now
d1350ee9faf8; the previous one is kept as ~/gcgpu/gcgpu-15dde8082fbb.ko. Rows run: none (a tool and docs only;
vendor-deqp.sh checked with sh -n and by the repeat run above).

**Follow-up: the six hardware-floor cases on the vendor driver (texture.vertex.cube.filtering.nearest_mipmap_{linear,
nearest}_linear_{clamp,mirror,repeat}).** Prediction (written first): the vendor fails the same six the same way; the
rest of texture.vertex.cube.filtering and the 2D nearest_mipmap_*_linear controls pass. **Wrong for the six.**
- Vendor (vendor-deqp.sh): texture.vertex.cube.filtering 36/36 Pass, the six included. 2D nearest_mipmap_*_linear 6/6
  Pass.
- Ours (Linux harness, gcgpu.ko d1350ee9faf8, the ES2 online pair): the six Fail ("Image comparison failed"), the other
  30 and the 2D six Pass. These are the same names as on Zephyr at 04a0e2c2.
- The pictures are the same. For each of the six, the vendor's Result and ours are identical: 0 pixels differ by more
  than 8. Both differ from the Reference our run logs in the same pixels: 4,387 (nearest_mipmap_linear_linear_*) or
  1,806 (nearest_mipmap_nearest_linear_*), all in one render cell (x 0-83, y 56-111 of the 168x112 picture). The
  vendor logs no Reference because it passed.
- So the vendor passes because dEQP gives it another reference, not because it draws differently.
  es2fVertexTextureTests.cpp:1154 sets `sampler.seamlessCubeMap = m_isES3Capable`, decided by GL_MAJOR_VERSION
  (gluContextInfo.cpp:64). The vendor context is ES 3.1, so dEQP samples its reference down the seamless path. Our
  report-es2 pair gets GL_INVALID_ENUM, so it goes down the per-face path. Mesa's CI context is ES 2.0 too
  (deqp-etnaviv-gc7000-r6204.toml `version_check = "GL ES 2.0.*git"`), so it fails them as well.
- What differs between the two paths is the ES 2.0 min/mag rule, not seamlessness (CORRECTED the same day: an earlier
  version of this paragraph said dEQP never switches at 0.5; that was wrong). TextureCubeView::sample
  (tcuTexture.cpp:4497-4503) takes the per-face path through sampleLevelArray2D with the texture's es2 flag.
  sampleLevelArray2DOffset (tcuTexture.cpp:3190-3193) then uses `magnified = lod <= 0.5` exactly when mag is LINEAR
  and min is NEAREST_MIPMAP_*. The seamless path (sampleLevelArrayCubeSeamless, :3801) uses lodThreshold 0.
  So the floor's written reason stands: in the failing cell (texture 1 at full-face scale, the LOD ~0.19 of the
  floor row), the ES 2.0 reference magnifies with LINEAR. The texture unit switches at 0 and samples NEAREST_MIPMAP,
  which is what the ES 3 reference expects.
- Consequence for the seamless-bit A/B team-lead asked for next: not run. TE_SAMPLER_CONFIG1_SEAMLESS_CUBE_MAP
  (0x02000000, state_3d.xml.h:1680; Mesa sets it only for GL seamless, etnaviv_texture_state.c:131 /
  etnaviv_texture_desc.c:391; src/vivante never writes it) cannot change which reference dEQP uses: the context
  version picks it. It also cannot move the min/mag switch, and the failing cell is a min/mag choice, not a
  face-edge effect. The six remain the hardware floor. The one thing that turns them into Pass is a context that
  reports ES 3 (the vendor's pixels, which equal ours, pass there). ES 3.0 itself drops the 0.5 rule and requires
  seamless cube filtering, so on our ES3 pair these six should be expected to pass; that has not been run.
- Evidence: records/imx8mp/qw-vendor-d1350ee9/ Results-{VENDOR,OURS}-vtx{cube,2d}.qpa (sha256 1e1ce29499b5a314,
  3a26978c7537f81d, 2ee5fa51210541f6, da6399b718404560), vtximg.py.
- Process note: my first staging of the shim wrote through ~/vendor-sysroot/libEGL.so.1 (a symlink) and replaced the
  vendor libEGL.so.1.5.0 on the board. The earlier vendor runs above were unaffected: they used a pristine local copy.
  A later rebuild picked up the overwritten file, and the shim then called itself and spun. The file is restored
  (md5 708c9726de81361623e505593e29fdb3, the same as the image's /usr/lib copy). vendor-deqp.sh now takes the vendor
  libEGL from the image, checks it, renames files over the links instead of writing through them, and points
  libEGL.so at the shim; without that last step the vendor stack loads a second EGL and glGetString returns NULL.
  The board is on Linux with galcore loaded.
- **Measured: the same cases on our ES 3.0-reporting pair** (d1350ee9, no report-es2, online compiler;
  dEQP-GLES2.info.version reads "OpenGL ES 3.0 YakoGL"; gcgpu.ko d1350ee9faf8). Prediction, written first: all 36
  cube cases pass, the six included, and the 2D six pass. Result:
  - The six floor cases now Pass: nearest_mipmap_{linear,nearest}_linear_{clamp,mirror,repeat}. Our Result images
    are identical to the ES2-pair run: 0 pixels differ by more than 8. Only dEQP's reference changed.
  - The 2D nearest_mipmap_*_linear_* 6/6 Pass.
  - **Four cases that pass on the ES2 pair now Fail:** texture.vertex.cube.filtering.linear_mipmap_linear_linear_
    {clamp,mirror} and linear_mipmap_linear_nearest_{clamp,mirror}. The _repeat pair passes. Our pixels are again
    unchanged, and the vendor passes all four. Our Result differs from the vendor's in 351 pixels (clamp) and 204
    (repeat), every one on a face edge (distance 0 from a 28-pixel face-cell border). Our Result differs from the ES3
    reference in 329 pixels.
  - So on this core the vertex-stage cube LINEAR is per-face, as the register state says (bit 25 never written). The
    vendor filters seamlessly on its ES 3.1 context, and dEQP's ES3 reference wants seamless.
  - Totals: cube 32 Pass / 4 Fail, 2D 6 Pass. The six floor cases are not a hardware limit on an ES 3 context. The
    seamless-iff-ES3 rule (set TE_SAMPLER_CONFIG1_SEAMLESS_CUBE_MAP in the descriptor when the context reports ES 3)
    is what the four new failures need. It is not implemented or tested here.
  - Evidence: records/imx8mp/qw-vendor-d1350ee9/Results-OURSES3-{vtxcube,vtx2d,info}.qpa (sha256 e25ffe4d04a97913,
    a12f6f575d958fe8, 3d2139106c8f7e4d), es3cmp.py. The board was returned to Linux with galcore loaded.

## Depth textures on the ES 2.0 surface: GL_OES_depth_texture + GL_OES_packed_depth_stencil, and rendered depth reaching the texels (branch gl/es2-depth-stencil-texture, 2026-10-01)

**Why.** 27 dEQP-GLES2 `fbo.completeness.attachment_combinations.*_tex` cases (a texture at
GL_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT) were NotSupported on every board: dEQP finds a stencil-renderable texture only
through `GL_OES_packed_depth_stencil GL_OES_depth_texture` (glsFboCompletenessTests.cpp:207, DEPTH_STENCIL /
UNSIGNED_INT_24_8). The 18 depth-texture cases that already passed used GL_DEPTH_COMPONENT16 textures, which
dEQP counts as depth-renderable under `GL_OES_required_internalformat` alone (:85-87, :234-235).

**What changed.**
- The pair is claimed on the ES 2.0 surface of the PowerVR and the GC7000 (not the V3D, below), with the
  extensions' upload rules (types, TEXTURE_2D only, base = format; glGenerateMipmap of a depth texture is
  GL_INVALID_OPERATION on both surfaces). A depth texture samples (d, d, d, 1) on ES 2.0 and (d, 0, 0, 1) on
  ES 3.0.
- Rendered depth reaches the texels. A render writes depth into the backend's own depth/stencil buffer, keyed
  by the texture, and nothing brought it into the texels (ES 3.0 core had the same hole). Now, before a draw
  samples a depth texture or the CPU writes one, the GL core waits for the kick that rendered it and the
  backend writes its depth plane into the R32F texels (`YakoglBackend::depth_resolve`, ABI 168 bytes).
- `GlesDraw::ds_id` carries a texture bit per half: a depth-stencil texture and a D24S8 renderbuffer of the
  same name number no longer share one packed PowerVR buffer.
- gl_test 169 `dstex`: (1) a 4x1 depth ramp uploaded and sampled; (2) one DEPTH_STENCIL texture on both points
  of an FBO, drawn with a stencil-only triangle, a depth ramp and a green quad under both tests; (3) that
  texture sampled.

**The layouts, measured.** Both were Mesa's readings before the boards ran:
- PowerVR: the ZLS store (no twiddle bits) is packed D24S8, depth in bits 23..0, row-linear at the ZLS-tile
  aligned width. **Confirmed**: 169 step 3 read 128 / 72 / 74 / 181, exactly.
- GC7000: etnaviv reads a depth surface without SUPER_TILED as 4x4 TILED; the first board run failed at 169
  check 10 (got 0x72, want 0x48; checks 1-9 right). The surface's words, dumped on the gcgpu Linux path, held
  (x + y + 1) / 128 at x + y * 64: **the PE writes it row-linear** at the row stride, row 0 at GL's y 0, with
  the PE_DEPTH_CONFIG this backend programs. The resolve reads it so (f83a7361).

**Board results** (predictions written first; all held except the GC7000 layout, fixed as above):

| board | image | result |
|---|---|---|
| AM62P, Zephyr, ES 2.0 | gl_test list 169,162,167,168,123 (a3856a06) | 0 of 5 failed; 169 12/12 checks |
| AM62P, Zephyr, ES 3.0 | gl_test 169 (a3856a06) | PASS, 12/12, red-only samples |
| AM62P, Zephyr | dEQP-GLES2 fbo.completeness.* (a3856a06) | 372 pass / 0 / 0 (mustpass 370 of 370) |
| AM62P, Zephyr | dEQP-GLES2 fbo.render.* (a3856a06) | 319 pass / 0 / 0 |
| i.MX8MP, Zephyr, ES 2.0 | gl_test sweep 128..175 (a3856a06) | 169 not passed, check 10 got 0xff727272 want 0xff484848; 162, 164, 165, 167, 168 pass |
| i.MX8MP, gcgpu Linux, ES 2.0 | gl_test 169 with the words dumped (a3856a06 + a dump, not committed) | the row-linear surface above |
| i.MX8MP, gcgpu Linux, ES 2.0 | gl_test 169,162,164,165,167,168 (f83a7361) | 0 of 6 failed |
| i.MX8MP, Zephyr, ES 2.0 | gl_test sweep 128..175 (f83a7361) | 162, 164, 165, 167, 168, 169 pass (the other cases of the range as at a3856a06) |
| i.MX8MP, Zephyr, ES 2.0 / ES 3.0 | gl_test 169 alone (f83a7361) | PASS, 12 checks, in both |
| i.MX8MP, Zephyr | dEQP-GLES2 fbo.completeness.* (f83a7361) | 372 pass / 0 / 0 |
| i.MX8MP, Zephyr | dEQP-GLES2 fbo.render.* (f83a7361) | 319 pass / 0 / 0 |

f83a7361 changes only src/vivante against a3856a06, so the AM62P rows stand for the landed tip. Host:
dEQP-GLES2 fbo.completeness 370 of 370 on both host pairs (27 NotSupported before).

**Performance (for the performance phase).** The resolve is a GPU sync (flush + finish of the kick that
rendered the texture) plus a CPU pass over the level, once per render of a depth texture that is then
sampled: a shadow map drawn every frame costs both every frame. Sampling the depth buffer in place would
remove both, and each back end needs one experiment first: the PowerVR, a TPU texture format that samples
U24 depth out of the packed D24S8 row-linear ZLS store (Mesa's D24S8 texture row); the GC7000, a TE format
that samples the PE's row-linear D24S8 (etnaviv's D24X8 family) and how it normalises.

**Not done.** The other direction: depth or stencil the CPU writes into a texture that is then attached is
not loaded into the backend's buffer. The stencil half of a depth-stencil texture needs nothing more: it is
never sampled (OES_packed_depth_stencil: "as if the base internal format was DEPTH").

**The V3D note.** The Pi 4 keeps the 27 NotSupported: v3d/texture.rs refuses every format but RGBA8/L8/A8/LA8,
and a depth texture is R32F. Needed: R32F sampling with a 32-bit TMU return (compiler and TMU config), or a
native depth format tiled at upload (Mesa's DEPTH_COMP16 / DEPTH24_X8); then a `depth_resolve` for its split
ZS buffers, then the claim and gl_test 169 on the Pi 4.

Same 27 case filters as sweep 28 (`2c87c2e4`), each image one boot on the Pi 4 (tryboot, UART record, watchdog back to Linux).

(tools/cts/deqp-uart-tally.py, timestamps stripped: no log MISSING or INCOMPLETE). 17,254 cases seen: 17,095 pass, 103 fail, 53 not supported, 3 QualityWarning.

Against tools/cts/gles2-mustpass.txt (17,165 names): 17,052 have a result, **113 have none in either sweep** (draw.random 51,
draw_arrays / draw_elements 50, clip_control 8, debug_marker 3, multisampled_render_to_texture.readpixels 1; the filters never select them, sweep 28 had the same 113). Among the 17,052: 16,893 pass, 103 fail, 53 n.s., 3 other.

### Per image

## Pi 4: sweep 29's 78 failures, closed (2026-10-01, branch v3d/loops-regression)

Sweep 29 (above) failed 78 mustpass cases that sweep 28 passed, and differed from it in the Zephyr version as
well as the commit. Both causes are settled; one was yakogl's compiler, one the image configuration. Neither
was the Zephyr version.

**shaders.loops (72) and return_in_dynamic_loop_never_fragment (1): a compiler bug, fixed in 69e2897d.**
The pattern in the names: every failing case has a uniform iteration count (`ui_*`, including the
`*_constant_iterations.select_iteration_count` cases, whose count is `ub_true ? 3 : 0`), and its loop body
rotates or swaps the carried vector (`res = res.yzwx`, `coords = coords.wzyx`). Fragment shaders fail in
for, while and do-while; vertex shaders only in do_while_uniform and infinite_with_conditional_break. The
dynamic cases (count `one * ui_*`, `one` from a varying) and the loops with a `continue` or a nested loop pass.

Host first. Three minimal pairs in tests/v3d_sim_mesa.rs, compiled by our V3D back end, run on the QPU
interpreter (sim.rs) and compared with the IR evaluator: es100/loop_uniform.frag (for_uniform basic, FS),
es100/loop_uniform.dowhile.vert (do_while_uniform basic, VS), es100/ret_dynloop_never.frag
(return_in_dynamic_loop_never). Bisect by running them at each commit:

| commit | loop_uniform (FS) | loop_uniform.dowhile (VS) | ret_dynloop_never (FS) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2c87c2e4 (sweep 28) | agree | agree | not run (added later; the two others' verdicts decided the range) |
| ca1a28bd^ | agree | agree | |
| ca1a28bd (a kept loop's pass-start guard dropped) | agree | **disagree** | |
| 2951fef9^ | agree | **disagree** | |
| 2951fef9 (a fragment shader's uniform bound leaves by a branch) | **disagree** | **disagree** | |
| c9b23dfb (sweep 29) | **disagree** | **disagree** | **disagree** |
| 69e2897d (the fix) | agree | agree | agree |

Cause: at the end of a counted loop's pass, prepare.rs gives each carried lane an `SOp::PhiNext` (lane takes
its next value), and select.rs made each one a `VOp::Copy`, in order. They are one parallel copy. While the
body was guarded (the unroller's selects on the break flag), every next value was a new value. ca1a28bd
(clear_at_pass_start) and 2951fef9 (`SOp::LoopBreak`) removed those guards, so a next value can be another
lane's phi: `res = res.yzwx` became x <- y, y <- z, z <- w, w <- x, and w read the x just written. A
vertex shader's for loop keeps its second guard (LoopBreak is fragment-only), which is why for_uniform vertex
passed on the board while do_while_uniform vertex failed. Fix (select.rs `Sel::phi_copies`): at a loop end's
first PhiNext, each source that a copy would read after an earlier copy of the same end has written it is
first moved into its own register. The three pairs are pinned in both builds (report-es2 and ES 3), with the
coverage and control counts re-derived (all mutants caught). V3D lib tests 2548 pass; fmt, clippy -D warnings
for `host-test,gpu-v3d,shaderc-online,no-shader-table`, `host-test,shaderc-online` and
`host-test,shaderc-online,report-es2`.

**texture.size.2d.2048x2048 (5): image configuration.** Sweep 28's T5 record reads `carve-out 64 MiB` and
`tiled copies kept up to 25165824` (high-water 16,781,312); sweep 29's T5 was built with prj.conf alone
(48 MiB, 16,777,216) and refused the draws by the tiled-copy budget. The two values were a per-image option
nobody had written down. They are now driver/samples/zephyr/v3d_deqp/texture-2048.conf
(`-DEXTRA_CONF_FILE=texture-2048.conf`), named by prj.conf and by the T5 line of the filter file. They stay out
of prj.conf so the other images keep the configuration they were measured with.

**Coverage.** tools/cts/pi4-full-tree.txt holds the whole tree in 29 lines: the 27 filters of sweeps 28/29
and two new images, DR (`draw.*`) and XT (`clip_control.*`, `debug_marker.*`,
`multisampled_render_to_texture.*`). Each of the 17,165 mustpass names is selected by exactly one line.
tools/cts/deqp-uart-tally.py now drops the Pi recorder's leading `HH:MM:SS ` (it reported every Pi record as
"no summary line"). On sweep 29's 27 records it gives the numbers above (17,052 with a result, 16,893 pass,
103 fail, 53 n.s., 3 QW).

v3d_tiling_mesa.c, marks that header as included and provides the four functions when CONFIG_POSIX_API is set; a
build without the POSIX layer is unchanged (the v3d_gl_test image has the same sha256 before and after).

## Both boards: the SN65DSI8x bridge in Rust from the TI data sheets (2026-10-01, branch form/5-display-sn65dsi8x, group E step 2)

`yakogl,sn65dsi8x` (C shim `driver/drivers/display/bridge_sn65dsi8x.c`,
register logic `driver/rust/src/ip/sn65dsi8x.rs` from TI SLLSEC2H / SLLSEC1I)
replaces `src/display/imx8mp_sn65dsi84.c`,
`drivers/display/panel_sn65dsi83_lvds.c` and `sn65dsi83_regs_from_mode`. The
sequence is the data sheet's Table 7-2 (on the AM62P the DSI host is now
attached before EN rises, as 7.4.1 asks; the old driver raised EN first), every
reserved or channel-B bit is kept by read-modify-write, the CSRs are read back
before the PLL starts, and the error status is cleared with 0xFF and read 1 ms
later. Predictions were written in the branch's build/STATE.txt before each run.

| board, image | route | evidence | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| AM62P, gl_triangle, `30ab4ee6e1725f11` | kexec, console on UART | `DSI link up` → `sn65dsi8x: ID "58ISD" rev 0x01 (attempt 1)` → `up, DSI 153600 kHz (range 0x1e), LVDS 51200 kHz = /3 (range 1), fmt 0x68` → `link clean (IRQ_STAT 0x00)`; triangle drawn, record `594b0400 ff403f80 35706c4e 04000258`; Linux back after 92 s | as predicted; the record is the pre-change one's; IRQ_STAT 0 is the first link check this board's driver has printed |
| i.MX8MP, gc_slint + `FORCE_COLD`, `0d04e54cc750680a` | normal (`CRASH=`) | record `594b021b 00ff0d01 0030027f 4d443c3f`: kind 2 PASS, 639 frames, display health 0x3f | as predicted: the teardown drops EN for 10 ms (the part forgets its CSRs), so BRIDGE_ANSWERS and BRIDGE_PLL_LOCK (PLL_EN_STAT) at the end are this driver's cold start |
| i.MX8MP, gc_slint (adopt), `d60f302fba36e5c0` | crash (`CRASH=1`) | record `594b021b 00ff0d01 00300281 99443b3f`: PASS, 641 frames, health 0x3f | as predicted; the adopt path only reads the bridge. Frame-time max 153 ms (step-1 runs: 77 ms), jump 60 s after Linux booted; not attributed, noted |

What changed in the registers: on the i.MX8MP's cold path `CHA_DSI_CLK_RANGE`
is 42 (0x2a), which is what Linux runs there and what Table 7-7 gives for a
213.3 MHz DSI clock; the old driver rounded up to 43. The host test compares
the whole image with the Linux dump: only 0xF4/0xF7 (outside the CSR map)
differ. On the AM62P the driver now leaves 0x1A at 0x01, not 0x00 (channel B's
termination, left at its reset value; channel B is off). Neither picture was
seen by me: a person (or the camera) looking at both panels is still owed.

## Armadillo-X2: first gc_slint run

2026-10-01, image `armadillo_x2/mimx8ml8/a53` gc_slint, jumped from Armadillo Base OS (Linux 6.12.105-0-at) on the crash route
(`crashkernel=256M@0x60000000`, load address 0x60000000, `root@armadillo.local`, loader and image staged in /tmp, nothing else on the board
touched). No sudo and no SNVS wrapper on this board, so the jump was a local copy of the kexec_run.sh steps (`kexec_zephyr zephyr.bin
0x60000000 --crash` as root).

**What had to change to build it.** The cluster is laid out for 1280x800 (SafeUI layout, BUILD_ASSERTs in main.c) and the X2's HDMI monitor
is 1920x1200 with no 1280x800 mode (the monitor offers 1920x1200 down to 640x480; no `modetest` on the board to change the mode anyway).
Both are 8:5, so `CONFIG_GC_SLINT_UI_SCALED` (new, set in `boards/armadillo_x2_mimx8ml8_a53.conf`) relaxes the two size asserts and
`slint_draw_frame` (gl_slint/rust/src/lib.rs) dispatches a Slint scale factor of width/1280 when the drawable is wider than 1280, so the
design fills the 1920x1200 buffers (scale 1.5; glyphs are the 1280x800 bitmaps scaled, so text will be softer). Nothing changes for the
Verdin (1280) and the AM62P (1024). The X2's DTS already says 1920x1200 for the adopt node; the adopt path found the LCDIF running at that
size. Image: 6.76 MB file, 111,063,040 bytes RAM footprint (image_size header) in the 268,435,456-byte crash window; `RAM 41%` of 256 MB.

**Jumps** (UART2 captured on this laptop's CP2102N `/dev/ttyUSB0`, verified to be the X2's console by writing to `/dev/ttymxc1`):

| run | image | jump | Linux back | UART |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | cb9656778166b9fe | 17:14:16 | 17:16:40 (144 s; fresh Linux up 11.5 s) | Zephyr boot to `carveout: 0x80000000 (64 MiB)`, then nothing |
| 2 | 4655cdda891c3934 (+ a printk per gc_render step, not committed) | 17:20:55 | 17:22:13 (78 s; fresh Linux up 11.2 s) | `X2DEBUG gc_render step 1`, `X2DEBUG gc_render st`, then U-Boot SPL |

The Zephyr part of the log, both runs: GPC gpumix/gpu3d on, GC7000 identity (rev 0x6204, product 0x70003), "GC7000 bring-up milestone 1
complete (core clock 800000000 Hz)", three secondary cores up, `adopting the LCDIF: 1920x1200, 32 bpp, pitch 7680 at 0xb0100000 -> ours`,
`display: adopted for the console`, `gc_slint: the 1280x800 cluster on a 1920x1200 panel`, then the render service starts and the console
goes silent. So: the loader and crash route work on this board, Zephyr boots on all four cores, the GPU answers, the adopt path takes the
running LCDIF3 over (the layer is re-pointed -- at physical address 0, as the cause below shows, which is why the screen is black),
and the run dies inside `gc_render_init` before the first frame. In neither run did a picture appear (run 1 watched by the user: black the
whole time; run 2 not watched). The two returns differ (132 s and 67 s from jump to the new Linux's boot), so they are not the same
failure: 67 s is about the 60 s hold plus U-Boot, 132 s is not.

**SNVS record.** None: the board has no `snvs-lpgpr` nvmem device (`/sys/bus/nvmem/devices/`: `imx-ocotp0`, `rv8803_nvram0`), so the
result record the Verdin scripts read is unreachable here. The only result channel is the UART, and it stops mid-line in run 2.

### The cause: the adopt driver pointed LCDIF3 at physical address 0

`gc_slint` (and `gc_gl_test`) call `imx8mp_display_on(0, 0)` first, to own the display before any GL work; the real buffer comes later.
The full driver (`imx8mp_display.c`, the Verdin's) returns early when `fb_phys == 0` ("adopting can do without an address").
`imx8mp_lcdif_adopt.c`, which only an adopt board builds, did not: it wrote our pitch and format and then `lcdif_set_fb(lcdif, 0)`. The
log said so all along -- `at 0xb0100000 -> ours`, with "ours" being 0. From the next vblank LCDIF3 scanned 1920x1200x4 = 9 MB from PA 0
sixty times a second: boot ROM, the CAAM secure RAM, OCRAM_S and the M7's TCM at 0x7e0000. A CPU read of 0x007e0000 from Linux hangs
this board the same way (done once by accident on 2026-10-01 while looking for a RAM channel: the X2 reset itself within a minute). The
interconnect wedges a fraction of a second after the call, which is why the console stopped at different places in gc_render_init's first
lines (run 2 earlier than run 1) and mid-line: the TX FIFO stopped draining. Return times: about 60 s when nothing fed WDOG1 after that
(Linux's imx2_wdt timeout), about 125 s when the sample's supervisor kept feeding until its 65 s deadline and then blocked in printk on
the dead UART.

Ruled out on the way, with evidence: (a) the GPU driver's CCM writes run in milestone 1, before prints that did come out, and touch only
roots 3/4/24/25 and CCGR 87/70 (UART2 is CCGR74, root 0xaf80); (c) WDOG1 is fed (`GC_SAMPLE_WDOG_BASE` 0x30280000; the supervisor
feeds every 250 ms); the SNVS stores (below): run 3 had them off and stopped at the same place as run 1.

**Fix** (`driver/src/display/imx8mp_lcdif_adopt.c`, general for every adopt board): `fb_phys == 0` adopts and writes nothing -- the
scan-out stays on Linux's buffer; our pitch and format go in with the first real buffer (`imx8mp_display_on(fb, pitch)` or
`imx8mp_display_set_fb`), in the same shadow load as the address; `set_fb(0)` is refused; Linux's address, pitch and format are captured
once, at the first adopt, so `imx8mp_display_off()` restores them and not our buffer.

### Two board findings on the way

**The SNVS record overwrote U-Boot's boot count.** The LPGPRs are readable from Linux through `/dev/mem` (SNVS is not claimed by a
driver here; most other MMIO and all RAM are refused by `CONFIG_IO_STRICT_DEVMEM`). After run 2 they read `dead0002 00000101 0000005e
00000003`: words 1..3 are our PROGRESS record (GPU step ENTER at 94 ms uptime, the third record), word 0 is U-Boot 2020.04-at30's boot
count (`0xdead0000 | count`), rewritten on the next boot. Every gc_* image wrote boot-loader state that outlives the run, and this board
has no nvmem device to read a record with anyway. `CONFIG_GC_COMMON_RESULT_SNVS` now defaults to n on the X2 (board `Kconfig.defconfig`);
the console on UART2 is the channel. Runs 3-6 left the LPGPRs as they were (`dead0002 00000101 0000005e 00000003` before and after).

**64 MiB of carveout is too little at 1920x1200.** With the scan-out fixed (run 4) the first frame was drawn and shown, then every frame
failed: `pool: 9338880 bytes at align 64 does not fit (58245376 of 66715648 used)` -> GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY, verdict FAIL, a still picture
on the monitor. Three 9 MB window buffers plus depth and Slint's own targets fill 58 MiB. The X2's carveout is now 128 MiB of galcore's
256 MiB `gcContMem` (board DTS); the image (106 MiB) and the carveout mapping still fit the 256 MiB `KERNEL_VM_SIZE`.

And `CONFIG_GC_SLINT_UI_SCALED` judged the first frame against the 1280x800 host reference grid although its help says it is not judged
(run 5: REFERENCE best 'scaled 0.8x' 90%, FAIL code 45, 340 s hold). The scaled build now skips the grid as the 1024x600 parity build
does; the five probe points are still judged (5/5).

### Runs after the fix

| run | image | change | Linux back | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | d04a4f1b8add066b | SNVS record off only | 145 s | same as run 1: silent after `carveout:` -- SNVS ruled out |
| 4 | 6bca5dd1f306586f | + adopt fix | 237 s | console alive to the end; `scan-out kept`; self-tests, READBACK 5/5; first frame shown (user: picture, not moving); then GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY every frame, FAIL, hold 160 s |
| 5 | e5e62831c2241de9 | + carveout 128 MiB | 415 s | animates (user: moving, slowly): 328 frames, 7 fps; FAIL code 45 = the reference grid, hold 340 s |
| 6 | b37fc1e8760125f5 | + grid not judged when scaled | 79 s | **PASS**: 328 frames at 7 fps (frame 128/133/150 ms, eglSwapBuffers 100/104/126 ms min/median/max), 5/5 probes, console to `resetting the SoC` |

Verdin iMX8M Plus, the same tree (gc_slint, crash route, image e4ea16813e84c850; the Verdin builds the full display driver and keeps
the SNVS record): `594b021b 00ff0d01 00300281 55443b3f` = kind 2 PASS, 641 frames, health 0x3f, Linux back after 88 s. No regression.

The user's verdict on the picture: runs 4 and 5 seen (a still cluster, then a moving one); run 6 (PASS) not separately confirmed.
Performance (328 frames at 1920x1200 here against the Verdin's 641 at 1280x800 in the same run time) is not part of this fix.

## gc_slint at 60 fps: where the frame goes, and the pipelined swap (2026-10-01, perf/gc-slint-60fps)

Goal (user, 2026-10-02 via team-lead): gc_slint at 60 fps on Zephyr, corrected to the Armadillo-X2 at 1920x1200 (UI scaled
1.5x, CONFIG_GC_SLINT_UI_SCALED). Branch on origin/main + x2/gc-render-hang 1c1f0230 (merged as is). Not reached; the
measurements say why.

**Instrument.** gc_slint times each loop phase with the architectural timer (8 MHz), not printk: `ui` = slint_draw_frame
(Slint + FemtoVG + the GL calls recording the frame), `swap` = eglSwapBuffers, `flip` = imx8mp_display_set_fb. The GL
wrappers time glDraw*, glTex(Sub)Image2D and glBuffer(Sub)Data. The driver adds `gc_render_perf()`: GPU busy time as the
union of each kick's submit..retire interval (stamped at submit and in the ISR), time inside gc_render_wait, and the
GPU's own HI_PROFILE TOTAL/IDLE cycles and read/write bytes (the clock check: 799 MHz). A run reports one page of six
16-bit per-frame averages as a kind 12 PERF record, picked by the selector `0x1000 | exp << 3 | page` (gc_result.h,
the Python record decoder decodes it); `exp` turns on a backend experiment (`gc_debug_perf_exp`, 0 in every product build):
1 every draw clipped to 8x8, 2 no per-draw flushes/stalls, 4 every fragment shader replaced by the clear's 1
instruction, 8 the first `exp >> 5` draws of a frame clipped, 16 the clears clipped. The MC_PROFILE SH/PE counters read
0 on this part; RA valid pixels work.

**X2 result channel.** No UART and no view of the HDMI; /dev/mem refuses RAM (CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM, "Operation not
permitted" on the crash window). The SNVS LPGPR1..3 survive the reset and this U-Boot (2020.04-at30) touches only LPGPR0,
its boot count. CONFIG_GC_COMMON_RESULT_SNVS_KEEP_LPGPR0 (the X2's default) moves the record one register up (w0..w2 in
LPGPR1..3, w3 dropped); the selector travels there too. Read and written from Linux with
driver/tools/kexec-zephyr/snvs_lpgpr (built with the Zephyr SDK's aarch64-zephyr-elf-gcc, -nostdlib -static), LPGPR0
written back as found (0xdead0002 before and after every run).

**Before (origin/main code), Verdin 1280x800, image perf1 (selector pages 0-2):**

| per frame | ms |
|---|---|
| frame | 68.2 (273 frames in the 18 s loop) |
| ui (Slint + FemtoVG + GL recording) | 12.6, of which glDraw* 3.9, texture uploads 1.1 (21 a frame) |
| eglSwapBuffers | 47.8 = the wait for the GPU |
| flip (LCDIF latch) | 7.7 |
| GPU busy | 47.8 (2 kicks a frame: 66 K command words overflowed the 64 K stream) |
| GPU memory traffic | 12.9 MB read, 10.3 MB written (~0.5 GB/s: not bandwidth) |

X2 1920x1200 (UART run, same code): frame 133.4 = ui 22.1 + swap 103.6 + flip 7.6; GPU busy 103.8; 263 draws; RA valid
pixels 4.83 M a frame (2.1 times the screen). The "9.3 MB allocation per frame" is the D24S8 buffer of each of the three
window surfaces (1920x1216x4), allocated once each.

**Cause 1 (fixed): every swap was a glFinish.** `gc_finish_previous` waited for the slot before `cur`, which with two
stream slots is the kick just submitted, so recording, GPU and flip ran in series. Now (src/vivante/backend.rs) it waits
for the kicks submitted before the previous swap, which is the backend contract and what the PowerVR does; four stream
slots of 128 K words (one kick a frame). gc_slint (driver/samples/zephyr/gc_slint/src/main.c) flips the previous,
complete buffer as gl_slint does on the AM62P (three buffers; two keep the old wait), and calls glFinish where it reads
pixels from the CPU (self-test, first frame) and before a ring publish. Host test
`a_swap_waits_for_the_previous_frame_not_the_one_it_submits`.

**Where the GPU time goes** (experiments, gpu-busy per frame):

| experiment | Verdin 1280x800 | X2 1920x1200 |
|---|---|---|
| none (pipelined) | 47.9 | 104.4 |
| every draw clipped to 8x8 | 0.41 | -- |
| no per-draw flushes and stalls | 47.4 | -- |
| every fragment shader = 1 instruction | 8.4 | 17.0 |
| first draw of each frame clipped (the window background) | 21.5 | 44.9 |
| clears clipped | -- | 104.5 |

So the GPU time is fill, and mostly fragment shading: the per-draw cost and the synchronisation are negligible, the
clear costs nothing measurable, and one draw, the window's `@linear-gradient` background drawn by FemtoVG's FillGradient
shader over the whole screen (56 instructions, ~47 executed per pixel: paint matrix, sdroundrect, dither, scissor),
is 59.5 of the X2's 104 ms. The GC7000UL runs about 1.6-2 G pixel-instructions a second (2 shader cores, one vec4
instruction a clock each at 800 MHz); 60 fps at 1920x1200 leaves ~33 M pixel-instructions a frame, about 14 per
screen pixel with no overdraw.

**After, default images (no selector):**

| board | record | reading |
|---|---|---|
| Verdin, slint-final 658b723fb9d4f941 | `594b021b 00ff0d01 00180391 4433133f` | PASS, 913 frames (was 641), median swap wait 24 ms, health 0x3f, frame min/median/max 19/51/68 ms |
| X2, x2-final 5f36a348d39f4a3c | LPGPR1..3 `594b021b 00ff0d01 004901a7` | PASS, 423 frames (was 328), median swap wait 73 ms |

Frame-time distribution (page 3): Verdin p50 51, p90 51, p99 52, max 61 ms, 17.2 % of frames at or under 34 ms, none
under 17 (the flip waits for the latch, so 48 ms of GPU becomes three vsync periods); X2 p50 100, p90 117, max 117 ms.
Verdin page 0: frame 47.96 = GPU-bound (gpu-busy 47.93, busy 998/1000), ui 11.8, swap 27.3, flip 8.6, 1 kick a frame.
X2 page 0: frame 104.4, ui 21.9, swap 73.7, gpu-busy 104.4.

**CPU clock.** Linux's governor leaves the A53s at 1.2 GHz when the jump comes (schedutil on the Verdin, ondemand on the
X2). With `performance` set before the jump (1.6 GHz inherited) the X2's ui went 17.9 -> 14.2 ms (trivial-shader runs);
the Verdin's stayed 11.8 ms. Not changed in any launcher; noted for the next step.

**What 60 fps at 1920x1200 needs** (none of it is in this branch):
- GPU: the non-shader floor alone is 17.0 ms (> 16.7), and shading is 87 ms more. The background gradient is the first
  target: a full-screen per-pixel box-gradient evaluation is the most expensive way to draw a two-stop vertical
  gradient. Options: a FemtoVG shader variant for linear gradients without sdroundrect/dither and without the scissor
  when there is none (upstream-able, our fork already adds NO_DISCARD), or a design that does not repaint a full-screen
  gradient every frame. Then the rest (45 ms): shorter FemtoVG shader variants, less overdraw (RA 2.1x the screen), and
  the ROP floor (linear colour and D24S8 surfaces, no tile status / fast clear) -- tiled surfaces with tile status is
  backend work.
- CPU: ui 22 ms at 1.2 GHz, 14 ms at 1.6 GHz; must fall under 16.7 with margin.

**Regression (Verdin, Zephyr, crash route):** dEQP image 75e63c5ec1ea189e: fragment_ops.blend 1060/1060 (`594b0808
00000424 00000000 ffff0424`), shaders.texture_functions 20/20 (kind 9, 0 resets, 0 timeouts). gl_test sweeps (SEL=256,
ES 1.00 set): 0..47 `031f / f9feff7f` (= the last record at 04a0e2c2), 96..143 `0013 / 47b51bf2` (identical), 144..
`0000 / 03f40060` (baseline bits all kept; 149 and 169 now pass, landed since), 48..95 `07d7 / dffffc70` on the first run
(77 and 83 not passed) and `07df / fffffc70` (the known baseline, 85 the known flipper) on the second; 77 alone PASS.
Lost work, resets and fence timeouts 0 in every run. Host: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy and tests for
host-test,gpu-vivante,shaderc-online clean (the counters test now uses GC_FRAMES).

## Route 3 on the Verdin i.MX8MP, 2026-10-01 (branch safeui/route3-revive)

Goal (user): SafeUI route 3 end to end on the Verdin iMX8M Plus, never seen working before (every earlier
route-3 reading was a normal-route failure, see "the normal kexec route dies before PRE_KERNEL_1"). The
Cortex-M7 runs the SafeUI safety firmware, owns the LCDIF, draws the speed, gear, READY, fuel and telltales
itself and blends them into the A53's frame; the A53 gc_slint producer (`prj_ring.conf`) renders the rich
cluster into the M7's application buffers and publishes through the frame ring with a heartbeat. **Result:
route 3 passes on the crash route, failover included, at 45 fps published / 46 fps latched by the M7.**
Nobody saw the panel; every reading below is the SNVS record and the M7's own status block.

**The M7 image.** SafeUI main eb1a48e (a fresh clone in the worktree's build/safeui), Zephyr af17c0c8
(<zephyr checkouts>, plus open-amp and libmetal from the SafeUI workspace, read only), board
`verdin_imx8mp/mimx8ml8/m7/ddr`, `-DCONFIG_SAFEUI_M7_TAKEOVER_AT_BOOT=y`, the ARM toolchain from the
slint-zephyr copy of zephyr-sdk-1.0.1 (the ~/org SDK has only aarch64). Build id **0xb87c5576**, ELF sha256
b6c67b1f0bf75c35. Slint 1.18 (the slint-zephyr checkout) does not build no_std:
`internal/core/graphics/path.rs:329` calls `f32::rem_euclid`, which needs std. The image was built from a
copy of the needed crates with that one line replaced by `t % 1.` folded into [0, 1) (build/slint-m7, not
committed anywhere; an upstream Slint issue to raise).

**Board commands** (passwordless sudo on torizon@verdin-imx8mp; nothing installed or enabled):

```sh
scp build/m7/zephyr/zephyr.elf torizon@verdin-imx8mp:/home/torizon/safeui/safeui_m7_b87c5576.elf
ssh torizon@verdin-imx8mp 'sudo -n env SAFEUI_FW_FILE=safeui_m7_b87c5576.elf /home/torizon/safeui/route3_boot.sh'
#   -> READY build=0xb87c5576 scanout=0x81808000 lcdif_flags=0x00000007 rproc_was=offline   (before every run)
BOARD_HOST=torizon@verdin-imx8mp KEXEC_ZEPHYR=<loader> IMX8MP_OUT=build/imx8mp-out CRASH=1 [SEL=0x100p] \
    <the i.MX8MP kexec runner> build/a53-ring/zephyr/zephyr.bin <label>
```

`route3_boot.sh` (already on the board, identical to the clone's) ran as a one-shot. Linux's fbcon is the
running scan-out (docker-compose is disabled, so "no container 'sarta'" is only a warning). The script stops
remoteproc0, points the firmware search path at ~/safeui and starts the M7, which adopts the LCDIF. The M7
alone (no producer): render 8.2 ms, composite 38 ms over all 1 024 000 pixels (its opaque stand-in), 66-76 ms
of work, ~10 fps. Every A53 run ends in a SYSTEM_RESET that takes the M7 down, so it was started again
before each jump.

**Runs** (A53 images built from this branch; record = SNVS w0..w3):

| run | image | record | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ring abf0f879 | `594b0219 000f0d02 00000000 00000000` | FAIL code 15 (a GL error in the loop), 0 frames, attach ok |
| 2 | ring bb6961f9 (+ code 15's detail) | `594b0216 000f0d02 15050000 00000000` | GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY left by the first frame's read-back (where 1) |
| 3 | ring 4b244dc3 (+ CPU view) | `594b021b 00280d02 00000376 00060000` | FAIL code 40 = read-back, probe mask 0b10101; 886 frames published |
| 4 | ring 2fc051d6 (+ buffers off fb_app) | `594b021b 00040d01 00000375 00060000` | **PASS**, code 4 (300..999 shown), 885 frames, failover ok |
| 5 | fps b5e3ea24 | `594b021b 000b0d01 0000039f 00000000` | pass, 31 fps |
| 6 | ring 101a27cc, SEL 0x1000 | `594b0c00 03900d12 088a0002 08c0036e` | frame 33.46 ms = ui 9.12 + flip (glFinish) 22.40; GPU 21.86 |
| 7 | opaque A/B f035125d, SEL 0x1000 | `594b0c00 03b31516 ffff0002 115d017d` | the gradient back: frame 53.98, flip 44.45 (GPU busy counter saturated) |
| 8 | ring 5654de8b (pipelined) | `594b021b 00040d01 000003c4 00060000` | PASS, code 4, 964 frames |
| 9 | same, SEL 0x1007 | `594b0c07 00fa0149 0ba6025e 00f30b7a` | M7: render 3.29, composite 2.50 (24 300 px), work 6.06, flip-to-flip 29.82 ms, 29.4 fps |
| 10 | same, SEL 0x1000 | `594b0c00 03830bef 089500a5 000003c2` | frame 30.55 = ui 8.99 + swap 1.65 + ~20 ms release wait; GPU 21.97 |
| 11 | fps b2b67820 (4 buffers) | `594b021b 00190d01 000c052d 00000000` | **pass, 45 fps**, 1325 frames, no release timeouts |
| 12 | ring e8afc77c (4 buffers) | `594b021b 00050d01 000c04f6 00060000` | **PASS**, code 5 (1000..2999 shown), 1270 frames, failover ok |
| 13 | same, SEL 0x1000 | `594b0c00 03c20916 089c0492 000004f1` | frame 23.26 = GPU-bound: GPU busy 22.04, ui 9.62, swap 11.70 |
| 14 | same, SEL 0x1007 | `594b0c07 00fb0124 086a023c 00ec11f8` | M7: render 2.92, composite 2.51 (23 600 px), work 5.72, flip-to-flip 21.54 ms, 46.0 fps |

The 6 release waits that time out in every verdict run are the failover window: for 2.5 s the M7 treats us
as gone, `shown` stops, and each wait gives up after 200 ms. The fps runs (no failover) have none. Return
times ranged 169-325 s for the same kind of record (slow Linux boots); the record, not the hold, is what was
read.

**Fixes (yakogl, this branch):**

1. **The A53's "ok" verdict was 6; the M7's is 7.** SafeUI 075fb74 (2026-09-22) put `APP_FRAME_STALE` (6)
   before `APP_FRAME_OK`, and gc_slint kept `M7_VERDICT_OK 6u`: every accepted frame would have read as a
   verdict failure (code 15 of the ring space). Now 7, and "stale" (code 14) is in the string table and
   the README.
2. **`ST_LCDIF_FLIPS` read word 26** (`lcdif_wait_us`); the field is word 25 (offsets checked with offsetof
   against the M7's m7_mem.h). Diagnostic only.
3. **The ring build started the display drivers anyway.** `CONFIG_SAFEUI_DISPLAY_IMX8MP=n` left the DT
   nodes' own drivers enabled: since land129 the media power domains' init re-runs the MEDIAMIX power-on
   (MEDIA_AXI/APB clock roots, MEDIA_BLK_CTRL enables) under the LCDIF the M7 is scanning, and the bridge
   driver pulls in I2C. `prj_ring.conf` now also sets `SAFEUI_IMX8MP_MEDIA_PD`, `SAFEUI_SN65DSI8X`, `PWM`
   and `I2C` to n. (Not measured as a failure: changed on reading, before the first run.)
4. **An imported buffer had no CPU view, so glReadPixels on it failed** (run 2). Route 3's window buffers are
   outside the GPU carveout; `gc_render_map_phys` mapped them for the GPU only; the GL core fell back to
   `gpu_read`, which had nothing to read through: zeros and GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY, which the render loop's first
   glGetError then failed on. Imports now also get a Normal non-cacheable CPU mapping (the attribute the
   ring code's own mapping of the same pages has), and `gc_render_free(_retired)` refuse any block outside
   the carveout. Code 15 now carries where and which GL error in w2[31:16].
5. **Buffer 0 was `fb_app`, where the M7 paints its stand-in** (run 3). `fallback_base()` in the M7's main.c
   fills 0x81408000 with its gradient whenever it has no usable frame -- before our first publish and while
   the heartbeat is stopped -- so the first frame's read-back found two probes overwritten. With more than
   one buffer the producer now uses 0x82008000, 0x82408000, 0x82808000 (and 0x82c08000), never `fb_app`.
6. **Pipelined publish and four buffers** (performance). The loop did a glFinish before every publish, so
   CPU and GPU ran in series (33.5 ms). It now publishes the previous frame, which the pipelined swap has
   finished. With three buffers that only moved the wait (30.6 ms: every iteration waited ~20 ms for the M7
   to latch the frame just published). With four (Kconfig range now 1..4, `prj_ring.conf` 4) the loop is
   GPU-bound at 23.3 ms: 31 -> 45 fps.
7. **The background is transparent in route 3** (`cluster.slint`: `background: root.standalone ?
   @linear-gradient(...) : transparent`; the probes expect 0,0,0 there), as the user's design says the MPU's
   background is. See below for what the M7 does and does not do with that.
8. Instruments: PERF page 7 of a ring build is the M7's own tick (render, composite, work, flip to flip,
   latched fps, composite pixels), sampled from its status block at every publish; the Python record decoder
   prints it.

**Measurements against the 16.7 ms budget** (Verdin 1280x800, A53 at Linux's 1.2 GHz, GPU 800 MHz):

| | per frame |
|---|---|
| A53 GPU, transparent background | **22.0 ms** (runs 6, 10, 13): over budget by 5.3 ms |
| A53 GPU, the opaque gradient (A/B) | ~44.5 ms (run 7, the glFinish wait; the busy counter saturated) |
| A53 CPU (Slint + FemtoVG + GL recording) | 9.0-9.6 ms |
| A53 frame, 4 buffers, pipelined | 23.3 ms, GPU-bound: 45 fps published |
| M7 per tick at 45 fps | render 2.9 + composite 2.5 (23 600 px, 2.3 % of the screen); work 5.7 ms; latches 46 fps |
| M7 alone, its opaque picture | render 8.2 + composite 38 ms (all 1 024 000 px): ~10 fps |

The background was 22.5 ms of the GPU's 44.5, half of it, and dropping it is what route 3 needs. The M7's
share (5.7 ms) is well inside a frame. 60 fps now waits on the A53's GPU (22 ms for the dials, arcs, ticks
and text) and nothing else.

**What the M7 does with a transparent background, and what it does not.** The user's statement was that
the MCU draws the background, the speed and the telltales in software, partially, and that the MPU's
background is transparent. Read against the firmware, half of that holds. The M7 draws the speed, RPM,
gear, READY, fuel and telltales, partially (23 600 pixels a frame). It does **not** draw a background under
a live A53 frame: `safety.slint` is transparent while the application is alive ("transparent while the
application paints the background underneath"), and the composite blends only the safety layer's own pixels
into our buffer. The LCDIF scans XRGB8888, so the transparent pixels show as **black**, and the cluster's
premultiplied edges look as if drawn over black. The design gradient is #0B1018 -> #04060A, nearly black,
so the picture changes little. But it has changed, and nobody has looked at it. A background drawn by the
M7 under the A53's frame would be a full-screen read-blend-write every frame; the M7's own full-screen
composite costs 38 ms (above), more than two frames. Options for the user: keep black (as now); a flat
`Layout.bg-bottom` window colour on the A53 (a glClear, measured free on this GPU in "gc_slint at 60 fps");
or a gradient the M7 paints once into buffers the A53 then draws over (a design change on both sides).

**Still open.** (a) Nobody has seen the panel in route 3: the picture (black background, safety layer
placement, tearing) needs eyes. (b) 60 fps needs the A53 GPU under 16.7 ms (22.0 now). (c) The M7 still
paints its stand-in into `fb_app`, so `RING_BUFFERS=1` keeps the race; the 64 MiB carveout makes that
configuration unnecessary. (d) The new M7 image is not the boot unit's firmware (`safeui_m7_route3.elf` on
the board is the 2026-09-21 build), and `safeui-route3.service` stays disabled. (e) Slint 1.18's no_std
`rem_euclid`. Regression check of the gc_render change: the default gc_slint (drives the panel, M7 off,
image e6bf5f629ad68853) returned `594b021b 00ff0d01 001b0396 3c330f3f`, the land131 smoke's record to the
bit (PASS, 918 frames, health 0x3f). The board is left as on 2026-09-23: Linux, remoteproc0 offline, safeui-route3 and
docker-compose disabled, crash window 256 MiB; the new M7 ELF is in ~/safeui.
