## Route 3: vehicle state and background from the M7, 2026-10-03 (branch safeui/route3-vehicle)

The user decided on 2026-10-03: the vehicle values live on the MCU and the MPU reads them; the background
is a static picture the M7 renders once, which the A53 draws first. On the panel, bottom to top: the M7's
background, the A53's UI, the M7's safety elements (still blended last, partially). **Result: route 3
passes with the failover at 37 fps. The A53 draws from the M7's vehicle state over the M7's picture.**
Nobody saw the panel; every reading is the SNVS record.

**Protocol (SafeUI branch `route3/vehicle-state-and-background`, adf4b943, pushed; yakogl mirrors
`frame_ring.h` byte for byte).** `SAFEUI_FRAME_RING_VERSION` is 3. `struct safeui_m7_page` sits at ring + 0x800
(0x81005800). It is 160 bytes, all 32-bit words, and the M7 writes it. Layout: magic 'M7PG', version 1, size
160, ring_version 3, 4 reserved; then `bg` (16 words: state written last, gen, pa_lo/hi, width, height,
stride, format 0x7, bytes, render_us, checksum = word sum, 5 reserved); then `vehicle` (16 words: a
sequence-lock gen that is odd while written and +2 per publish, time_ms, speed x10, rpm, gear, fuel,
tank, odometer, trip, valid bits, lamps (indicator switch L/R and the flasher phase kept apart, low beam,
engine running, ignition), warnings, source, 3 reserved). The background is at 0x83008000, above the
A53's four buffers, and the M7 refuses a frame overlapping it. An old A53 gets the new M7 verdict 8 "old
producer", appended after ok = 7. An old M7 gets the A53's attach result 7, hold code 28; the background
failures are 29..34 and "the vehicle state never moved" is 35. The new w3 is attach | bg << 8 | vehicle
read (bit 12) | moved (bit 13) | release timeouts << 16.

**The A53 side.** At attach the A53 checks the page. It waits up to 3 s for the background, checks the
descriptor against its map, and re-counts the checksum through the NC view (passed on every run). It
copies the picture into a texture once, reordering B,G,R,X into RGBA rows with glTexSubImage2D, and draws
it as a full-screen quad from Slint's BeforeRendering notifier (new `slint_set_underlay`, installed only
when asked, so other builds are unchanged). The program is the offline table's `uv.vert` + `texture.frag`.
Run A1 failed with code 18 because a shader written in the sample does not compile on this target:
glShaderSource accepts only table GLSL. Every frame it reads the vehicle state (`ring_vehicle()`). The
first-frame background probes now expect the M7's picture at their points.

**Two M7 bugs found on the board, both fixed in the SafeUI branch.**
1. A `@linear-gradient` on a Rectangle makes the M7 take a usage fault, "division by zero", in Slint's
   `draw_linear_gradient`. The division `(255 * size_x) / start` is guarded by `start == 0`, but the
   compiler hoists the SDIV above the guard, and Zephyr turns on DIV_0_TRP. A window gradient is filled
   flat by the software renderer (checked on the host). The background is now 800 solid 1-px rows.
   Worth an upstream report.
2. **The M7 main stack (64 KiB) overflows in route 3.** The M7 stopped dead 2-15 s into every A53 run
   (hold code 26): verdict frozen at ok, no fault, magic intact. A 100 ms PC sampler on the M7, reported
   through the A53's record, showed the sampler itself stopping, with the idle thread's WFI as the last
   PC: the whole core stops. Bisection (records in build/STATE.txt): C background → hang; original
   safety.slint → hang; no `vehicle_publish()` → no hang; `vehicle_publish()` inlined but never called
   → **hang**; 128 KiB + INIT_STACKS → PASS. On the stand-in path main already used ~51 KiB of 64.
   prj.conf now has 128 KiB and INIT_STACKS.

(The very first start at 16:10, before the coordinator held the board for land132, also failed. It was a
different picture: Linux had run 25 min, and after it even the known-good b87c5576 could not start on that
boot. A clean reboot fixed it. Every run below was started on a fresh boot.)

**Runs** (M7 image **0xcfc7c618**, `~/safeui/safeui_m7_cfc7c618.elf`, ELF sha256 e4fb4e85eb58e83f; A53 images
from this branch; the M7 started by route3_boot.sh before every jump):

| run | image | record | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | M7 b87c5576 + A53 e8afc77c (10/1 run 12) | `594b021b 00050d01 000a04f2 00060000` | PASS: the board was fine today |
| R1 verdict | ring aebd47ed | `594b021b 00050d01 000f0401 00073000` | **PASS**, 1000..2999 shown, 1025 published; vehicle read + moved, bg ok, attach ok, 7 failover timeouts |
| R2 fps | fps a67a3d1c | `594b021b 00110d01 000f0435 00003000` | **37 fps**, 1077 frames, no timeouts |
| R3 PERF p0 | ring, SEL 0x1000 | `594b0c00 03b40afc 0a7c068f 00010404` | frame 28.12 ms: ui (CPU) 9.48, GPU busy 26.84 |
| R4 PERF p7 | ring, SEL 0x1007 | `594b0c07 01070174 0acb0299 00f60f24` | M7: render 3.72, composite 2.63 (24 600 px), work 6.65, flip-to-flip 27.63 ms, 38.8 fps |
| R5 default | gc_slint 038ef263, M7 offline | `594b021b 00ff0d01 001b0395 3c330f3f` | PASS, 917 frames: unchanged |

Against 10/1: the A53 GPU went from 22.0 to 26.8 ms. The full-screen copy costs ~4.8 ms (predicted 2-3), and
the rate falls from 45 to 37 fps. The M7's composite is unchanged (2.5 → 2.6 ms). Its render rose
(2.9 → 3.7 ms, within the noise of a different drive-cycle phase). The background costs the M7 23.9 ms,
once at boot.

**Open.** (a) The picture still needs eyes. (b) The copy is 4.8 ms of the A53's GPU. A zero-copy
EGL_NATIVE_PIXMAP_KHR import of the M7's buffer exists in the GL but is exercised only on the PowerVR, and
it would save the 4 MB upload, not the per-frame sampling. Drawing the A53's opaque parts first and the
picture only where nothing is drawn is the real saving. (c) Telltale semantics: the lamps word carries
the indicator switch and the flasher phase separately; low beam = engine running, as the safety layer
already assumes; `lights` and `engine_warn` have no real source in the model. (d) Real vehicle data: no
bus is invented. The hook is `plat_set_inputs()` (or feeding the snapshot's sensors) in place of
`demo_inputs()`, and `source` says which. (e) The Slint DIV_0_TRP hoisting is worth an upstream issue.
(f) The boot unit's firmware on the board is still the 2026-09-21 build, and `safeui-route3.service`
stays disabled. The board is left on Linux with remoteproc0 offline. `~/safeui` holds b87c5576,
cfc7c618 and the old route3 ELF. The bisection ELFs were removed.

## AM62P display in Rust on the board (2026-10-02, branch am62p/display-rust-board)

The Rust DSS1 / Cadence DSI / D-PHY drivers of form/5-am62p-display (9d9b849e, group E steps 6 and 7)
run on the Verdin AM62P (Zephyr af17c0c8, kexec from Torizon 6.6.138, the AM62P kexec runner on
usb-serial-1:35933). Details, the dump's resolution and the open questions: driver/docs/am62p-display-cold.md,
"On the board".

- **Dump.** driver/docs/am62p-display-dump-linux.txt: 265 registers of DSS1 (common, VIDL1, VID, OVR1/2,
  VP1/2), the DSI wrapper and controller and the D-PHY, read through /dev/mem while Linux drove the
  panel (STRICT_DEVMEM, not IO_STRICT: nothing blocked), plus the SN65DSI83 by i2cdump (IRQ_STAT 0).
- **WIZ.** MOD_VER 69924881h (MODULE_ID 992h) at +F00h; +0h..+14h read 0. TI's driver is right, the
  SPRUJ83D summary (14.8.6.3.2) is not.
- **Golden.** 27 first differences: 10 were model gaps (TRM reset values, IRQENABLE_CLR reads the
  enables, status read through the model), 16 became allow-list lines (live status, the WIZ revision
  field, our VSYNC interrupt, safety-layer format and layer placement, no gamma table, CBA_CFG not
  written, an undocumented PHY register) and one (PSM_FREQ) the test's PSM clock, 16 MHz on the board
  as Linux's clk_summary shows. No driver change. Linux agrees
  with the C drivers on every TRM difference (VSIZE1 11/22/12, WAIT_BURST_TIME 0, FIFO low size/2, MFLAG
  2/3, 1/3): those stay allow-listed and the board decided them.

| image (same tree) | result | as predicted |
|---|---|---|

## Route 3 toward 60 fps (branch safeui/route3-60fps, 2026-10-02)

Goal (user): the Slint cluster on the A53 at 60 fps in route 3 on the Verdin i.MX8MP (1280x800). Starting point
(section above): A53 frame 28.1 ms, GPU 26.8 ms, 37 fps. **Result: the A53 frame is no longer the limit. GPU
24.7 -> 10.5 ms, CPU (ui) 30.4 -> 8.4-11.1 ms, 37 -> 58 fps published, and the M7 latches a frame at every
vblank (58.76 fps). The panel itself refreshes at 58.76 Hz, so 60 fps needs a faster pixel clock, not a faster
frame** (below). Nobody saw the panel; every reading is the SNVS record. A human look is owed.

**Trees.** The no_std Slint and femtovg trees were rebuilt from the patches in this repository (upstream Slint
1007c03 + slint-nostd.patch; crates.io femtovg 0.26.0 / glow 0.18.0 + their patches). The earlier route-3 images
were built from a copy (`imx8mp-board/build/nostd-old`) that predates the 2026-09-26 patches (gradient pool,
one-pass strokes, text spares). So the baseline was measured again: M7 image 0xcfc7c618 (unchanged), A53 ring
image 27e326697651fce3, PERF p0 frame 32.25, ui 30.36, GPU 24.73 ms (`594b0c00 0bdc0c99 09a90002 0001037e`).

**Host draw list.** A host harness (build/hostfvg in the worktree, not in the repository) links gl_slint's own
staticlib for the host against Mesa (surfaceless EGL, llvmpipe), wraps the GL calls and prints every draw: its
FemtoVG program (matched against tools/shaders/femtovg), primitive, covered area and the scissor uniforms. The
route-3 frame: 214 draws + the underlay. fill_color 114 draws, 398 000 px (the two dial faces 154 000 each);
fill_image (text) 96 draws, 458 000 px; conic gradients 4 draws, 13 000 px. **No draw has a scissor.** Text is
drawn as one texture per Text item the size of the item's box (`bitmapfont.rs`): the six SAFEUI letters are
500x35 quads, 17 000 px each. The pictures compared below are this harness's read-backs.

| step | image | PERF p0 (frame / ui / GPU ms) | fps | what changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B0 | 27e32669 | 32.25 / 30.36 / 24.73 | -- | the patches as on origin/main |
| L0 | 85103b69 | 26.19 / 8.79 / 24.92 | -- | gradient pool cools (lever 0, below) |
| L2 | 7770de94 | 20.53 / 8.63 / 19.44 | -- | + NO_SCISSOR fills (lever 2) |
| L3 | a879ccaf | 18.08 / 8.41 / 14.21 | -- | + text cut to its ink (lever 3) |
| L4 | 371ff1ff | 18.12 / 8.62 / 14.56 | 57 (52cfc7fc) | + background around the faces (lever 1) |
| L5 | 87ebbff7 | 18.18 / 8.57 / 13.44 | -- | + no window clear, stencil cleared every frame |
| L6 | 7959e3bd | 18.19 / 8.37 / 10.30 | 57 (f93949f0) | + stencil cleared in the first 8 frames only |
| L8 | a82631eb | 18.10 / 11.07 / 10.47 | **58** (91db4f16) | + early publish, background flushed ahead |

**Lever 0 (not in the list, found first): texture uploads waited for the GPU.** B0 page 1/2: 21.8 ms a frame in
gc_render_wait, 1.7 waits and 22.1 ms of upload time a frame. The harness, tracking each upload against the frame
that last drew the texture: the four conic-gradient tables of the dial bands were refilled from femtovg's table
pool while the previous frame -- still on the GPU in the pipelined swap -- drew them, so the GL core flushed and
waited. The pool releases at every flush, and Slint flushes twice a frame when a BeforeRendering notifier is
installed (it flushes the clear before calling it): route 3's underlay. A pooled table is now refilled only after
two releases (`POOL_COOL`, femtovg patch). ui 30.36 -> 8.79 ms (prediction ~9).

**Lever 2: NO_SCISSOR programs.** femtovg (patch) builds, for FillGradient/Image/ImageGradient/Color and the two
conic types, a no-discard program whose scissor mask is the constant 1.0 and uses it when the draw's scissor
matrix is zero and extent and scale are 1 (what Params writes for no scissor). The variant's text is main-fs.glsl
with the one line replaced, so every existing program's text, and every offline table's key for it, is unchanged;
a GL that cannot compile a variant keeps the old program (the AM62P's PowerVR table has no rows for them yet, so
the AM62P runs as before). GC7000 instructions (etna_shc): fill_color 31 -> 7, fill_image 44 -> 20, conic 77 ->
53, fill_gradient 56 -> 32. The six rows are appended to src/shaderc/vivante_blobs.rs by the new
`gen_shader_table.py --append`, which keeps the 324 existing rows byte for byte (this host's etna_shc,
e224bebc..., reproduces none of them, so a regeneration would be a new reference). GPU 24.92 -> 19.44 ms
(predicted 14-16: the per-instruction model overestimates; the fill floor is larger than it assumed).

**Lever 3: overdraw.** The text quads were 458 000 of the 856 000 pixels the UI drew (no FBO layers, no box
shadows, no stencil: the rest is the faces). compose_text now cuts the composed texture to its ink plus one
transparent pixel, rounded out to 16x4 so a changing text keeps its texture size, and the item renderer draws it
at its offset (`ItemGraphicsCacheEntry::Text`, Slint patch). Text pixels 458 000 -> 86 000, upload bytes 389 KB ->
73 KB a frame; the host picture is identical to the uncut one (0 bytes differ). GPU 19.44 -> 14.21 ms (predicted
10-12).

**Lever 1: the background only where the UI leaves it visible.** bg_build_mesh (gc_slint) draws the M7's picture
as a triangle list that leaves out a 32-slab polygon inscribed 2 px inside each dial face (opaque Theme.face, 2 x
154 000 px). 14.21 -> 14.56 ms: **no measurable gain**. The experiments said why the background costs what it
does: with the first draw (the background, and the clear fused into it) clipped to 8x8 the GPU is 4.82 ms
(`594b0c40`); with only the clears clipped, 10.32 (`594b0c80`). **The clear was 4.2 ms, not the picture.** Slint
clears the window (colour + stencil) before the notifier; in route 3 every pixel is then covered opaquely by the
picture or a face, so `slint_set_underlay_covers()` (gl_slint) makes the renderer skip it (Slint patch,
`set_skip_window_clear`), and the underlay clears the stencil itself. Clearing the stencil every frame still costs
3.1 ms (L5 13.44 vs L5n 10.33, image 576a92ec); FemtoVG leaves the stencil zero after every fill and stroke, so it
is cleared in the first 8 frames only (`GC_SLINT_RING_CLEAR_STENCIL=n`, the default). Sampling the picture from a
4x4-tiled copy (debug `gc_debug_fs_tiled`, textures of 256x256 and more) saves 0.5 ms (9.77, image 69138937): the
picture's ~5 ms is the fill of the linear target, not the texture layout. (With every 2D texture tiled, the text
copies ran the GPU heap out: code 15, GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY, image 83ed97e8.) The face mesh stays: it is what makes
"covers every pixel" true without a clear under the faces.

**What paced the frame after that.** L4: the M7 flips every 17.93 ms (p7 `594b0c07 01040147 07010262 00e316f4`:
render 3.27, composite 2.60, work 6.10 ms, 58.76 fps latched); 45 % of our frames waited for the M7 to release a
buffer (`GC_SLINT_RING_REPORT_WAITS`, `594b021b 00090d01`); frame-time p50 17 / p90 18 ms. Two changes put each
frame in the M7's hands earlier: the loop publishes the previous frame as soon as its fence has signalled after
acquiring the next buffer (glFenceSync after the swap, glClientWaitSync with timeout 0), instead of after the next
frame is recorded; and the underlay flushes the background to the GPU before Slint records the items, so the
frame completes ~5 ms sooner. Page 6 of a ring build now carries the share of early publishes and the release
wait: L8 `594b0c06 0a7a0000 06410164 03a903d0` = 976 of 1000 frames published early, 9.37 ms a frame waiting
for the M7. 57 -> 58 fps. The M7 still latches 58.76 fps, flip to flip 17.86 ms (`594b0c07 0103014c 06fa0262
00e416f4`), the same to the hundredth as before: a rate that does not move with the producer is the panel's.

**The panel refreshes at 58.76 Hz.** Linux's clk_summary: video_pll1 1039.5 MHz, media_disp1_pix 69.3 MHz
(/15). The panel (`panel-rvt101hvdwc00b` in the running DT): htotal 1280+36+24+64 = 1404, vtotal 800+8+8+24 =
840, 69.3 MHz / 1 179 360 = 58.76 Hz. The DT's typical pixel clock is 71.1 MHz (60.3 Hz; its range is 66.3-78.9
MHz). The M7 adopts Linux's LCDIF timing at the takeover, so 60 fps needs the pixel clock at 70.8 MHz or more
(e.g. a video PLL that divides to 71.1 MHz) -- a change to the Linux DT or to the M7's takeover, the user's call.
The A53 has the margin for it: GPU 10.5 ms and ui 8.4-11.1 ms against 16.7.

**ui varies between runs** (8.4 ms in L3-L6, 10.9-11.1 in L5n and L8): the A53 runs at whatever clock Linux's
governor left (lever 4). Not needed for the frame rate now; setting the A53 PLL from Zephyr would remove the
variance.

**Lever 5 (tiled colour/depth surfaces, tile status, fast clear) was not needed for the A53 and was not done.**
What is left of the GPU's 10.5 ms is ~5 ms of picture fill (linear target) and ~5 ms of UI; a supertiled render
target with tile status would make clears free and cut the linear PE's write cost. What it would take: a
supertiled colour surface for the window (the PE already supports it for MSAA, backend.rs), a resolve (RS/BLT)
into the linear buffer the M7 reads at every swap (~4 MB a frame, which costs bandwidth back), tile-status buffers
and their fast-clear values, and the same for D24S8. Several days with board measurements; it pays only if the
GPU budget is needed again (a larger panel, the Armadillo-X2 at 1920x1200).

**Regression.** Final image a82631eb (L8, the branch tip's code): verdict `594b021b 00050d01 0000064a 00063000` =
PASS, code 5 (1000..2999 shown), 1610 frames, failover seen, vehicle read and moved, background ok; the first
frame's read-back and reference grid pass. fps image 91db4f16: 58 fps, no release timeouts. Default standalone
gc_slint (M7 offline) 9c7d402d: `594b021b 00ff0d01 00070680 33220e3f` = PASS, health 0x3f, **1664 frames (was
918)**: the standalone build gets the same femtovg/Slint changes; its median swap wait is 7 ms. The host harness
reads back the route-3 frame identical to the B0 trees' with all changes on.

**Other GPUs.** The femtovg/Slint patches are shared with the AM62P (gl_slint, PowerVR offline table) and the Pi
4 (v3d_gl_slint, online compiler); neither was run here. The AM62P has no table rows for the NO_SCISSOR texts, so
it falls back to the existing programs; the text cut and the pool change apply to both. gl_slint/rust's
`slint_set_underlay_covers` needs the regenerated Slint tree: a tree older than this patch does not build it.

**Open.** (a) The picture needs eyes. (b) 60 fps needs the pixel clock (above). (c) PowerVR table rows for the
six NO_SCISSOR texts (glsl2usc, pco_shc build-new) to give the AM62P the same gain. (d) Board runs of gl_slint on
the AM62P and v3d_gl_slint on the Pi 4 with the new patches. (e) The A53 clock from Zephyr (lever 4) for a
deterministic ui time.

## Verdin panel at 60 Hz (branch safeui/route3-60hz + SafeUI route3/pixel-clock-60hz, 2026-10-02)

The user's decision (2026-10-04, 「いいよ」): raise the Verdin i.MX8MP panel's pixel clock so it refreshes at
60 Hz or more. Linux programs 69.3 MHz (VIDEO_PLL1 1039.5 MHz / 15) and everything before this kept it:
1404 x 840 pixels a frame, 58.76 Hz, and route 3 could not show more than 58 fps.

**The clock: 71.1 MHz, the panel's typical, 60.286 Hz.** The highest pixel clock that satisfies all three limits:

| limit | arithmetic | 71.1 MHz |
|---|---|---|
| the panel | `panel-timing` clock-frequency 66.3 / 71.1 / 78.9 MHz (board's Linux devicetree, /proc/device-tree/panel-rvt101hvdwc00b) | typical |
| the DSI link | pixel x 24 / 4 lanes <= 426.6 Mbit/s (DSIM PLL 12 MHz x 711 / (5 x 4)) -> pixel <= 71.1 MHz | exactly at the cap; 71.1 MHz + 1 Hz and 71.43 MHz are refused by `ip::samsung_dsim::plan` |
| the bridge | DSI clock 213.3 MHz -> `CHA_DSI_CLK_RANGE` 42; divider 213.3 / 71.1 = 3; LVDS 71.1 MHz, range 2 | the same CSRs as at 69.3 MHz (integer divider 3 there too) |
| VIDEO_PLL1 | p 2, s 1: m + k/65536 = 1066.5 x 4 / 24 = 177.75 -> m 178, k -16384 (VCO 2133 MHz; Linux's 1039.5: 2079) | 1066.5 MHz / 15, exact |

At 71.1 MHz the DSIM's blanking word counts are HFP 21, HBP 42, HSA 12: exactly the board's Linux's (golden
MHPORCH 0x0015002a). Linux sets its DSIM up for the 71.1 MHz mode and its CCM then gives the LCDIF 69.3 MHz;
the cold path's old HBP 43 was that mismatch. Nothing on the DSI side changes.

**Where it is set.**
- **The A53 cold path** (yakogl): `gc_common/verdin_imx8mp_display.dtsi`, display0 `clock-frequency = <71100000>`,
  `video-pll1-frequency = <1066500000>`, and the DSIM node's `pixel-clock-frequency`. The C display facade and
  the Rust LCDIF/DSIM both take the plan from there. Host tests `soc::imx8mp::dsi_chain_tests::verdin_60hz`
  (6 tests) read the dtsi and check the three limits, the bridge CSRs, the PLL dividers, the pixel root's choice
  of VIDEO_PLL1 / 15, and a cold bring-up in the register model against the golden Linux image with MHPORCH off
  the allow-list. `media::tests::bring_up_at` takes the wanted clock.
- **The M7 at takeover** (SafeUI `platform/fw_imx8mp/src/pixclk_m7.c`, `CONFIG_SAFEUI_M7_PIXEL_CLOCK_HZ` default
  71100000, 0 = keep): at the first adoption, right after its first flip latched (start of vertical blanking), the
  M7 moves `MEDIA_DISP1_PIX` to the 24 MHz oscillator, re-programs VIDEO_PLL1 with the Rust cold path's sequence
  (reset low, dividers, 3 us, release, PLL_LOCK, gate) so the root's unchanged /15 gives 71.1 MHz, moves the root
  back, and writes 0 to the LCDIF's write-1-to-clear `INT_STATUS_D1` (below). The LCDIF timing, the DSIM, its PLL
  and the bridge are untouched. Status block v11: `pixclk_rc`, `pixclk_before_hz`, `pixclk_hz`, `pixclk_lock_us`,
  `pixclk_step`. A chain the A53 cold path lit is found at 71.1 MHz and left alone (`PIXCLK_ALREADY`).
- **The adopt path** inherits the previous owner's clock: Linux's 69.3 MHz in the kexec dev loop, 58.76 Hz,
  until Linux's devicetree changes (not ours).

**The M7 hang, and the one write that stopped it.** The first M7 image re-tuned correctly (69.3 -> 71.1 MHz,
relock about 500 us) but then stopped for good on most starts: heartbeat 1, uptime frozen at about 110 ms, the
whole core stopped (its 100 ms sampler too), the LCDIF scanning on unharmed (Linux saw VSYNC and DMA_DONE
keep coming, no UNDERRUN). Step markers written with a DSB placed the stop after the re-tune had returned: in
the first cacheable DDR read after it (printk, or a deliberate read of a cold line), once inside the re-tune.
One reboot and one M7 start per trial:

| variant | starts | M7 stopped |
|---|---|---|
| re-tune off (`PIXEL_CLOCK_HZ=0`) | 1 | 0 |
| root to 24 MHz and back, PLL untouched | 1 | 0 |
| PLL reset and relocked at the dividers found (1039.5 MHz) | 1 | 0 |
| k nudged without a reset (69.32 MHz) | 1 | 0 |
| to 1066.5 MHz and straight back | 1 | 0 |
| **ending at 71.1 MHz, no LCDIF access after** (both sequences, panic on or off) | 12 | **10** |
| ending at 71.1 MHz, then one LCDIF register write (PANIC0_THRES = 0, or 0 to INT_STATUS_D1) | 9 | 0 |
| the shipped image accf0897 (write of 0 to INT_STATUS_D1) | 3 + 5 route-3 starts | 0 |

So it takes the new rate AND no access to the LCDIF straight after; the LCDIF's panic is not it (off before
the re-tune: 3 of 3 stopped). Why an LCDIF write prevents a stall of the M7's DDR reads is not known, and
nothing in IMX8MPRM covers it. The first route-3 run with the first image failed with code 8 (the M7's
last verdict "no ring", 139 release waits timed out): an M7 that had survived its start and stopped later,
which the write may or may not also cover -- 3 route-3 runs and 2 PERF runs with accf0897 since saw no stop.

**Board results** (Verdin i.MX8MP, crash route; predictions in build/STATE.txt first):

| run | record | result | predicted |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) gc_slint FORCE_COLD (cold path at the new plan) | `594b021b 00ff0d01 00070677 2b210f3f` | PASS, 1655 frames, health 0x3f, frame median 33 ms (2 vblanks of 16.59); the same record again from the tip image | PASS 0x3f |
| (a) same, PERF page 7 (new: 60 vblanks timed after the run) | `594b0c07 0001004a 0676061b 40cb178c` | **60.28 Hz, 16 587 us** | 60.29 Hz |
| (c) gc_slint adopt (Linux's chain) | `594b021b 00ff0d01 0007067f 44220e3f` | PASS, 1663 frames, median 34 ms | unchanged (1664) |
| (c) same, PERF page 7 | `594b0c07 0001004a 06800619 427a16f4` | 58.76 Hz, 17 018 us | 58.76 |
| Linux, LCDIF1 VSYNC counted from /dev/mem for 3 s | -- | 58.756 Hz; after the M7 (accf0897) started: **60.284 Hz** | 60.286 |
| (b) route 3, verdict (M7 accf0897) | `594b021b 00050d01 00000671 00063000` | PASS code 5, 1649 frames, failover clear | PASS code 5 |
| (b) route 3, fps | `594b021b 00270d01 000006be 00003000` | **59 fps** (code 39), 1726 frames (was 58, 1687) | >= 60 -- **missed** |
| (b) route 3, PERF page 7 | `594b0c07 01000104 06c60216 00dc16c6` | M7 render 2.60, composite 2.56, work 5.34, flip to flip 17.34 ms, latched 58.30 fps | ~60.3 latched -- missed |
| (b) route 3, PERF page 0 | -- | A53 frame 17.49, ui 8.52, GPU busy 10.40 ms, 1652 frames | -- |

The panel now runs at 60.28 Hz in every path that ends with our code owning it. Route 3 does not reach 60:
the limit has moved to the A53, whose frame averages 17.49 ms against a 16.59 ms vblank (at 58.76 Hz it had
17.0 ms and fit; the M7 latches what the A53 publishes, 58-59 a second, its own work is 5.3 ms).

The ring images are b35c961e + origin/main 131423bf with the devicetree change (the ring build links no display
code, so the dtsi does not reach them); the standalone images are the branch tip's.

**Open.** (a) **The picture needs a human look** at 71.1 MHz: cold path and route 3 (a DSI link at exactly its
capacity is what the 2026-09-23 break-up looked like, though that one ran 71.43 MHz on a 428 MHz link). (b) The
M7 stall: the mechanism is unknown; the write is an empirical fix measured on 9 + 8 starts. Whether the A53 cold
path can trip the same stall when it re-programs VIDEO_PLL1 with the M7 already running (the direct-boot order)
is untested. (c) Route 3 at 60 fps needs about 1 ms off the A53's frame. (d) Linux's devicetree still asks for
69.3 MHz, so adopt runs stay at 58.76 Hz.

  C arm, so the reading stands.
- Of the doc's "What only the board can confirm" list, these runs exercised
  the whole bring-up (power, handshake wait, identify with MINOR_FEATURE_1..5,
  reset, init, MMU, ring, events, the ISR under the spinlock, the `dmb sy`
  ordering) through three applications, with the C's records reproduced
  exactly. The staged smaller steps (gc_identify, gc_fence, gc_clear,
  gc_triangle) and the dEQP groups were not run; the Armadillo-X2 adopt run
  and the default-flip are the owner's next calls.

Read: a predicated-off group costs time, 0.11 to 0.29 ms a frame, 14 to 36 %

arms as pco does (`afa12e9b`) loses to a branch once the never-run arm is
large enough; where the crossover lies needs the cost of a branch, not yet
measured.

    gl_test: ifbranch 1 predicate: off arm +8 groups: best 56 ms; per frame 3D busy 55420 us, TA busy 225 us
    gl_test: ifbranch 1 branch: off arm +8 groups: best 56 ms; per frame 3D busy 55338 us, TA busy 225 us
    gl_test: ifbranch 2 predicate: off arm +32 groups: best 60 ms; per frame 3D busy 59331 us, TA busy 225 us

Arithmetic, 3D busy per frame:
- the branched form is 55337 / 55338 / 55338 / 55338 us at N = 0 / 8 / 32 / 128:
  the same at every N, 55.34 ms; the never-run arm is skipped;
- at N = 0 it costs 55337 - 54562 = 775 us (+0.78 ms) more than the predicated
  form: the six control groups and the branch, less the 31 base groups of the
  arm it no longer issues;
- the predicated form grows by 0.107 ms per group at small N (case 194), so the
  branch wins from N = 0.78 / 0.107 = 7.2, N = 7 on, that is once the never-run
  arm exceeds about 38 groups (31 + 7);
- at N = 128 the branch saves 91144 - 55338 = 35806 us (35.8 ms).

Read: `fill_color`'s own scissor arm (31 groups) is right to stay predicated,
the default. Not measured: the branched form's cost when the arm is taken
(radius > 0), which the compiler needs to choose by arm size; gl_test 195 is
being extended for it.

  (+2.80 ms); N = 32: 88325 - 86005 = 2320 us (+2.32 ms); N = 128:
  162452 - 163104 = -652 us (0.65 ms less: the predicated form then pays the
  23-group else arm masked at the large-arm rate);
- an executed group: (66907 - 59046) / 8 = 0.98 ms per added group, consistent
  with cases 184 and 185;
- the branch's fixed cost, the six control groups plus the taken branch: radius
  0, 0.78 ms net plus the 31 masked groups it no longer issues (31 x 0.107 =
  3.3 ms); radius 4, 2.88 ms net plus the 23 masked groups (23 x 0.107 = 2.5
  ms); about 4 to 5 ms a frame either way, about six executed groups.

Read: branching saves the masked cost of the arm it skips (case 194's curve,
0.107 to 0.38 ms a group). Which arm is skipped is unknown at compile time, so
the rule that never loses is: branch when both arms' masked cost exceeds the
fixed cost. For `fill_color` (31 and 23 groups, about 3.3 and 2.5 ms)
predicating, the default, is right; for a symmetric `if` the crossover is about
38 groups an arm. Left: the rule in the compiler and its board proof.

## Correction (2026-10-06): an executed group costs 0.79 ms, not 0.98

The 2026-10-06 entry "gl_test 195 ifbranch with the arm taken" divides
(66907 - 59046) by 8 and reads 0.98 ms per executed group. Going from N = 0 to
N = 8 adds 10 groups to the then arm (the 8 fmad and two uniform copies), so the
figure is (66907 - 59046) / 10 = 786 us, about 0.79 ms; cases 184 and 185
measured about 0.8. The branch's fixed cost is then about 6.8 executed groups
(5336 / 786), 5.2 with the arm off (4092 / 786), not "about six". Only this
division changes; the measurements above stand. Source: the message of
`5f4d3677`, which also sets the default rule: branch an `if` iff the masked
cost of each arm exceeds `BRANCH_FIXED_US` = 5336 us (arm taken 2875 + 23 x 107;
arm off 775 + 31 x 107 = 4092, the larger taken), crossed at 49 groups an arm;
on the corpus 0 of 168 `if`s branch. The off arm of case 193 grows by N + 2
(N fmad and two copies), as ours does, not by the N fmad alone. Board run of
the rule: pending.

## i.MX8MP: the panel showed one and a half copies of the frame per line (issue #23, 2026-10-06)

Symptom: the user saw one and a half copies of the frame per line on the
i.MX8MP panel (Toradex Capacitive Touch Display 10.1" DSI = Riverdi
RVT101HVDWC00-B via the SN65DSI84, the devicetree's panel; Linux on the board
uses the overlay `verdin-imx8mp_panel-cap-touch-10inch-dsi`). The rendered bytes
are correct: the PICTURE crc32 is identical (0xe7284c58 above), and gl_test's
"last frame" is the CPU-drawn panel console, so the display chain is at fault,
not the GPU. A read-only comparison with the board's Linux showed every
LCDIF / DSIM / SN65DSI84 register equal except the pixel clock: our dtsi asked
71.1 MHz (the 2026-10-02 "60 Hz" change above), which puts the DSI lane rate at
exactly pixel x 24 / 4 with no packet-overhead margin, the same condition that
broke the picture on 2026-09-23; Linux runs 69.3 MHz (2.6 % headroom). The fix,
commit `e372545f`: the dtsi back to 69.3 MHz, a 25 per mille margin rule in
`ip::samsung_dsim::plan` with the dtsi host test and a `BUILD_ASSERT`, and an
opt-in DISPLAY record kind 22. It is in the gate; the proof is the panel viewed
after it lands. The host gate cannot see scanout: only eyes or a camera can.

## i.MX8MP: gl_test case 44 on `f2a13877` still fails (2026-10-11)

`tools/board.sh imx8mp`, `BOARD_BOOT=uboot-mmc`, `gc_gl_test` with `CONFIG_GL_TEST_CASES="44"`
built from origin/main `f2a13877`. Record
`records/imx8mp/gc44-f2a13877/20261011-0032-gc44-f2a13877-81722382` (SNVS record, no
console): verdict `failed`, `CASE` record `594b010e 002c0302 40042814 40043904`: **case 44
(`es3hdr`) check 3 status 2, got `0x40042814` want `0x40043904`.**

`466e1b00`'s two fixes (the `PE_COLOR_FORMAT` write mask, RGBA16F textures sampled from a
4x4-tiled copy) did not move it. `0x40042814` is texel (5,0)'s colour; `0x40043904` is (7,0)'s,
the value the linear sampler reads back. The same wrong texel reads through both sampling
paths, so it is not the sampler: the pixel engine (or the rasteriser) stores (5,0)'s colour at
(7,0) of an 8-wide linear RGBA16F target. The ranked hypotheses and the fix each calls for are
in `src/vivante/VIVANTE_NOTES.md`, "RGBA16F targets"; a layout probe (case 44's check 3,
`hdr_layout_probe`) is built but has not run on a board.
